people.summary:
Alice Weidel's harm profile is rated "major" (final score 0.67; coverage and confidence 1.0). The largest factor is energy and climate statements (severity 3). In a ZDF debate she said wind power costs more than coal and German energy prices are the world's highest; DeSmog reports both claims were false and were not corrected on air [R1-E03: https://www.desmog.com/2025/02/21/anti-climate-attacks-heat-up-before-critical-german-elections]. The same source reports her "We will tear down all wind turbines" remark [R1-E04]. She also called the 2023 heating law a "Verarmungs- und Enteignungsgesetz" [R1-E10: https://www.bundestag.de/dokumente/textarchiv/2023/kw27-de-urteil-bverfg-957176].

The second factor is severity 1, involving litigation and press access. She sued a journalist over reported health claims [R2-E02: https://www.politico.eu/article/alice-weidel-sues-journalist-german-election]. A court ordered her party to admit excluded journalists in Thuringia, but the record does not show she personally ordered the exclusion [R2-E03: https://www.yahoo.com/news/court-rules-germanys-afd-must-164235573.html].

Severity 0 items are lower weight. A reported cash-paid cleaner arrangement was denied by her lawyer [R3-E03: https://www.dw.com/en/far-right-afd-leader-alice-weidel-employed-syrian-refugee-as-cleaner/a-40495560]. A donation investigation was closed without charges, and the illegal-donation fine was imposed on the party, not Weidel personally [R4-E02: https://www.zeit.de/politik/deutschland/2023-03/alice-weidel-parteispendenaffaere-urteil-berufung].

Benefit: none documented (benefit confidence 0.5). This is not a negative finding and does not offset the harm profile.

evidence.claim: Expressed doubt that human influence on global warming is decisive (2019), citing Henrik Svensmark's view that CO2's influence is overestimated.
evidence.quote: in 2019, Weidel expressed that she did not believe "that human influence on global warming is decisive."
evidence.source_title: Alice Weidel - Wikipedia

evidence.claim: Called the government's plan to convert home heating to renewables a 'heating massacre' and said it would 'impoverish' the people; the AfD's climate position is that human-caused climate change is 'not scientifically proven' per DeSmog.
evidence.quote: The plans to convert home heating systems to renewable energy are, for Weidel, no less than a "heating massacre."
evidence.source_title: Germany's far-right AfD profits from climate change spat

evidence.claim: Told a ZDF election debate (Feb 2025) that wind energy was more expensive than coal and Germany's energy prices were the highest in the world; DeSmog reports both statements were false and not debunked on air.
evidence.quote: During an official election debate on ZDF, AfD chancellor candidate Alice Weidel told over five million viewers that wind energy was more expensive than coal and that Germany's energy prices were the highest in the world.Both statements are false, and were not debunked in the course of the programme.
evidence.source_title: Anti-Climate Attacks Heat Up Before Critical German Elections

evidence.claim: Said 'We will tear down all wind turbines' at AfD national party conference in Saxony (early 2025).
evidence.quote: “We will tear down all wind turbines,” she said. “Down with these windmills of shame.”
evidence.source_title: Anti-Climate Attacks Heat Up Before Critical German Elections

evidence.claim: Called for Germany to end its boycott of Russian oil and gas and restore cheap Russian energy supplies; said industry depends on it.
evidence.quote: Germany needs "a sustainable, reliable and cheap energy resource that has been guaranteed by Russia for the last four decades," she added, claiming that sanctions on Russia have "destroyed" Germany's "business model."
evidence.source_title: AfD's Alice Weidel urges quick Ukraine talks and a return to cheap Russian energy

evidence.claim: Reported to be preparing talks with Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev on resuming Russian gas supplies (Reuters-sourced report; planned, not confirmed as executed).
evidence.quote: Leaders of Germany’s far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party are preparing to meet with Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev next year to discuss resuming Russian natural gas supplies to Germany, Reuters reported.
evidence.source_title: AfD Leaders Plan Talks With Putin Envoy on Russian Gas

evidence.claim: Opposed German military support for Ukraine, saying 'We do not want Taurus missiles to be delivered to Ukraine because by doing so Germany would become a party to the conflict'; called continued financing of 'an already lost war' wrong.
evidence.quote: "We do not want Taurus missiles to be delivered to Ukraine because by doing so Germany would become a party to the conflict," Alice Weidel said.
evidence.source_title: Germany's AfD candidate for chancellor calls for ending ...

evidence.claim: Called for halting German financial and military aid to Ukraine, saying it is wrong to continue financing 'an already lost war'.
evidence.quote: "I think it is wrong to continue with the prolongation of financing of an already lost war.
evidence.source_title: AfD leader threatens to pull German funding for Ukraine and repeats Putin talking points in worrying interview

evidence.claim: Opposed the EU AI Act's regulatory approach; AfD motion warned of overregulation of AI in Germany and the EU (Bundestag debate, 2023).
evidence.quote: Die AfD warnt in ihrem Antrag unter anderem vor einer Überregulierung von KI in Deutschland und der EU.
evidence.source_title: Abgesetzt: Debatte über die Europäische KI-Verordnung

evidence.claim: Called the 2023 Heating law (Gebäudeenergiegesetz) a 'Verarmungs- und Enteignungsgesetz' and welcomed the Constitutional Court's ruling on it; AfD's parliamentary group opposed climate-protection measures.
evidence.quote: Alice Weidel (AfD) nannte das Heizungsgesetz ein „Verarmungs- und Enteignungsgesetz“.
evidence.source_title: Deutscher Bundestag - Kontroverse nach Beschluss des Bundesverfassungsgerichts

evidence.claim: Weidel sued the producers of the satire show 'Extra 3' seeking an injunction against the 'Nazi slut' remark; the Hamburg court rejected the request, holding that public figures must 'put up with exaggerated criticism'. This is a use of litigation by a critic-target, not retaliation by Weidel against a critic; recorded as the lawsuit against a media/satire critic.
evidence.quote: A German court on Wednesday rejected a request by a senior figure in the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) not to rerun a satirical TV program in which she was called a 'Nazi slut' by the presenter
evidence.source_title: Politico Europe: German AfD leader loses case against TV show that called her 'Nazi slut'

evidence.claim: Weidel's lawsuit against a journalist: the AfD said the journalist (unnamed) had alleged in research conversations that Weidel had health problems; Weidel filed suit against the journalist.
evidence.quote: The AfD said the journalist, whom it did not name, had alleged in "research conversations" that Weidel had health problems.
evidence.source_title: Politico: German far-right leader Weidel files lawsuit against journalist

evidence.claim: Weidel's party excluded several journalists from its Thuringia election-night party; the Erfurt Regional Court ordered the AfD to admit them, finding press freedom was threatened. The snippet does not establish Weidel personally ordered the exclusion; it concerned the party's accreditation process.
evidence.quote: The Regional Court of Erfurt ruled in favour of the media companies that saw press freedom threatened, a decision made one day before the election for the regional parliament in Thuringia on Sunday.
evidence.source_title: Court rules Germany's AfD must allow journalists at election party (Yahoo/DPA)

evidence.claim: Weidel filed a lawsuit against the AfD's 'extremist' classification by domestic intelligence (challenging the state's classification); she characterised the classification as abuse of state power. Recorded as a challenge to an oversight/security body's designation, not as an act against the body.
evidence.quote: "With our lawsuit, we are sending a clear signal against the abuse of state power to combat and exclude the opposition," party co-leaders Tino Chrupalla and Alice Weidel said on Monday
evidence.source_title: Al Jazeera: AfD sues over 'extremist' classification

evidence.claim: Prosecutors in Konstanz opened a formal investigation of Weidel for alleged campaign-finance violations (donations from a Swiss company in 18 tranches, more than EUR 132,000); the AfD executive dismissed the allegations as baseless. Outcome not found in research. This is a campaign-finance matter, not a retaliation or subversion act; recorded for balance only.
evidence.quote: German prosecutors have opened a formal probe into AfD leader Alice Weidel over alleged election campaign donations from Switzerland.
evidence.source_title: DW: AfD's Alice Weidel under official investigation

evidence.claim: Weidel and Beatrix von Storch were reported to police/prosecutors for possible incitement to hatred over a New Year's 2018 post describing 'imported, marauding, groping, abusive, knife-stabbing migrant mobs'; Weidel's posts were deleted by platforms and she is described as being under investigation. Police said both may be guilty of incitement to hatred; no outcome given in the source.
evidence.quote: Alice Weidel, one of the party's leaders, wrote on Facebook that authorities were submitting to "imported, marauding, groping, abusive, knife-stabbing migrant mobs".
evidence.source_title: BBC: German AfD MPs under fire for anti-Muslim New Year's Eve messages

evidence.claim: In a 2018 Bundestag debate, Weidel said journalist Deniz Yücel was 'neither a journalist nor a German' and that he should not have German citizenship; rhetoric directed at a named journalist, with no documented direct sanction in the sources reviewed.
evidence.quote: Weidel explains that for her Yücel is neither German nor a journal- ist, and that this "'journalist' who hates our country...should not have German citizenship."
evidence.source_title: Rensmann, Radical Right-Wing Populists in Parliament (2018)

evidence.claim: Weidel used the term 'remigration' at the AfD's Riesa party congress in January 2025 and said 'if it's going to be called remigration, then that's what it's going to be: remigration'; critics characterised the term as mass deportation including of citizens with migrant background. Rhetoric with no documented direct follow-up in the sources reviewed; AfD later omitted the term from a policy paper (Reuters, July 2025).
evidence.quote: "And I have to be honest with you: if it's going to be called remigration, then that's what it's going to be: remigration," she said.
evidence.source_title: BBC: AfD embraces mass deportation of migrants as German election nears

evidence.claim: In a Bundestag general debate, Weidel referred to 'Burqas, girls in headscarves, knifemen enjoying social support, and other no-goods' as threats to prosperity; the speech drew a formal call to order from the Bundestag presidium and criticism from CDU parliamentary leader Volker Kauder. Rhetoric about migrants and Muslims with no documented physical follow-up in sources reviewed.
evidence.quote: "Burqas, girls in headscarves, knifemen enjoying social support, and other no-goods will hardly help to secure (Germany's) wealth, growth and social system."
evidence.source_title: InfoMigrants: Debunking some of the AfD's statements regarding migration

evidence.claim: Weidel won a Hamburg court case against a Facebook user's insulting comment and against Facebook's delayed removal; the court found the comment violated her rights. This is a personal defamation case where Weidel was the complainant.
evidence.quote: The rights of AfD's co-leader Alice Weidel were infringed upon by a vulgar Facebook comment at her expense, a Hamburg court has decided.
evidence.source_title: DW: German court sides with Weidel in Facebook suit

evidence.claim: AfD (with Weidel as co-leader) said lawsuits and rulings were efforts by state power to exclude the opposition, and accused the intelligence agency of 'abuse of state power'; the AfD also said Weidel's party was targeted (rhetoric against institutions, followed by litigation rather than physical act).
evidence.quote: "With our lawsuit, we are sending a clear signal against the abuse of state power to combat and exclude the opposition,"
evidence.source_title: France 24: German AfD party sues after spy agency's label

evidence.claim: Weidel's AfD district association (Kreisverband Bodensee), of which she was deputy chair, received about 132,000 euros in 2017 from Swiss pharmaceutical/wholesale firm PWS, in 18 tranches marked 'Wahlkampfspende Alice Weidel'; the donation was not from an identifiable donor and was partly returned only in April 2018. The Berlin administrative court upheld a roughly 396,000 euro penalty against the AfD for accepting it.
evidence.quote: Auf das Konto von Alice Weidels Kreisverband Bodensee flossen 2017 aus der Schweiz Spenden in Höhe von 132 000 Euro. Ein Gericht verurteilte die AfD zu fast 400 000 Euro Strafe, weil Weidels Kreisverband illegale Zahlungen aus der Schweiz annahm.
evidence.source_title: AfD-Spendenaffäre: Partei muss hohe Strafe zahlen - SZ.de

evidence.claim: Per reporting, Weidel's campaign spending was partly paid from the Swiss-sourced donation: her lawyer's and social-media campaign bills were reportedly routed to the Kreisverband; the parliamentary group spokesman confirmed it, though the Kreisverband disputed it.
evidence.quote: Alice Weidel hat mit den 130.000 Euro aus der Schweiz offenbar einen Medienanwalt und Internetwahlkampf bezahlt, bestätigt ein Sprecher der AfD-Fraktion.
evidence.source_title: AfD: Alice Weidel zahlte mit dubioser Spende offenbar Anwalt und Internetwahlkampf - DER SPIEGEL

evidence.claim: In 2017 Weidel was reported by Die Zeit to have had a Syrian asylum seeker clean her home without a written contract or invoices, paid in cash at 25 Swiss francs per hour (Weidel's lawyer denied employment or salary).
evidence.quote: Both women were paid 25 Swiss francs (€22, $26) per hour in cash, said the report, and neither had a contract of employment and no invoices were provided.
evidence.source_title: AfD's Weidel 'employed asylum-seeker' - DW

evidence.claim: Weidel publicly called the planned abolition of mini-jobs (Minijobs) by the pension commission a disaster, saying up to 7 million people would be affected, and her party's position is to expand mini-jobs.
evidence.quote: Die AfD will die Möglichkeit von Minijobs ausweiten, SPD, Linke und Grüne sind für die Abschaffung.
evidence.source_title: Minijobs abschaffen? Wer dafür ist und warum - ZDFheute

evidence.claim: The DGB union federation characterizes the AfD's tax programme, which Weidel's parliamentary group leads, as a flat tax (max 25%) and abolition of the solidarity surcharge, inheritance, gift and property taxes, with revenue losses in the triple-digit billions; the DGB is an advocacy source.
evidence.quote: Kernstück ist eine Flat Tax mit einem maximalen Steuersatz von 25 Prozent – was vor allem Spitzenverdiener\innen und Unternehmen massiv entlasten würde.
evidence.source_title: AfD: Der Feind der Beschäftigten - DGB

evidence.claim: Weidel's parliamentary group leader proposed to offset the revenue loss from tax cuts by cutting labour and social spending; the AfD opposes a wealth tax on multi-millionaires and has called for abolishing the inheritance tax on very large fortunes (DGB characterization).
evidence.quote: Sie lehnt die Vermögenssteuer für Multimillionäre ab, will die Erbschaftssteuer auf riesige Vermögen gänzlich abschaffen
evidence.source_title: AfD: Der Feind der Beschäftigten - DGB

evidence.claim: Weidel's 2017 Swiss-donation-linked campaign: a Swiss pharmacy/financial firm's donation was linked to Weidel's campaign; the Swiss firm's director said the payment was made 'in trust' for a business friend.
evidence.quote: Das Geld wurde meines Erachtens im Auftrag eines Geschäftsfreundes von einer europäischen Bank an unsere Firma überwiesen mit der Massgabe um dementsprechende Weiterleitung.
evidence.source_title: Spenden-Affäre - Schweizer Pharma-Firma bestätigt AfD-Spende - SRF

evidence.claim: Weidel's Bundestag biography lists her roles as an analyst and vice president in investment advisory at financial firms, and later leadership of a food-industry group's investment management and start-up work.
evidence.quote: Als Analystin und Vice President in der Kapitalanlageberatung und im Vorstandsbüro von führenden Finanzunternehmen beschäftigt
evidence.source_title: Archivierte Abgeordnetenbiografie von Dr. Alice Weidel in der 19. Wahlperiode (2017–2021) - Deutscher Bundestag

evidence.claim: Prosecutors (Staatsanwaltschaft Konstanz) opened an investigation into Weidel and three other AfD Lake Constance Kreisverband officials over alleged illegal Swiss campaign donations (about 132,000 euro in 18 tranches in 2017). Status: investigation, later closed without charges.
evidence.quote: German prosecutors have opened a formal probe into AfD leader Alice Weidel over alleged election campaign donations from Switzerland.
evidence.source_title: AfD's Alice Weidel under official investigation (DW)

evidence.claim: The Bundestag administration treated the 2017 Swiss-sourced payments to Weidel's Kreisverband as an illegal anonymous donation and imposed a fine of 396,016.56 euro on the AfD (the party, not Weidel personally). Courts upheld it in 2022-2023. Status: administrative fine against the party; Weidel not personally sanctioned.
evidence.quote: Der Bundestag wertete dies als verbotene Annahme anonymer Spenden und verhängte ein Bußgeld in Höhe des Dreifachen des überwiesenen Betrags.
evidence.source_title: AfD: Gericht bestätigt Bußgeld in Spendenaffäre um Alice Weidel (Die Zeit)

evidence.claim: Per Spiegel reporting, the 2017 donation of 150,000 Swiss francs was split into inconspicuous tranches and routed through accounts of two Swiss pharma companies; prosecutors reportedly linked the companies' incoming payments to billionaire Henning Conle. Reporting, not a finding against Weidel.
evidence.quote: Das Geld war in unauffällige Tranchen gestückelt und über die Konten von zwei Schweizer Pharmafirmen geleitet worden.
evidence.source_title: AfD und die Parteispendenaffäre: Alice Weidel schweigt zu Kontakten mit Milliardär Henning Conle (Spiegel)

evidence.claim: Weidel's office did not answer Spiegel's questions on whether she personally knew billionaire Henning Conle or when she last had contact with him. Unresolved disclosure question; no finding.
evidence.quote: Die Anfragen blieben unbeantwortet.
evidence.source_title: AfD und die Parteispendenaffäre: Alice Weidel schweigt zu Kontakten mit Milliardär Henning Conle (Spiegel)

evidence.claim: Allegation only: Austrian authorities reportedly examined whether ex-FPÖ official Gerhard Dingler was a straw donor for a 2.35 million euro AfD donation in 2025, reportedly linked to Conle. Unproven; the AfD says Dingler assured it the money was his own. Weidel is not named as a subject of this allegation in the sources reviewed.
evidence.quote: Nach Recherchen des Spiegel und des österreichischen Standard besteht der Verdacht, dass Ex-FPÖ-Funktionär und Geschäftsmann Gerhard Dingler für die Millionentransaktion lediglich als Strohmann fungierte.
evidence.source_title: Illegale Großspende für die AfD? (tagesschau)

evidence.claim: Weidel and co-chair Chrupalla raised their own faction stipend (Funktionszulage) from 6,000 to 12,000 euro per month by faction resolution, on top of the Bundestag salary. Set by the faction itself; reported as disclosed; not a finding of misconduct.
evidence.quote: Per Fraktionsbeschluss haben sich die AfD-Fraktionschefs Alice Weidel und Tino Chrupalla die eigenen Bezüge deutlich von monatlich 6.000 auf 12.000 Euro mit sofortiger Wirkung erhöht.
evidence.source_title: AfD-Fraktionsspitze: Hohe Zulagen für Weidel und Chrupalla (tagesschau)

people.name: Álvaro Uribe
notes: R3: insufficient evidence

people.summary:
Harm tier: major (final score 0.658; harm score 0.7). Benefit tier: none_documented (benefit score 0.0; benefit confidence 0.5). No benefit evidence was found or rated. This is not a negative finding.

Main reasons, in order of weight:

1. Rubric R2 (accountability and state power) scored severity 3, the only nonzero harm score. Under Uribe's presidency, the DAS intelligence agency surveilled journalists, judges and opposition figures from 2004 to 2009 [R2-E06, https://cpj.org/2015/05/officials-sentenced-in-colombia-for-spying-on-jour]. The Supreme Court said two former officials acted with Uribe's consent, and Uribe denied knowledge of the spying [R2-E07]. He took "legal and political responsibility" for his chief of staff's actions while denying ordering illegal wiretaps [R2-E08, https://latamjournalismreview.org/articles/colombias-ex-president-takes-responsibility-for-spying-on-journalists-opponents]. That chief of staff was sentenced to eight years' house arrest [R2-E09].

2. Rubrics R1 and R4 each scored 0 despite recorded evidence. R1 includes the "false positives" findings attributing 6,402 killings to 2002–08 [R1-E06, https://justiceforcolombia.org/jep-peace-court-findings-increase-false-positive-army-killings-to-7837-victims]. Much of the paramilitary material consists of allegations.

3. A 2025 first-instance conviction for witness tampering was overturned on appeal in October 2025 [R2-E02, https://www.nbcnews.com/world/south-america/former-colombian-president-uribe-found-guilty-bribery-trial-rcna221635]. Other matters remain investigations [R4-E06, https://www.bbc.com/mundo/articles/c20y1jk8xy4o].

Rubric R3 had insufficient evidence. Confidence is moderate (0.625) with coverage of 0.75. Many items are allegations or secondary sources, and Uribe denies wrongdoing.

evidence.claim: Supported Convivir private security cooperatives in Antioquia while governor; Human Rights Watch reported Convivir groups in Magdalena Medio and southern Cesar were directed by known paramilitaries and threatened civilians.
evidence.quote: Within his jurisdiction, Uribe openly supported a national program of licensed private security services that became known as CONVIVIR... The groups quickly became controversial – while some reportedly improved security in communities and intelligence coordination with the military, their members were accused of abusing civilians and operated without serious oversight.
evidence.source_title: Álvaro Uribe - Wikipedia

evidence.claim: Colombia's Supreme Court declared three paramilitary massacres (1996-1998) 'crimes of lesser humanity'; imprisoned paramilitary leaders said Uribe was closely involved in forming their organisations; a paramilitary leader alleged a government helicopter hovered over a massacre zone.
evidence.quote: Imprisoned paramilitary leaders involved in the crimes have said that Uribe was closely involved in the formation of their organisations.
evidence.source_title: Former president Uribe implicated in paramilitary massacres - Justice for Colombia

evidence.claim: Colombian Peace and Justice Branch ordered an investigation of Uribe for promoting, sponsoring and supporting paramilitary groups and Convivir connected to them, including while president.
evidence.quote: This Branch affirms the order to furnish copies so that he (Alvaro Uribe Vélez) can be investigated for promoting, sponsoring, and supporting paramilitary groups and Convivir connected to them and/or making plans with them, not only while he was Governor of Antioquia, but later, and even while he was the President of Colombia.
evidence.source_title: Alvaro Uribe, the Convivir, and the Paramilitary Armies (Colombia Support Network)

evidence.claim: Uribe was convicted in Aug 2025 of witness tampering/procedural fraud (pressuring jailed paramilitaries to deny links to him); conviction overturned on appeal in Oct 2025. Conduct is relevant to obstruction of accountability for paramilitary ties; no finding of arms or fossil conduct.
evidence.quote: Uribe, 73, was convicted in August of pressuring paramilitaries to deny links to him, marking the first criminal conviction of a Colombian ex-president.
evidence.source_title: Colombia court overturns former president Uribe's witness tampering conviction - France 24

evidence.claim: Attorney General opened a probe into Uribe for crimes linked to the creation of a paramilitary group (June 2026).
evidence.quote: The office of Colombia's Attorney General has opened an investigation into former President Alvaro Uribe for crimes connected to the creation
evidence.source_title: Colombia's attorney general opens probe into ex-president Uribe over paramilitary case

evidence.claim: Under Uribe's presidency, the JEP's 'false positives' findings attribute 6,402 killings (2002-08) of civilians presented as combat kills; Uribe's government created a reward system for combat kill counts.
evidence.quote: The previous figure declared by the court found 6,402 cases committed in the period 2002-08, during the hard-right government of Álvaro Uribe.
evidence.source_title: JEP peace court findings increase False Positive army killings to 7,837 victims

evidence.claim: A complaint against Uribe under universal jurisdiction was filed in Argentina over alleged responsibility for 6,000+ executions and forced disappearances by the military while president; Argentine courts admitted the case in July 2024 (per secondary sources).
evidence.quote: A complaint has also been filed against him in Argentina, where universal jurisdiction allows for the prosecution of crimes committed anywhere in the world.
evidence.source_title: Colombia court overturns former president Uribe's witness tampering conviction - France 24

evidence.claim: Uribe's administration (through Justicia y Paz law he sponsored, Ley 975 of 2005) demobilized roughly 30,000 paramilitaries; UN criticized that the law did not require full confession or ensure dismantling; the UN OHCHR asked for amendments.
evidence.quote: la ley no exige la plena cooperación del desmovilizado con la justicia.
evidence.source_title: La ONU pide modificar la Ley de Justicia y Paz (Wikinoticias)

evidence.claim: Uribe resigned his Senate seat in August 2020 while under a Supreme Court probe, later withdrew the resignation; a judicial investigation into witness tampering was the stated reason. (Not a safety act; recorded for context only.)
evidence.quote: announced Tuesday that he is resigning his Senate seat, saying his position as a lawmaker has been impeded by a Supreme Court probe
evidence.source_title: Ex-Colombia President Uribe resigning Senate seat amid probe

evidence.claim: Uribe's 2016 campaign against the FARC peace agreement: he publicly led the 'No' campaign and opposed the deal as granting too many benefits to demobilized combatants, and later proposed rolling back agreements.
evidence.quote: Uribe maintained that peace itself was not at issue, but rejected an agreement that, in his view, granted too many benefits to people who had
evidence.source_title: Colombia, 10 Years After Saying 'No' to Peace

evidence.claim: Uribe was ordered into pretrial house arrest by the Colombian Supreme Court (Special Instruction Chamber) on Aug 4, 2020 for alleged witness tampering and procedural fraud; the court cited testimonial evidence, telephone interceptions and risk of obstruction.
evidence.quote: the Special Instruction Chamber ... ordered Uribe's pretrial detention via house arrest
evidence.source_title: NYC Bar Association statement on judicial independence in Colombia

evidence.claim: On 28 July 2025 Judge Sandra Liliana Heredia found Uribe guilty of bribery of witnesses and procedural fraud for attempting, via a lawyer, to get imprisoned paramilitaries to change testimony against Senator Iván Cepeda; sentenced to 12 years house arrest on 1 Aug 2025. Later overturned on appeal on 21 Oct 2025 (appeal court cited structural deficiencies and wiretap exclusion); cassation to Supreme Court announced by Cepeda.
evidence.quote: Judge Sandra Heredia said there was enough evidence to determine that Uribe conspired with a lawyer to coax three former members of paramilitary groups who were in prison into changing testimony they had provided to Ivan Cepeda
evidence.source_title: NBC News / AP: Former Colombian President Uribe found guilty in bribery trial

evidence.claim: Uribe filed a 2012 libel suit against Senator Iván Cepeda, a critic, before the Supreme Court; the Court dismissed the case against Cepeda in 2018 and opened an investigation into Uribe, which Uribe's side characterizes as politically motivated.
evidence.quote: Uribe in 2012 filed a libel suit against Cepeda in the Supreme Court. But in a twist, the high court in 2018 dismissed the accusations against Cepeda and began investigating Uribe.
evidence.source_title: AP News: Appeals court overturns conviction of Colombian ex-President Álvaro Uribe

evidence.claim: Uribe resigned his Senate seat in 2020 (a move that transferred jurisdiction of his case from the Supreme Court to the Attorney General) and later withdrew the resignation, per reporting.
evidence.quote: This led Uribe to renounce his Senate seat in 2020 in a move calculated to transfer jurisdiction of his case to the then-Attorney General, an Uribe ally.
evidence.source_title: Justice for Colombia: Former president Uribe guilty of witness tampering

evidence.claim: WOLA reports that while Attorney General Barbosa (appointed from a list by Uribe protégé President Duque) was in office, he attempted to dismiss the case against Uribe.
evidence.quote: While in office, Barbosa attempted to dismiss the case against Uribe.
evidence.source_title: WOLA: Historic Ruling in Colombia: A Win for the Country's Legal System

evidence.claim: Under Uribe's presidency, the DAS intelligence agency (reporting to the presidency) intercepted phones of reporters, hacked emails and surveilled journalists, judges, human-rights activists and opposition politicians, 2004-2009. At least 17 former DAS officials were identified/convicted out of 68 identified as responsible.
evidence.quote: the DAS, from 2004 to 2009, intercepted the phone calls of local reporters, hacked their e-mails, and subjected them to surveillance and harassment.
evidence.source_title: CPJ: Officials sentenced in Colombia for spying on journalists

evidence.claim: In 2015 the Colombian Supreme Court sentenced two former senior officials; the court said both Hurtado and Moreno acted with the consent of Uribe. Uribe denied knowledge of the spying.
evidence.quote: According to news reports, the court said that both Hurtado and Moreno acted with the consent of Uribe ... Uribe denied any knowledge of the spying ring
evidence.source_title: CPJ: Officials sentenced in Colombia for spying on journalists

evidence.claim: Uribe assumed 'legal and political responsibility' for actions of his chief of staff Bernardo Moreno, one of nine former officials sanctioned in the DAS espionage scandal; Uribe has denied ordering illegal wiretaps.
evidence.quote: Former President Álvaro Uribe has assumed “legal and political responsibility” for actions taken by his former chief of staff, Bernardo Moreno
evidence.source_title: LatAm Journalism Review: Colombia's ex-president takes responsibility for spying on journalists

evidence.claim: Uribe's chief of staff Bernardo Moreno was sentenced to eight years house arrest for his role in the DAS spy program; he was banned 18 years from public service.
evidence.quote: Bernardo Moreno, who was the chief of staff for former President Uribe, was sentenced to eight years of house arrest for his involvement in the spy program.
evidence.source_title: CPJ: Officials sentenced in Colombia for spying on journalists

evidence.claim: A 2009 DAS episode targeted the Supreme Court, which was investigating pro-Uribe lawmakers; DAS agents monitored judges' chambers, including placing a recorder in court chambers via a cleaning lady.
evidence.quote: the DAS targeted the Supreme Court. At the time, the court was investigating dozens of pro-Uribe lawmakers ... In one episode, a DAS agent convinced a cleaning lady to place a tiny tape recorder in
evidence.source_title: TIME: Colombia: Cloud of Scandal Haunts Uribe's Legacy

evidence.claim: HRW reports Uribe's administration engaged in a broad pattern of verbal attacks and intimidation of journalists and Supreme Court justices, and that he amended the constitution to seek a second term and sought a referendum for a third term (rejected by Constitutional Court 7-2 in Feb 2010).

evidence.source_title: HRW: Those Who Value the Rule of Law Should Back Supreme Court's Independence in Colombia

evidence.claim: In 2005 Congress amended the constitution to allow Uribe a second consecutive term; the Constitutional Court upheld the amendment 7-2 in 2005.
evidence.quote: Back in 2005, in a 7-2 decision, the Colombian Constitutional Court decided to uphold the constitutional amendment that allowed current president, Álvaro Uribe, to be reelected.

evidence.claim: Uribe's government's 'false positives' killings: JEP found 6,402 civilians were killed by security forces 2002-2008, during Uribe's government; the JEP has not established how high up the chain of command knowledge reaches. Uribe and Santos claimed some cases were false claims.

evidence.claim: Uribe's side has had actions and rhetoric toward the court: after the July 2025 verdict, Uribe supporters made statements designed to smear and intimidate the court; Senator Cepeda received death threats; Uribe's son posted calling for Cepeda to hand himself to US authorities. evidence.quote: Uribe supporters in Colombia, including influential political leaders, reacted to the court's ruling with groundless accusations and threats. They made statements designed to smear and intimidate the court
evidence.source_title: HRW: Those Who Value the Rule of Law Should Back Supreme Court's Independence in Colombia

evidence.claim: Uribe was the subject of a US federal court subpoena seeking testimony about the Drummond coal company's alleged links to paramilitaries that were accused of killing workers and union leaders; he was not a defendant in that case.

evidence.source_title: Colombia's ex-leader Alvaro Uribe subpoenaed in U.S. federal court

evidence.claim: Prosecutors/plaintiffs said Drummond's Colombian subsidiary president allegedly delivered money to paramilitaries to pay for killings of two union leaders at a Drummond mine; Drummond denied involvement. Uribe is not named as having ordered these killings in this source.

evidence.claim: Special Jurisdiction for Peace (JEP) found the military murdered 6,402 civilians between 2002 and 2008 and presented them as combat kills ('false positives'), during Uribe's presidency; later JEP figure was 7,837 victims 1990–2016.

evidence.claim: Chiquita, not Uribe, paid AUC paramilitaries about $1.7 million 1997–2004 and was found liable by a US jury in 2024 for funding the AUC; the AUC's victims included trade unionists. Uribe is not named in this source as a participant.

evidence.claim: Uribe's 2002 government proposed a 'democratic security' tax on liquid net assets of companies and individuals to fund the military buildup; this is a tax policy he promoted, not a structuring act.
evidence.quote: The government of Álvaro Uribe proposed a tax (not bonds) for "democratic security" to support the military buildup against the Colombian guerrillas.

evidence.claim: Uribe, as governor of Antioquia and then president, pursued policies to encourage foreign investment and handed out thousands of mining titles; the 2001 mining law set generous conditions for foreign firms.

evidence.claim: STATUS: first-instance conviction (Aug 2025, later overturned). On 28 July 2025 Judge Sandra Heredia (Bogotá Juzgado 44 penal) found Uribe guilty of procedural fraud and bribery of a witness/bribery in criminal proceedings, as determinador (instigator), for trying to get imprisoned ex-paramilitaries to change testimony given to Senator Iván Cepeda. evidence.claim: Investigation (not a finding): Colombia's Fiscalía opened a formal investigation into Uribe for alleged links to a paramilitary group in Antioquia and two 1990s massacres, and planned to summon him for questioning (indagatoria) over the 1998 killing of human rights defender Jesús María Valle Jaramillo. evidence.source_title: BBC News Mundo: La Fiscalía de Colombia abre una investigación contra el expresidente Uribe por presuntos vínculos con paramilitares y dos masacres de los 90

evidence.claim: Allegation (unproven) of links between Uribe and Odebrecht: Brazilian diplomatic cables reported four or more meetings between Uribe and Odebrecht executives (including Marcelo Odebrecht) during 2008-2010, a period when Odebrecht later paid bribes for Colombian contracts. Uribe said in 2018 these were open-door meetings with investors. No finding of wrongdoing by Uribe in the Odebrecht matter was located.

people.summary:
Andrew Tate's harm profile is rated minor (final score 0.3952; harm score 0.52), with full coverage and confidence. The main reasons, in order of weight:

Financial conduct (R3, severity 2, top dimension X2): In December 2024, a UK civil court found the brothers had not paid tax on about £21 million of online revenue, and the judge said he was satisfied they engaged in long-standing deliberate conduct to evade tax [R3-E02, https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cm2v1rnvrv0o]. A Romanian ruling records undeclared income for linked companies [R3-E03, https://www.judiciary.uk/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/CCDC-v-TTJ-ruling.pdf]. Hustler's University's affiliate programme paid members for recruiting subscribers and was closed in August 2022 [R3-E09, https://www.businessinsider.com/andrew-tate-closes-program-a-day-being-banned-from-tiktok-2022-8].

Civil findings and criminal allegations (R4, severity 2, top dimension C1): The same UK ruling allowed police to seize about £2.68 million, and the judge left any criminal offences to Romanian courts [R4-E02]. Romanian prosecutors indicted Tate in September 2026 on trafficking, sex-with-a-minor and money-laundering allegations, which are unproven and denied [R4-E05].

Intimidation of accusers (R2, severity 2, top dimension D1): New Yorker reporting describes associates hijacking accounts and posting images of women, and a campaign of legal filings against accusers [R2-E06, R2-E07, https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2026/06/15/andrew-tates-empire-of-abuse]. Prosecutors allege victims were paid or intimidated [R2-E04]. The Tates deny these claims.

Russia-related items (R1) scored severity 0.

Benefit: No benefit evidence was found or rated (benefit_tier none_documented, benefit confidence 0.5). This is not a negative finding.

Caveat: Most items are allegations or civil findings, not criminal convictions, and none has been adjudicated in a criminal court.

evidence.claim: Hustler's University, an online paid course platform headed by Tate, charged subscribers about $49/month and reportedly took crypto payments; Elliptic identified over $2.5 million in crypto payments to its wallets. This is financial-education commerce, not frontier AI, weapons, or fossil fuels.
evidence.quote: Elliptic has identified wallet addresses linked to Hustler's University, which is an online "financial education" platform headed by the controversial – and now banned – social media influencer Andrew Tate.
evidence.source_title: Andrew Tate's "Hustler's University" receives over $2.5 million in crypto | Elliptic

evidence.claim: Hustler's University, which sells AI-related courses (per its own marketing), is a loosely relevant P3 item only as a consumer product; the sources found do not document Tate selling dangerous AI capabilities or access to actors with atrocity records.
evidence.quote: Hustlers University teaches 10+ money-making skill campuses, including e-commerce, strategic marketing, cryptocurrencies, freelancing, business mindset, artificial intelligence, social media and fitness.
evidence.source_title: Hustlers University | Learn Real Money-Making Skills

evidence.claim: Tate's Hustler's University affiliate programme let members earn commission by recruiting new subscribers and encouraged them to post Tate's videos; a commentator called it a social media pyramid scheme (Tate denied this).
evidence.quote: Under the affiliate marketing program, members could earn commission by signing up new subscribers to the course and were encouraged to post videos of Tate to get as many referrals as possible.
evidence.source_title: Andrew Tate closed his Hustlers University affiliate marketing program that helped him go viral a day after he was banned from Meta and TikTok

evidence.claim: Andrew and Tristan Tate travelled to Russia in June (2025) and took part in battlefield-style military training, posting footage of themselves in body armour and helmets and with a Soviet-era T-80BV tank; they attended the St Petersburg International Economic Forum. UK MP Alicia Kearns referred them to Counter Terrorism Policing, alleging possible breach of foreign influence laws; the Tates deny any Russian state payment or direction.
evidence.quote: The Tate brothers shared footage of themselves travelling to Russia in June and taking part in battlefield-style training.
evidence.source_title: Tate brothers referred to counter-terror police over Russia trip

evidence.claim: Kearns alleged the Russia trip raised concerns that the Tates were acting under Russian state direction or paid by it; the Tates deny this. The allegation is unproven and not a finding; no weapons sale or arms contract by Tate is documented in sources found.
evidence.quote: "For the avoidance of any doubt, neither brother received any payment, compensation, financial assistance or direction from the Russian state in connection with the visit."
evidence.source_title: Tate brothers referred to counter-terror police over Russia trip

evidence.claim: Tate's Russia trip footage included a Russian Kremlin-aligned propaganda framing according to critics; the MP said the brothers used Russian military hardware while spouting Russian propaganda. This is a political allegation, not a documented arms sale or weapons transfer.
evidence.quote: Andrew Tate and Tristan Tate's use of Russian military hardware while "spouting Russian propaganda" has been reported to the police by Conservative MP for Rutland and Stamford Alicia Kearns.
evidence.source_title: Tate Brothers Referred To Counterterrorism Police For Alleged Russian Influence

evidence.claim: Romanian appeal court sent the human trafficking case against the Tate brothers back to prosecutors, finding irregularities in the indictment; the court also said Andrew Tate's right to a defense was violated in how he was informed of one accusation.
evidence.quote: The judges also said Andrew Tate's right to a defense was violated in the way he was informed of the accusation of human trafficking regarding one of the alleged victims.
evidence.source_title: Romanian Court Sends Case Against Tate Brothers Back To Prosecutors (RFE/RL)

evidence.claim: Tate publicly attacked prosecutors after the December 2024 ruling, saying they had sought to 'tear apart my life, target everyone I know, and even subpoena the mother of my child'.
evidence.quote: They’ve had years to build their case -- years to tear apart my life, target everyone I know, and even subpoena the mother of my child,
evidence.source_title: Romanian Court Sends Case Against Tate Brothers Back To Prosecutors (RFE/RL)

evidence.claim: Tate and brother Tristan were held in detention then house arrest; courts repeatedly cited flight risk and risk to the investigation. Appeal court denied bail in early 2023.
evidence.quote: In previous rulings that extended their stay in police custody, judges have said the Tate brothers posed a flight risk and that their release could jeopardise the investigation.
evidence.source_title: Internet personality Andrew Tate moved to house arrest after court ruling (Reuters)

evidence.claim: Romanian prosecutors (DIICOT) alleged the Tate brothers' victims had been paid or intimidated to influence them 'not to give statements or to give false statements' in the 2025 indictment.
evidence.quote: DIICOT alleges in the new indictment that their victims had been paid or intimidated in attempts to influence them “not to give statements or to give false statements.”
evidence.source_title: Romanian prosecutors indict Andrew Tate on trafficking minors and money laundering (NBC News)

evidence.claim: Lawyer for alleged victims (Dani Pinter) said supporters doxed the accusers and relatives and that private investigators pursued them; she said she lacked hard evidence Tate directed these attacks, and Tate denied encouraging harassment.
evidence.quote: Supporters of the brothers have doxed private information of her clients and their relatives online, Pinter said, while at least two private investigators have also pursued her clients, digging into their past and showing up at their homes.
evidence.source_title: Andrew Tate accusers forced into hiding after online harassment from 'troll army,' lawyer says (ABC News)

evidence.claim: Per New Yorker investigation based on leaked files: the Tates repeatedly ordered associates to punish women by hijacking their social-media accounts and posting pornographic images of them to followers; Tristan told a worker to 'burn it down' after she fled.
evidence.quote: The Tates’ messages show that they repeatedly ordered associates to punish women by hijacking their social-media accounts and posting pornographic images of them to their followers.
evidence.source_title: Andrew Tate's Empire of Abuse (The New Yorker)

evidence.claim: New Yorker reports the Tates' representatives devised a campaign to attack accusers with scores of legal filings, while affiliates harassed and smeared them online; a team member described it as 'textbook victim intimidation'.
evidence.quote: they devised a campaign to attack his accusers with scores of legal filings, while Tate’s affiliate network harassed and smeared them online. Even one of his team members described it as “textbook victim intimidation.”
evidence.source_title: Andrew Tate's Empire of Abuse (The New Yorker)

evidence.claim: New Yorker reports that a former associate who left was verbally attacked and had her social-media accounts hacked by Tristan Tate, and one associate threatened to set fire to her car.
evidence.quote: he attacked her verbally and hacked her social-media accounts. One of his associates threatened to set fire to her car.
evidence.source_title: Andrew Tate's Empire of Abuse (The New Yorker)

evidence.claim: Florida's attorney general opened a criminal investigation into the Tate brothers in March 2025, issuing search warrants and subpoenas. The Tates' lawyer called the move biased, noting the AG publicly took a side in a lawsuit the Tates filed against a Florida woman.
evidence.quote: Based on a thorough review of the evidence, I've directed the Office of Statewide Prosecution to execute search warrants and issue subpoenas in the now-active criminal investigation into the Tate brothers.
evidence.source_title: Florida opens criminal investigation into Tate brothers (BBC)

evidence.claim: Tate's public statement on the Romanian case: he said prosecutors had 'no evidence' and that there was a conspiracy to silence him; the Romanian court found the indictment flawed.
evidence.quote: Andrew Tate, who has amassed 9.1 million followers on the social media platform X, has repeatedly claimed that prosecutors have no evidence against him and that there is a political conspiracy to silence him.
evidence.source_title: Romanian court extends judicial measures against internet influencer awaiting human trafficking trial (PBS)

evidence.claim: Tate's brothers left Romania in February 2025 after Romanian prosecutors lifted travel restrictions, following reports that US officials pressed for it; DIICOT said charges remained in force and warned failure to observe restrictions could bring harsher measures.
evidence.quote: However, the charges against the Tates remain in force, and they will be expected to return to Romania for court appearances, according to a statement from Romania's Directorate for Investigating Organized Crime and Terrorism, or DIICOT.
evidence.source_title: Andrew Tate and brother land in Florida, DeSantis says they're not welcome (ABC News)

evidence.claim: Tate's 2016 Big Brother removal: footage appeared to show him attacking a woman with a belt; he said it was edited and 'a total lie'.

evidence.quote: IN PARTS OF ANOTHER EXCHANGE, STERN ASKING, WHY DO YOU WANT TO BEAT ME? TATE ALLEGEDLY RESPONDING, WHAT'S THE POINT OF HAVING YOU IF I DON'T BEAT AND

evidence.claim: UK Devon and Cornwall Police civil proceedings alleged that Andrew Tate and his brother failed to pay tax in any country on about £21 million of revenue from their online businesses between 2014 and 2022.
evidence.quote: Devon and Cornwall Police in southwest England brought the case, alleging that the siblings failed to pay taxes, in any country, on revenues of some 21 million pounds (roughly €25 million or $27 million) from their online businesses between 2014 and 2022.

evidence.claim: Westminster Magistrates' Court (Chief Magistrate Goldspring) ruled police could seize about £2.68m from the Tates' frozen accounts; the judge was satisfied the brothers engaged in long-standing deliberate conduct to evade tax.
evidence.quote: In his written ruling, the judge said he was "satisfied" that the brothers had "engaged in long-standing, deliberate conduct in order to evade their tax".

evidence.claim: Police evidence summarised in the ruling shows funds from one account used for debit payments referencing prestige vehicles such as a Bugatti (£689,971.29) and Lamborghini ($644,464.62).
evidence.quote: demonstrates the use of the funds credited to Account 5 for debit payments referencing prestige vehicles such as a Bugatti £689,971.29, Lamborghini $644,464.62, Aston Martin £183,935, Maclaren £332,885.89

evidence.claim: The Tates provided no evidence of tax or VAT returns or payments in the asset-forfeiture proceedings; their planned expert-accountant evidence was abandoned.

evidence.claim: Tate and his brother told the Daily Mirror in June 2022 they ran a 'total scam' business in Romania that used cam models to lure men into sending money.

evidence.source_title: Andrew Tate Closes Marketing Program a Day Being Banned From TikTok - Business Insider

evidence.claim: Tate presided over the War Room network, which charged about $8,000 a year for membership, per the New Yorker investigation.

evidence.claim: Romanian prosecutors (DIICOT) indicted Andrew Tate for trafficking minors, sex with a minor and money laundering; they allege the brothers kept about $1.25 million (about 80% of one victim's camshow earnings) and laundered funds by buying four luxury cars.
