evidence.claim: Tate publicly described his webcam business as relying on getting women to fall in love with him so they would do webcam work, per a since-deleted page on his website.
evidence.quote: “My job was to get women to fall in love with me. Literally, that was my job,” the website said. “My job was to meet a girl, go on a few dates, sleep with her, test if she’s quality, get her to fall in love with me to where she’d do anything I say, and then get her on webcam so we could become rich together.”
evidence.source_title: Andrew Tate said he broke a woman's jaw ahead of Romanian arrest

evidence.claim: Tate claims his webcam business employed 75 women across four countries (his own claim, unverified).
evidence.quote: Andrew Tate claims he was earning $600,000 (£500k) a month during the height of his webcam business which employed 75 women across four countries.
evidence.source_title: Andrew Tate's webcam business employed 75 women across four countries (Mirror)

evidence.claim: Google removed Tate's The Real World app from Google Play after complaints it was a pyramid scheme; advocacy-sourced.
evidence.quote: Google has removed Andrew Tate’s online “learning platform” from Google Play after campaigners complained that the influencer’s The Real World app is a pyramid scheme which exploits teens
evidence.source_title: Andrew Tate's 'The Real World' app banned by Google amid claims it's a pyramid scheme (McCue Jury & Partners)

evidence.claim: UK civil ruling (Dec 2024, Westminster Magistrates' Court, Senior District Judge/Chief Magistrate Paul Goldspring): police may seize £2,683,345 from Andrew Tate, Tristan Tate and a third person, after the court found the brothers had not paid tax on £21m of online-business revenue 2014-2022. Judge said he was 'satisfied' they 'engaged in long-standing, deliberate conduct in order to evade their tax'. Legal status: civil proceedings under Proceeds of Crime Act (civil forfeiture); a civil finding, not a criminal conviction. The tax-evasion finding is a civil-court finding; no criminal tax charge reported in these sources.
evidence.quote: the judge said he was "satisfied" that the brothers had "engaged in long-standing, deliberate conduct in order to evade their tax"
evidence.source_title: Andrew Tate: Police can seize more than £2m from Tate brothers, court rules (BBC)

evidence.claim: In the UK civil forfeiture ruling, the judge found the brothers' financial arrangements 'consistent with concerted tax evasion and money laundering' and that none of the funds were declared to UK or Romanian tax authorities; the brothers provided no evidence on tax payments, and their planned expert-accountant evidence was abandoned. Civil finding; the judge expressly said criminal offences would be determined by Romanian courts.
evidence.quote: the Respondent brothers' "entire financial arrangements are consistent with concerted tax evasion and money laundering"
evidence.source_title: Chief Constable of Devon and Cornwall Police v Emory Andrew Tate and others, ruling (Westminster Magistrates' Court)

evidence.claim: Civil recovery: in August 2025 a further £180,000 deposit on an Aston Martin Valhalla was ordered forfeit in civil court at Westminster Magistrates' Court; the Tate brothers did not oppose the orders. Police said the court was told Andrew Tate paid the deposit in July 2021. Civil forfeiture, unopposed.
evidence.quote: Devon & Cornwall Police has secured a further £180,000 from influencer Andrew Tate in civil court over a deposit he had placed on an Aston Martin supercar.
evidence.source_title: Devon & Cornwall Police seizes £180,000 Aston Martin deposit from Andrew Tate

evidence.claim: Civil tax-evasion claim in London: Devon and Cornwall Police civil proceedings alleged Andrew Tate, Tristan Tate and a woman 'J' paid no tax on £21m of revenue from online businesses 2014-2022. Allegation in a civil proceeding; the brothers denied wrongdoing and the claim was at the time an unproven allegation that later produced the forfeiture ruling above.
evidence.quote: the brothers' traceable earnings of £21m between 2014 and 2022 seemingly came about despite the men having "no significant qualifications, business experience, established companies, shares, intellectual property or similar assets"
evidence.source_title: Andrew Tate: Police can seize more than £2m from Tate brothers, court rules (BBC)

evidence.claim: Romanian criminal case (allegation, unproven, not convicted): DIICOT formally indicted Andrew Tate in Sept 2026 for trafficking minors, sex with a minor, money laundering and witness tampering, and alleged that victims were paid or intimidated 'not to give statements or to give false statements'. Prosecutors allege the brothers kept about $1.25m (~80%) of one victim's webcam income and bought four luxury cars to launder funds. Tate denies all charges. This is an indictment, not a finding.
evidence.quote: DIICOT alleges in the new indictment that their victims had been paid or intimidated in attempts to influence them "not to give statements or to give false statements."
evidence.source_title: Romanian prosecutors indict Andrew Tate on trafficking minors and money laundering (AP via WBAL)

evidence.claim: Allegation (unproven): Romanian prosecutors say the brothers tried to launder webcam-derived funds by buying four luxury cars; Andrew Tate is charged with money laundering and witness tampering. Indictment stage only; no trial verdict.
evidence.quote: The brothers tried to launder the funds by buying four luxury cars, they added.
evidence.source_title: Romanian prosecutors indict Andrew Tate for trafficking minors, money laundering (CNN)

evidence.claim: Romanian investigation (allegation): in Aug 2024 police expanded the investigation to include attempting to influence witnesses; in April 2023 the brothers filed criminal complaints against two witnesses, which the witnesses' lawyer characterised as intimidation. Also a threat letter threatening to sue an accuser for $300m unless she retracted statements (2023). Allegations; the brothers' side disputes intimidation.
evidence.quote: In April 2023, the brothers filed criminal complaints in Romania against two witnesses in the case. The witnesses' lawyer characterised this as intimidation
evidence.source_title: Legal affairs of the Tate brothers (Wikipedia)

evidence.claim: Accuser threat (documented letter, as reported): the Tates' lawyers sent a letter threatening to sue an accuser and her parents for $300m unless she retracted statements; a lawyer for the Tates said otherwise. Allegation of intimidation; no finding.
evidence.quote: The letter threatened to sue the woman and her parents for $300m (£249m) if she did not retract her statements.
evidence.source_title: Andrew Tate threatens legal action against accuser (BBC)

evidence.claim: Court filings by the Tates' own lawyers in US federal extradition/bail proceedings (Aug 2026) stated that luxury cars shown in their social media were rented, a $50m superyacht does not belong to them and they were paid to promote it, and that their multiple-passport claims were satirical; the lawyers described their public wealth displays as 'theatrical'. This is a documented statement to a court that contradicts public wealth claims; it is not a finding of fraud against investors or followers.
evidence.quote: The $50 million superyacht they show off also "does not belong to the Tates," the documents state, explaining they "received payment to promote the ship on social media."
evidence.source_title: Tate brothers admit lavish show of wealth is fake (NY Post)

evidence.claim: Prosecutors in the US federal extradition proceedings (Aug 10, 2026 filing) say the brothers recruited dozens of women into webcam pornography beginning 2014 (allegation, not adjudicated).
evidence.quote: Prosecutors said in an August 10 court filing that Andrew and Tristan Tate recruited dozens of women to engage in work doing webcam pornography beginning in 2014.
evidence.source_title: US court denies Tate brothers' bid to be released from Miami jail (Al Jazeera)

evidence.claim: Florida Attorney General opened a 'now-active' criminal investigation into the Tate brothers in March 2025, issuing search warrants and subpoenas. Investigation only; no charges reported in these sources.
evidence.quote: Based on a thorough review of the evidence, I've directed the Office of Statewide Prosecution to execute search warrants and issue subpoenas in the now-active criminal investigation into the Tate brothers.
evidence.source_title: Florida opens criminal investigation into Tate brothers (BBC)

evidence.claim: Romanian prosecutors lifted a two-year travel ban on the brothers in Feb 2025 after reported pressure from the US administration; NYT investigation reports an order from high levels of Romanian government told prosecutors to find a compromise. Prosecutors said the case was not dropped. This concerns state conduct, but is relevant to the Tates' dealings with officials; the Tates' own role is reported as lobbying through Trump-adjacent allies.
evidence.quote: The prosecutors were told to find a compromise with the Tates. Despite their misgivings, they lifted the travel restrictions
evidence.source_title: How Andrew Tate, Manosphere Star Accused of Rape and Trafficking, Was Freed (NYT)

evidence.claim: Dismissed defamation suit: a US federal judge dismissed a Tate defamation lawsuit against a former US Marine who reported Andrew Tate to the US Embassy and military officials, ruling the sergeant had assisted authorities. Cuts against a claim of retaliation against a witness.
evidence.quote: Rosenberg ruled that the sergeant had assisted the authorities in their investigation and had done what the law encourages people to do against those they suspect of engaging in a crime.
evidence.source_title: Legal affairs of the Tate brothers (Wikipedia)

people.name: Barack Obama
people.summary:
Harm tier: minor (harm score 0.73, final score 0.365; coverage and confidence both 1.0).

Main reasons, in order of weight:

1. Arms sales (R1, severity 3). The administration approved over $278 billion in foreign arms sales, mostly to Mideast nations [R1-E01, https://www.defenseone.com/business/2016/11/obamas-final-arms-export-tally-more-doubles-bushs/133014]. It offered over $115 billion in weapons to Saudi Arabia in 42 deals [R1-E02, https://www.defensenews.com/pentagon/2016/12/14/us-to-halt-arms-sales-to-saudi-arabia-over-yemen-casualties], and approved a UAE sale of about 14,000 Paveway bombs and JDAM kits in July 2016 [R1-E04, same URL]. A $1.15 billion tank sale went ahead despite 64 members of Congress urging delay [R1-E03, https://www.amnestyusa.org/press-releases/saudi-arms-deal-must-be-halted-after-failed-senate-vote].

2. Press and leak investigations (R2, severity 2). The Justice Department obtained two months of phone records for about 20 Associated Press reporters and editors [R2-E01, https://www.ap.org/media-center/ap-in-the-news/2013/govt-obtains-wide-ap-phone-records-in-probe]. A warrant affidavit named Fox News reporter James Rosen a "criminal co-conspirator" though he was not charged [R2-E02, https://www.cbsnews.com/news/fox-news-reporter-secretly-monitored-by-obama-administration-court-documents]. Six employees were indicted under the Espionage Act for sharing classified information with the press, more than all prior administrations combined [R2-E03, https://www.rcfp.org/journals/six-federal-employees-charg].

R3 and R4 scored zero.

Benefit tier: minor_guardian (benefit score 0.2), but benefit confidence is low (0.23) and rests on one item. In December 2016 the administration halted a planned Raytheon munitions sale to Saudi Arabia worth about $350 million over civilian casualties in Yemen [R1-E05, https://www.defensenews.com/pentagon/2016/12/14/us-to-halt-arms-sales-to-saudi-arabia-over-yemen-casualties]. This benefit evidence is reported separately and does not offset the harm findings.

evidence.claim: Obama administration approved more than $278 billion in foreign arms sales over its eight years, more than double the prior administration's total, with most going to Mideast nations.
evidence.quote: The Obama administration has approved more than $278 billion in foreign arms sales in its eight years, more than double the total of the previous administration, according to figures released by the Pentagon on Tuesday.
evidence.source_title: Obama's Final Arms-Export Tally More than Doubles Bush's

evidence.claim: Since January 2009 the Obama administration offered more than $115 billion in weapons to Saudi Arabia in 42 separate deals, more than any US administration in the US-Saudi relationship's history, per a Center for International Policy report.
evidence.quote: Since taking office in January 2009, the Obama administration has offered more than $115 billion in weapons to Saudi Arabia in 42 separate deals, more than any US administration in the 71-year history of the US-Saudi relationship
evidence.source_title: US to Halt Arms Sales to Saudi Arabia Over Yemen Casualties

evidence.claim: In late 2015 the administration sold over $1 billion in bombs and related parts to Saudi Arabia; in September 2016 the Senate failed to block a $1.15 billion tank sale that the administration pursued despite 64 members of Congress urging postponement.
evidence.quote: Ahead of today's vote, 64 Members of Congress urged President Obama in a letter to the White House to postpone the latest arms sale so that the U.S. Congress could properly debate the issue.
evidence.source_title: Saudi Arms Deal Must Be Halted After Failed Senate Vote | Amnesty International USA

evidence.claim: Obama administration approved a UAE sale of more than 14,000 Raytheon-made Paveway bombs and JDAM kits worth about $785 million in July 2016, while UAE was in Yemen air operations.
evidence.quote: As recently as July, the US State Department approved a possible foreign military sale to the United Arab Emirates for more than 14,000 Raytheon-made Paveway guided bombs and Joint Direct Attack Munition kits worth an estimated $785 million. The UAE had been involved in air operations in Yemen since March.
evidence.source_title: US to Halt Arms Sales to Saudi Arabia Over Yemen Casualties

evidence.claim: In December 2016 the administration halted a planned Raytheon precision-guided munitions sale to Saudi Arabia (valued around $350 million) over civilian casualties in the Yemen campaign.
evidence.quote: "We've decided not to move forward with some foreign military sales cases for air-dropped munitions, PGMs (precision-guided munitions)," the unnamed US official told Reuters. "That's obviously a direct reflection of the concerns that we have about Saudi strikes that have resulted in civilian casualties."
evidence.source_title: US to Halt Arms Sales to Saudi Arabia Over Yemen Casualties

evidence.claim: Obama personally oversaw a drone and CIA strike program; the Bureau of Investigative Journalism counted 563 strikes in Pakistan, Somalia and Yemen across Obama's two terms, with 384 to 807 civilians reported killed; the Bureau says Obama oversaw ten times more strikes than Bush.
evidence.quote: A total of 563 strikes, largely by drones, targeted Pakistan, Somalia and Yemen during Obama's two terms, compared to 57 strikes under Bush. Between 384 and 807 civilians were killed in those countries, according to reports logged by the Bureau.
evidence.source_title: Obama's covert drone war in numbers: ten times more strikes than Bush

evidence.claim: The administration's own count said 64 to 116 civilians were killed by US drone and other strikes outside war zones in Pakistan, Yemen and Africa since 2009; Obama signed an executive order on limiting civilian casualties.
evidence.quote: The Obama administration said Friday that between 64 and 116 civilians have been killed by drone and other U.S. strikes in Pakistan, Yemen and Africa since President Barack Obama took office in 2009.
evidence.source_title: Obama reveals how many civilians died in U.S. drone attacks | PBS News

evidence.claim: Obama approved a 2013 presidential policy guidance under which he personally must approve lethal drone strikes against US citizens outside combat areas; the document was disclosed only in edited form after an ACLU FOIA suit.
evidence.quote: President Barack Obama has to personally approve the killing of a U.S. citizen targeted for a lethal drone strike outside combat areas, according to a policy Obama adopted in 2013.
evidence.source_title: Obama releases drone strike 'playbook'

evidence.claim: Obama's Pentagon issued DoD Directive 3000.09 (Nov 2012) on autonomy in weapon systems, which HRW reviewed as allowing human-supervised autonomous weapons and which HRW argued should be strengthened to a ban on fully autonomous weapons.
evidence.quote: On November 21, 2012, the US Department of Defense issued its first public policy on autonomy in weapons systems. Directive Number 3000.09 (the Directive) lays out guidelines for the development and use of autonomous and semi-autonomous weapon systems by the Department of Defense.
evidence.source_title: Review of the 2012 US Policy on Autonomy in Weapons Systems | Human Rights Watch

evidence.claim: Obama approved Shell's Arctic Chukchi Sea exploration drilling; the Obama administration granted final permit to drill for oil in the Arctic Ocean in August 2015, drawing criticism from environmental groups.
evidence.quote: The Obama administration's approval of the final permit to drill for oil in the Arctic Ocean clashes with the message President Barack Obama will deliver when he visits Alaska to emphasize the dangers of climate change
evidence.source_title: Obama administration approves Arctic drilling ahead of president's visit to Alaska

evidence.claim: Obama expanded domestic offshore oil and gas exploration (Alaska, Atlantic, Gulf of Mexico) in 2010, and in his second term lifted the crude oil export ban and approved LNG exports; the Clean Power Plan was blocked by the Supreme Court.
evidence.quote: In his second term, Obama lifted the ban on crude oil exports and approved liquified natural gas exports; his planned regulatory approach to reducing greenhouse pollution in the electricity sector, the Clean Power Plan, was blocked by the U.S. Supreme Court.
evidence.source_title: Energy policy of the Obama administration

evidence.claim: In December 2016 Obama withdrew most of the US Arctic Outer Continental Shelf and certain Atlantic areas from future oil and gas leasing, a permanent ban on new offshore drilling.
evidence.quote: On December 20, 2016, in partnership with our neighbors and allies in Canada, the Obama Administration took historic steps to build a strong Arctic economy, preserve a healthy Arctic ecosystem and protect the United States' fragile Arctic waters, including designating the bulk of our Arctic water and certain areas in the Atlantic Ocean as indefinitely off limits to future oil and gas leasing.
evidence.source_title: Climate & Energy | The Obama Foundation

evidence.claim: Obama's Arctic and Atlantic offshore drilling withdrawal was described by Defenders of Wildlife as 'a visionary act' and recognized that climate goals cannot be achieved while expanding oil and gas into pristine areas.
evidence.quote: And it marks the important recognition that we cannot achieve the nation's climate change goals if we continue to expand oil and gas development into new, pristine environments like the Arctic and Atlantic Oceans.
evidence.source_title: President Obama Bans New Offshore Drilling in Federal Waters of Arctic and Atlantic

evidence.claim: Obama's administration reportedly said the Iran nuclear deal was not an arms-control concession; the administration negotiated and promoted the JCPOA and sought congressional support, with Vice President Biden lobbying Senate Foreign Relations Committee Democrats.
evidence.quote: Obama repeatedly urged Congress to support the agreement, noting the inspections regime's vigor and criticizing opponents for failing to offer a viable alternative.
evidence.source_title: Iran nuclear deal - Wikipedia

evidence.claim: The Obama administration issued the 2016 National AI R&D Strategic Plan and a report on the future of AI that favored industry-government collaboration and did not propose binding safety regulation; the 2016 report called on government to manage AI risks through collaboration.
evidence.quote: 'In the coming years, AI will continue to contribute to economic growth and will be a valuable tool for improving the world, as long as industry, civil society, and government work together to develop the positive aspects of the technology, manage its risks and challenges'
evidence.source_title: President Obama Sets Out US AI Plan

evidence.claim: The Justice Department secretly subpoenaed and obtained two months of phone records for about 20 Associated Press reporters and editors (cell, home and office lines), in a leak investigation; AP was notified after the records had already been handed over. The White House said it was not involved in the decisions.
evidence.quote: The Justice Department secretly obtained two months of telephone records of reporters and editors for the Associated Press news agency, including
evidence.source_title: Gov't obtains wide AP phone records in probe (AP)

evidence.claim: FBI sought a search warrant that named Fox News reporter James Rosen a 'criminal co-conspirator' though he was not charged; agents monitored his movements in and out of the State Department, searched his personal emails and combed his cell phone records, in a leak probe. Court documents (a warrant affidavit) were the source.
evidence.quote: In seeking a search warrant, the FBI called Fox News' James Rosen a "criminal co-conspirator," even though he isn't charged with any crime.
evidence.source_title: Fox News reporter secretly monitored by Obama administration: court documents (CBS News)

evidence.claim: Administration indicted six government employees under the Espionage Act for sharing classified information with the press, more than all previous administrations combined; in each case that reached a courtroom, all or part of the Espionage Act charges were dropped (e.g., Thomas Drake pleaded to a misdemeanor after felony charges were dropped; Kiriakou pleaded to a non-Espionage charge).
evidence.quote: The Obama Administration has indicted six government employees under the 1917 Espionage Act for sharing classified information with the press — more than all previous administrations combined. However, all of the employees whose cases have seen the inside of the courtroom have had all or part of the Espionage Act charges against them dropped.
evidence.source_title: The six federal employees charged under the Espionage Act (Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press)

evidence.claim: Former NSA official Thomas Drake, a whistleblower who raised concerns about the Trailblazer project, was indicted under the Espionage Act in 2010; the government dropped all 10 felony counts in 2011 in exchange for a guilty plea to one misdemeanor, with no jail time.
evidence.quote: On June 9, 2011, all 10 original charges against him were dropped. Drake rejected several deals because he refused to "plea bargain with the truth". He eventually pleaded to one misdemeanor count for exceeding authorized use of a computer.
evidence.source_title: Thomas A. Drake (Wikipedia)

evidence.claim: Former State Department contractor Stephen Kim was prosecuted for discussing a classified North Korea report with Fox News reporter James Rosen; he received a 13-month sentence after a plea deal (per Cato commentary, which is advocacy-leaning).
evidence.quote: The administration prosecuted Stephen Kim, a former State Department official, merely for discussing a classified report about North Korea with Fox News reporter James Rosen.
evidence.source_title: Barack Obama's War on a Free Press (Cato Institute)

evidence.claim: Obama removed Corporation for National and Community Service Inspector General Gerald Walpin in June 2009; the letter to Congress said only that the President no longer had 'the fullest confidence' in him. A House Oversight report (Republican-led) said the firing was contrary to the IG Act; the D.C. Circuit and district court rejected Walpin's challenge, finding the explanation satisfied the minimal statutory mandate.
evidence.quote: It is vital that I have the fullest confidence in the appointees serving as Inspectors General. That is no longer the case with regard to this Inspector General.
evidence.source_title: The Firing of the Inspector General for The Corporation for National and Community Service (House Oversight Committee report)

evidence.claim: Obama's Walpin removal: the explanation was found impermissibly vague by a House report, and the White House wrote a second letter to Congress after the first; a court later upheld the removal as meeting the minimal statutory mandate. The CRS notes Obama was the only president to remove an IG in that period per FactCheck.
evidence.quote: Both the D.C. Circuit and the district court below rejected the IG's arguments, holding that the President's "explanation satisfies the minimal statutory mandate"
evidence.source_title: Congress's Authority to Limit the Removal of Inspectors General (CRS, via EveryCRSReport)

evidence.claim: US intelligence (DNI) reported 473-526 counterterror strikes outside areas of active hostilities in Jan 2009-Dec 2016 with 64-117 non-combatant deaths; NGO estimates (Bureau of Investigative Journalism, New America) were higher. Strikes were in Pakistan, Yemen, Somalia and Libya.
evidence.quote: As many as 117 civilians have been killed in drone and other counterterror attacks in Pakistan, Yemen and elsewhere during President Barack Obama's presidency, according to a report released late Thursday by U.S. intelligence officials.
evidence.source_title: Up to 117 civilians died in strikes during Obama presidency (AP)

evidence.claim: Obama's drone program: CFR reports the 542 strikes Obama authorized killed an estimated 3,797 people including 324 civilians (CFR estimate). Obama reportedly told aides in 2011: 'Turns out I'm really good at killing people.'
evidence.quote: The 542 drone strikes that Obama authorized killed an estimated 3,797 people, including 324 civilians.
evidence.source_title: Obama's Final Drone Strike Data (Council on Foreign Relations)

evidence.claim: Obama's Obama-era drone campaign: the administration's first kinetic action was two drone strikes in Waziristan, Pakistan on January 23, 2009, which killed as many as twenty civilians per CFR.
evidence.quote: On January 23, 2009, just three days into his presidency, President Obama authorized his first kinetic military action: two drone strikes, three hours apart, in Waziristan, Pakistan, that killed as many as twenty civilians.
evidence.source_title: Obama's Final Drone Strike Data (Council on Foreign Relations)

evidence.claim: Obama's Gaza ceasefire statement was criticized on social media as dehumanising and biased (no documented follow-up action; this is a former president's statement and criticism is from social media posts, not a finding).
evidence.quote: Former US President Barack Obama is facing backlash on social media for dehumanising and biased language in his Gaza ceasefire statement.
evidence.source_title: Instagram post on Obama Gaza ceasefire statement backlash

evidence.claim: Obama administration's Treasury (April 2016) took action to limit corporate inversions; the White House said Joint Committee on Taxation estimated inversions could cost the Treasury up to $40 billion over ten years.
evidence.quote: According to Congress’s Joint Committee on Taxation, corporate inversions will cost the U.S. Treasury as much as $40 billion over the next ten years.
evidence.source_title: The Corporate Inversions Tax Loophole: What You Need to Know (whitehouse.gov)

evidence.claim: Obama administration's trade pitch for the Trans-Pacific Partnership (TPP) described it as containing the strongest labor standards in history; critics (Time, Ballotpedia) argued the process was dominated by industry lobbyists and that the deal was bad for American workers. Documented as an act of promoting a trade rule, with labor-standard provisions.
evidence.quote: The TPP includes the strongest labor standards in history, from requiring a minimum wage and worker safety regulations to prohibiting child
evidence.source_title: Here's the deal: the Trans-Pacific Partnership (whitehouse.gov)

evidence.claim: Obama's Ballotpedia-cited critics said the TPP advisory committees were 100% industry representatives and the process was closed to the public; Obama's administration said TPP would bring labor standards.
evidence.quote: Many of the committees - including those on chemicals and pharmaceuticals, aerospace equipment, textiles and clothing, and financial services - are one hundred percent industry representatives.
evidence.source_title: The Trans-Pacific Partnership trade deal: An overview (Ballotpedia)

evidence.claim: Obama's White House attempted to shape labor enforcement through NLRB appointments; Senate Republicans repeatedly opposed his NLRB nominees, jeopardizing the quorum; the administration used recess appointments to circumvent it.
evidence.quote: Senate Republicans, however, repeatedly opposed Obama’s nominees, jeopardizing the quorum the NLRB requires to issue rulings.
evidence.source_title: Labor - Obama Presidency Oral History (Columbia University)

evidence.claim: Obama's Flint water response: state of emergency declared January 2016; federal aid ordered. The Flint Water Advisory Task Force found the MDEQ, MDHHS, Governor's office and state-appointed emergency managers 'fundamentally accountable'; an EPA OIG report found EPA Region 5 failed to implement management controls, delaying the federal response.
evidence.quote: While Flint residents were being exposed to lead in drinking water, the federal response was delayed, in part, because the EPA did not establish clear roles and responsibilities
evidence.source_title: EPA Releases Report on Flint Water Crisis (ASCE summary of EPA OIG)

evidence.claim: Obama's Wikipedia-summarized presidency record: the administration failed to close the 'revolving door' between government and business, though it avoided conflict-of-interest scandals.
evidence.quote: Obama had failed to close the "revolving door" of officials moving between government and business.
evidence.source_title: Presidency of Barack Obama (Wikipedia)

evidence.claim: Obama's post-presidency income: books (royalties of $15.6 million between 2009 and 2017 per The Week), speaking fees, production company deals, and a Netflix deal estimated around $50 million; estimated net worth about $70 million (2024-2025 reporting).
evidence.quote: total royalties of $15.6 million between 2009 and 2017
evidence.source_title: Barack Obama's net worth (The Week)

evidence.claim: The FEC imposed a $375,000 civil penalty on Obama for America (the 2008 Obama presidential campaign committee) via a conciliation agreement for campaign reporting violations (missing 48-hour notices for ~1,266-1,300 contributions totaling ~$1.8-1.9M, late excessive-contribution refunds, wrong contribution dates). Status: civil administrative finding/settlement without admission stated; the FEC dismissed allegations of foreign-national and unknown-donor contributions. Obama himself is not described as personally fined; the committee and DNC paid. Experts quoted called the infractions relatively minor.
evidence.quote: The Commission dismissed allegations that the Committee accepted contributions from foreign nationals or contributions from unknown persons in the name of another in light of the speculative nature of the allegations and the de minimis sums at issue
evidence.source_title: FEC Week of January 7 - January 11, 2013

evidence.claim: Politico reported the Obama 2008 campaign's FEC penalty was paid, with $230,000 from the campaign and the remainder from the DNC; independent experts (former FEC commissioner Michael Toner) called the infractions relatively minor.
evidence.quote: But independent experts, including former FEC commissioner Michael Toner, said after the audit was released that the infractions were relatively minor, given the scope of the campaign.
evidence.source_title: Obama 2008 campaign fined $375,000 - POLITICO

evidence.claim: In June 2012, during the House Oversight Committee's Operation Fast and Furious investigation, Obama invoked executive privilege over disputed Justice Department documents, the first such assertion of his presidency, on the morning of a scheduled committee contempt vote against Attorney General Eric Holder. The DOJ later declined to prosecute Holder. Status: congressional oversight dispute; no finding of obstruction by Obama; contested by Republicans, defended by the administration as deliberative-process protection.
evidence.quote: On the morning of the June vote, Obama invoked executive privilege over the disputed documents, marking the first such assertion of his presidency.
evidence.source_title: The fast, the furious, and the executive privilege - RCFP

evidence.claim: The House panel voted 23-17 to cite Attorney General Holder for contempt of Congress; Obama invoked executive privilege the same morning. (Contempt was against Holder, not Obama.)
evidence.quote: The 23-17 vote to hold Holder in contempt of Congress came as President Obama on Wednesday morning invoked executive privilege of certain documents
evidence.source_title: House panel votes to cite Holder for contempt of Congress - ABC News

evidence.claim: A federal judge in the Southern District of Texas found in 2015 that the Obama administration's attorneys misled the court about early implementation of expanded work permits (DACA/DAPA-related), and ordered limited discovery. This is a judicial finding of misrepresentation by government counsel, as reported by the Texas Attorney General's press release excerpting the order; the judge's wording was 'whether by ignorance, omission, purposeful misdirection, or because they were misled by their clients, the attorneys for the Government misrepresented the facts.' Not a sanction; the judge did not find intentional deception.
evidence.quote: "Whether by ignorance, omission, purposeful misdirection, or because they were misled by their clients, the attorneys for the Government misrepresented the facts."
evidence.source_title: Excerpts from Federal Judge's Order Admonishing Obama Administration for Misleading Court

evidence.claim: Obama accepted a $400,000 fee to give a speech at a healthcare conference hosted by Wall Street firm Cantor Fitzgerald in September 2017, less than 100 days after leaving office; reported by media (not an adjudicated ethics finding). Also reported: a $400,000 speech to A&E Networks and a $60 million book deal. Critics (Sanders, Warren) criticized the fees; no ethics violation was found in these sources.
evidence.quote: The 44th president has accepted an offer to speak at a healthcare conference hosted by Cantor Fitzgerald in September, US media report.
evidence.source_title: Obama criticised for '$400,000 Wall Street speech' - BBC News

evidence.claim: NPR reported Obama had a $60 million book deal and two $400,000 speaking fees after leaving office, and that Republicans and Democrats criticized the Cantor Fitzgerald check; Sanders said 'It just does not look good.' Reporting only; no ethics finding.
evidence.quote: Since stepping out of the Oval Office and into regular-shaped rooms, he's inked a $60 million book deal and two $400,000 speaking fees.
evidence.source_title: Obama Under Scrutiny For Paid Speeches - NPR

evidence.claim: Obama is reported to have said in 2009: 'I did not run for office to be helping out a bunch of fat cat bankers on Wall Street.' (Context for the later Wall Street speaking fees; a statement of intent, not a finding.)
evidence.quote: In 2009, he told CBS: "I did not run for office to be helping out a bunch of fat cat bankers on Wall Street."
evidence.source_title: Obama criticised for '$400,000 Wall Street speech' - BBC News

evidence.claim: ALLEGATION, UNPROVEN: In July 2025 DNI Tulsi Gabbard declassified documents and made a criminal referral alleging Obama-era officials 'manufactured' the 2017 Intelligence Community Assessment on Russia; Gabbard said Obama led the manufacturing. In August 2025 AG Pam Bondi reportedly directed prosecutors to open a grand jury investigation. No charges have been filed against any person per reporting. CNN reported the allegations misrepresent the intelligence community's conclusion. Obama's spokesperson called the claims 'bizarre' and 'ridiculous'.
evidence.quote: No charges have been filed at this point against any potential defendants.

people.summary:
Harm tier: major (harm score 0.78, final score 0.73). Coverage and confidence are both 1.0 for the evidence reviewed.

The main reasons, in order of weight:

1. Institutional conflict (R2, severity 3). The cabinet voted to dismiss Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara, and the High Court later annulled the dismissal [R2-E01, R2-E02]. The government moved to fire Shin Bet chief Ronen Bar, and the court ruled that unlawful [R2-E03, https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/5/21/israeli-top-court-rules-shin-bet-chief-bans-firing-by-netanyahu-unlawful]. In 2026 the government voted to defy a Supreme Court ruling on the broadcast regulator [R2-E04]. Press-related actions include a government boycott of Haaretz and a libel suit against Haaretz and a reporter [R2-E06, R2-E07].

2. Arms and security policy (R1, severity 3). The government approved NIS 350 billion for an independent arms industry [R1-E01, https://www.jpost.com/defense-and-tech/article-881386], and defense exports reached a record $19.2 billion in 2025 [R1-E02]. Reporting alleges Unit 8200 used Microsoft Azure to store Palestinian phone calls for mass surveillance [R1-E05, https://apnews.com/article/microsoft-israel-military-gaza-hamas-artificial-intelligence-3f4bf8036e7e02f385b258bd353af1fd]. This remains an allegation.

3. Economic measures (R3, severity 2). The 2003 austerity package, under Netanyahu as finance minister, cut public-sector wages and reduced income subsidies for many households [R3-E01, R3-E03, https://www.haaretz.com/2003-03-25/ty-article/knesset-approves-economic-plan-histadrut-threatens-strike/0000017f-e1c5-d7b2-a77f-e3c7841d0000]. The 2018 electricity reform was set to cut about 1,800 jobs [R3-E09].

Corruption cases were scored at zero (R4). The charges are unproven allegations in ongoing trials and are not counted as findings here.

Benefit tier: none documented (benefit confidence 0.5). No costly risk-reducing acts were found or rated. This is not a negative finding and does not offset the harm profile.

evidence.claim: Israel's defense exports reached a record $19.2 billion in 2025, rising about 30%; Israel's Defense Ministry reported a 2025 reform that eased export licensing and expanded the list of eligible countries (Netanyahu's government oversaw this ministry)

evidence.claim: Netanyahu's cabinet voted unanimously to dismiss Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara, a critic who had opposed government actions; the Supreme Court froze the move pending legal review.
evidence.quote: The Israeli Cabinet on Monday voted unanimously to fire the attorney general, escalating a long-running standoff between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and the judiciary that critics see as a threat to the country's democratic institutions.

evidence.claim: Israel's High Court unanimously annulled the government's dismissal of the Attorney General, ruling the removal process unlawful.

people.summary:
Bernie Sanders: harm tier "minor" (harm score 0.15, coverage 1.0, confidence 0.81).

Main reasons, in order of weight:

1. Campaign finance (R4, severity 1). The FEC found reason to believe his 2016 and 2020 committees accepted prohibited foreign-national contributions. A conciliation agreement was accepted in August 2022, and the excerpt shows no admission of fault [R4-E01, https://www.fec.gov/files/legal/murs/7587/7587_28.pdf]. A separate 2016 settlement carried a $14,500 civil penalty for in-kind foreign contributions, with no admission of fault [R4-E02, https://vtdigger.org/2018/02/28/sanders-fined-accepting-foreign-donations-2016-election].

2. Other rubrics scored 0. The defense-spending vote record [R1-E15, https://www.politico.com/story/2016/02/bernie-sanders-defense-budget-pentagon-219386] and the Amazon injury findings [R3-E01, https://www.help.senate.gov/dem/newsroom/press/news-sanders-releases-sweeping-report-exposing-how-amazons-obsession-with-speed-injures-workers-at-unprecedented-rates] were rated zero. The Amazon items document the company's injury rates, not Sanders' conduct.

Unproven allegations [R4-E03, R4-E04, R4-E07] have no recorded findings and are not counted as established.

Benefit profile: "minor_guardian" (benefit score 0.35, confidence 1.0). Documented acts include the AI Data Center Moratorium Act [R1-E01, https://www.sanders.senate.gov/press-releases/news-sanders-ocasio-cortez-announce-ai-data-center-moratorium-act], the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act [R1-E02, https://www.sanders.senate.gov/press-releases/news-sanders-casar-introduce-legislation-to-ban-artificial-superintelligence-and-temporarily-pause-advanced-ai-development], and a 2026 Senate panel on AI risks [R1-E05, https://www.sanders.senate.gov/videos/the-existential-threat-of-ai-and-the-need-for-international-cooperation]. These are reported separately and do not offset the harm profile.

evidence.claim: Sanders introduced the AI Data Center Moratorium Act (March 25, 2026) with Rep. Ocasio-Cortez, proposing an immediate federal pause on new AI data center construction until national safeguards are enacted; the bill would also restrain development of advanced AI.
evidence.quote: instituting an immediate federal moratorium on AI data centers until strong national safeguards are in place
evidence.source_title: NEWS: Sanders, Ocasio-Cortez Announce AI Data Center Moratorium Act

evidence.claim: Sanders and Rep. Greg Casar introduced the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (Sept 2026), which would permanently ban development and deployment of superintelligent AI and temporarily pause advanced AI development until a federal regulator sets safety rules.
evidence.quote: The Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act would permanently ban the development and deployment of superintelligent AI and temporarily pause advanced AI development until a federal regulator has established safety rules.
evidence.source_title: NEWS: Sanders, Casar to Introduce Legislation to Ban Artificial Superintelligence and Temporarily Pause Advanced AI Development

evidence.claim: Sanders has publicly called on AI companies to stop funding super PACs opposing AI regulation and criticized AI-influenced super PAC spending.
evidence.quote: Sanders urges a pause on advanced AI and calls on AI companies to stop funding super PACs that oppose AI regulation.
evidence.source_title: Bernie Sanders Calls for AI Guardrails and Criticizes Trump ... (SBS News, Facebook)

evidence.claim: Sanders introduced legislation proposing a 50% tax on AI to fund a sovereign wealth fund, a proposal that would impose costs on AI companies.
evidence.quote: Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., has legislation to slap a 50% tax on AI.
evidence.source_title: Anthropic spends millions in fight over AI regulations in Congress (NY Post)

evidence.claim: Sanders convened a April 2026 Senate panel with leading US and Chinese AI scientists on existential AI risks and international cooperation.
evidence.quote: That's why I'm bringing together leading AI scientists from the U.S. and China to discuss the risks posed by AI.
evidence.source_title: The Existential Threat of AI and the Need for International Cooperation (Sanders Senate site)

evidence.claim: Sanders voted in favor of joint resolutions (June 2019) to block about $8 billion in weapons transfers to Saudi Arabia and other states, citing the Saudi-led war in Yemen.
evidence.quote: he voted in support of joint resolutions to block the transfer of $8 billion in weapons to Saudi Arabia and other states

evidence.claim: Sanders supporters circulated the contact information of Nevada Democratic chair Roberta Lange after the convention, and she received harassing calls and emailed death threats.
evidence.quote: Later that night Sanders supporters circulated the contact information for state party chair Roberta Lange, who was subjected to harassing calls, external and emailed death threats.
evidence.source_title: Nevada chaos should worry Democrats (BBC News)

evidence.claim: Since the convention, Lange was harassed with threatening messages and phone calls, including death threats, and had to be equipped with a security detail, police said.
evidence.quote: Since the convention, state party Chairwoman Lange has been harassed with threatening messages and phone calls, including death threats, and has had to be equipped with a security detail, police said.
evidence.source_title: Ugly Scenes at Nevada Convention Spark Concern Among DNC Officials (ABC News)

evidence.claim: The Sanders statement did not directly address the death threats and allegations of violence at the convention, and did little to ease tensions; Sanders's statement was criticized by Senate Democratic leader Harry Reid.
evidence.quote: The Sanders release, which did not directly address the death threats and allegations violence on Saturday, did little to smooth over raw emotions.
evidence.source_title: Nevada chaos should worry Democrats (BBC News)

evidence.claim: The Nevada state party filed a formal complaint with the DNC alleging the Sanders campaign's 'encouragement of, and complicity in, a very dangerous atmosphere' at the convention.
evidence.quote: We write to alert you to what we perceive as the Sander campaign's penchant for extra-parliamentary behaviour - indeed, actual violence - in place of democratic conduct in a convention setting, and furthermore what we can only describe as their encouragement of, and complicity in, a very dangerous atmosphere
evidence.source_title: Nevada chaos should worry Democrats (BBC News)

evidence.claim: Four Sanders campaign affiliates, including the national data director, accessed and saved Clinton campaign voter-list searches in the party's voter database; the DNC penalized the campaign and briefly limited its access, and the campaign fired one staffer and sued the DNC for breach of contract.
evidence.quote: documents obtained and reviewed by NBC News appeared to show that at least four individuals affiliated with the Sanders campaign conducted searches and saved the Clinton campaign's lists of potential voters over a period of more than 40 minutes.
evidence.source_title: Documents Show Sanders Staffers Breached Clinton Voter Data (NBC News)

evidence.claim: More than two dozen former Sanders 2016 campaign staffers signed a letter about 'sexual harassment and violence' on the campaign; the letter named no specific incidents or individuals and did not imply Sanders himself was involved.
evidence.quote: The letter does not detail any specific incidents or identify anyone suspected of wrongdoing. Nor does it imply that Sanders himself was involved in any of the incidents.
evidence.source_title: Ex Bernie Sanders Staffers Write Letter About 'Harassment and Violence' in 2016 (TIME)

evidence.claim: Sanders, as HELP Committee chair, led an 18-month investigation into Amazon workplace safety; the committee found Amazon warehouses recorded over 30% more injuries than the warehousing industry average in 2023.
evidence.quote: Amazon warehouses recorded over 30 percent more injuries than the warehousing industry average in 2023. The Committee also found that in each of the past seven years, Amazon workers were nearly twice as likely to be injured as workers in other warehouses.
evidence.source_title: Sanders Releases Sweeping Report Exposing How Amazon's Obsession with Speed Injures Workers at Unprecedented Rates (HELP Committee)

evidence.claim: The HELP committee report found Amazon manipulated its workplace injury data to make warehouses appear safer, and that more than two-thirds of its warehouses have injury rates above the industry average.
evidence.quote: Amazon manipulates its workplace injury data to make its warehouses seem safer than they actually are.
evidence.source_title: Connecticut Senate Democrats on Sanders Amazon report

evidence.claim: Amazon's 2019 Prime Day recordable injury rate was over 10 per 100 workers, more than twice the industry average, per the Committee's interim report, which Amazon disputes.
evidence.quote: the graph shows that during Prime Day 2019, Amazon's recordable injury rate—which represents the injuries Amazon is required to disclose to OSHA—was over 10 injuries per 100 workers. That is more than twice the industry average.
evidence.source_title: Amazon Investigation Interim Report, HELP Committee, July 15, 2024

evidence.claim: Sanders' net worth was estimated by Politico at approaching at least $2 million, with three homes; in 2009 his estimated net worth was $105,000 per the Center for Responsive Politics.
evidence.quote: How did he amass three houses and a net worth approaching at least $2 million?
evidence.source_title: The Secret of Bernie's Millions (Politico)

evidence.claim: The FEC found reason to believe that Bernie Sanders and his 2016 and 2020 campaign committees accepted prohibited foreign-national contributions by hiring Cesar Vargas, a Mexican national, for advisory campaign positions and accepting direct contributions from him. Vargas did not respond to the complaint. Status: a conciliation agreement was accepted by the Commission on August 8, 2022. Regulatory conciliation; the excerpt does not show an admission of fault.
evidence.quote: The Commission found that there was reason to believe Respondents violated 52 U.S.C. § 30121(a)(2) and 11 C.F.R. § 110.20(g) and (i)
evidence.source_title: MUR 7587 Bernard Sanders, et al.

evidence.claim: Sanders' 2016 presidential campaign agreed to a $14,500 civil penalty to the FEC to settle a complaint that it accepted prohibited in-kind foreign contributions: the Australian Labor Party paid flights and stipends for seven Australian volunteers ($24,422 total). The campaign did not admit fault in the settlement, which was reached to avoid litigation expense. The campaign said staff mistakenly believed the volunteers' services were exempt.
evidence.quote: The Sanders campaign did not admit fault as part of the agreement, which according to the complaint was reached "solely for the purpose of settling this matter expeditiously and to avoid the expense of litigation."
evidence.source_title: Sanders fined for accepting foreign donations in 2016 election

evidence.claim: Allegation (unproven): Common Cause filed an FEC complaint that Our Revolution, a nonprofit founded by Sanders in 2016, accepted contributions above federal limits and failed to disclose donors while supporting his 2020 campaign. AP reported nearly $1 million from donors who exceeded limits in 2016-2018 tax filings. Our Revolution denied wrongdoing. No FEC finding in sources reviewed.
evidence.quote: Our Revolution has taken in nearly $1 million from donors whose donations exceeded those limits and whose identities it hasn't fully disclosed, according to tax filings for 2016, 2017 and 2018.
evidence.source_title: Watchdog group claims pro-Sanders nonprofit violated campaign finance law

evidence.claim: Allegation (unproven): a Vermont Republican Party official asked prosecutors in 2016 to investigate Sen. Sanders' office; a former bank executive reportedly complained that the office pressured the bank to make the Burlington College loan. No finding against Sanders was recorded.
evidence.quote: Toensing said that in the spring of 2016, a former executive from People's United Bank "complained that Sen. Sanders office pressured them to make the loan to Burlington College."
evidence.source_title: Bernie Sanders defends wife from investigation, fires back at her accuser

evidence.claim: Between April 2021 and November 2024, Sanders directed his presidential and Senate campaign accounts to deposit about $775,000 into the Sanders Institute, a nonprofit run by his wife and stepson, per campaign finance records. Stepson David Driscoll earned $120,000 as executive director in 2023 per tax disclosures. Characterized as diversion by the Washington Examiner; no ethics finding in sources reviewed.
evidence.quote: Between April 2021 and November 2024, Sanders directed his presidential and senatorial campaign accounts to deposit $775,000 into the Sanders Institute, campaign finance records show.
evidence.source_title: Bernie Sanders uses campaign dollars to bankroll family charity

evidence.claim: Our Revolution provided a $105,000 seed loan to the Sanders Institute, founded by Sanders' wife and stepson, which paid the stepson $100,000 a year as executive director; the loan was repaid in 2018. Our Revolution denied wrongdoing in the context of the Common Cause complaint (unproven).
evidence.quote: Our Revolution also provided a $105,000 seed loan to the Sanders Institute, a think tank founded by O'Meara Sanders and her son, David Driscoll.
evidence.source_title: Watchdog group claims pro-Sanders nonprofit violated campaign finance law

evidence.claim: Allegation (unproven): Sen. Bill Cassidy, ranking Republican on HELP, asserted that Sanders, as HELP chair, used committee resources for a field hearing near a nurses' strike to support one side of a labor dispute. No finding was recorded.
evidence.quote: “The Senate HELP Committee should not be used to take sides in a private labor dispute, and especially not to support a favored political organization,” Cassidy wrote to Sanders on Friday.
evidence.source_title: Bernie Sanders accused of ethics violations over allegedly misusing Senate committee to promote strike

evidence.claim: Sanders' former Iowa campaign manager was named in a $30,000 federal discrimination settlement with two former 2016 campaign employees; Sanders apologized and said he had not known of the settlement. This is an employment matter, recorded as context only and not a corruption finding.
evidence.quote: Bernie Sanders apologizes, says he didn't know about $30,000 settlement of 2016 campaign staffer accused of sexual harassment
evidence.source_title: Bernie Sanders apologizes, says he didn't know about $30,000 settlement

people.name: Bill Gates
people.descriptor: American businessman and philanthropist, co-founder of Microsoft
notes: power backfilled from hand-entered reach and authority, not from a research run
people.summary:
Final harm tier: minor (score 0.445; coverage 1.0; confidence 0.98). Benefit tier: minor_guardian (score 0.15), with low benefit confidence (0.23) because only one benefit item was rated.

Harm reasons, in order of weight:

1. Tax structuring (severity 2). A Senate subcommittee estimated Microsoft's Puerto Rico structure saved over $4.5 billion in taxes [R3-E05, https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CHRG-112shrg76071/html/CHRG-112shrg76071.htm]. The IRS later said Microsoft owed about $28.9–29 billion, which Microsoft disputes [R3-E02, https://www.propublica.org/article/irs-microsoft-audit-back-taxes-puerto-rico-billions]. These items concern the company, not Gates personally, and Microsoft says the structures are legal.

2. Antitrust-era conduct (severity 1). Government proposed findings cite a 1996 Gates memo on strategy against Netscape [R2-E01, https://www.justice.gov/atr/file/704861/dl] and testimony that Gates called OEM CEOs to warn them off Netscape [R2-E04, https://www.justice.gov/atr/file/705201/dl]. These rest on testimony and documents.

3. Fossil fuel holdings (severity 1). A Guardian analysis reported $254m invested in fossil fuel extractors in 2024 [R1-E02, https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/jan/19/bill-gates-charity-trusts-holdings-in-fossil-fuel-firms-rise-despite-divestment-claims]. This is press analysis, not an adjudicated finding.

4. Epstein-related matters (severity 0). No legal or regulatory finding against Gates was located.

Benefit: one item was rated. In 2026 Gates publicly called for government safeguards on AI [R1-E07, https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/bill-gates-ai-safeguards-9.7360347]. The record describes this as a public position, not a binding act. Benefit is reported separately and does not offset the harm profile.

evidence.claim: In March 2025 Breakthrough Energy (founded by Gates) laid off dozens of staff, including its European unit and its US public policy team, pulling back from public policy advocacy; the reported reason given was that it 'was not likely to have a significant effect in Washington'.
evidence.quote: In March 2025, Bill Gates dissolved the unit working in Europe and the United States unit working on public policy, because "it was not likely to have a significant effect in Washington"
evidence.source_title: Breakthrough Energy - Wikipedia

evidence.claim: Guardian analysis (Jan 2026) reported that the Gates Foundation Trust invested $254m in companies that extract fossil fuels (Chevron, BP, Shell) in 2024 per end-of-year filings, despite Gates' 2019 divestment claims; the figure was a nine-year high per the report.
evidence.quote: End-of-year filings reveal that in 2024 the trust invested $254m in companies that extract fossil fuels such as Chevron, BP and Shell.
evidence.source_title: Bill Gates charity trust's holdings in fossil fuel firms rise despite divestment claims (Guardian)

evidence.claim: Jacobin analysis (Feb 2025) found the Gates Foundation Trust's IRS-reported fossil fuel stake appeared to have increased after Gates' 2021 announced divestment from direct oil and gas holdings; the foundation reported $8.9bn in Berkshire Hathaway, which holds Chevron and Occidental.
evidence.quote: In 2021, Bill Gates announced that the foundation that bore his name had divested all its "direct holdings in oil and gas companies." But recently available IRS records show that four years on, the Gates Foundation Trust... appears to have done very little to back off oil and gas. In fact, its stake in fossil fuels seems to have increased.
evidence.source_title: Bill Gates Is Playing Both Sides of the Climate Crisis (Jacobin)

evidence.claim: Cascade Investment (Gates's private firm) held a roughly 9% stake in Canadian National Railway, which transports tar sands oil, per investigative reporting; Global Energy Monitor also cites a $1.6bn Cascade investment in CN Rail.
evidence.quote: Cascade invested $1.6 billion dollars in the Canadian National Railway, a major
evidence.source_title: Bill Gates - Global Energy Monitor

evidence.claim: Microsoft, co-founded by Gates, provided Azure cloud and AI services to Israel's Unit 8200 that stored and analyzed millions of intercepted Palestinian phone calls; Microsoft later ceased those services to the unit (Sept 2025) after a Guardian investigation, while saying it does not provide technology to facilitate mass surveillance of civilians.
evidence.quote: Microsoft has cut off cloud computing and AI services to an Israeli military intelligence unit after an investigation revealed the technology was being used for mass surveillance of Palestinian civilians.
evidence.source_title: Times of India: Microsoft cuts cloud services to Israeli military unit (citing Brad Smith memo)

evidence.claim: Microsoft (where Gates was then a non-executive board member/adviser) provided cloud and AI services to dozens of Israeli military units between Oct 2023 and Jan 2025 per leaked commercial records; the company said it provided 'special access to our technologies beyond the terms of our commercial agreements' to Israel's military during the war.
evidence.quote: Microsoft said it had also provided "special access to our technologies beyond the terms of our commercial agreements" and "limited emergency support" to Israel
evidence.source_title: Fortune: Microsoft says it provided AI to Israeli military for war

evidence.claim: In 2026 Gates publicly called for legislation requiring government safeguards on AI, saying self-regulation is not enough; he said AI is powerful enough to 'cause a billion deaths' if used maliciously. These are public positions, not binding acts against his interests.
evidence.quote: "No one thinks self-regulation is enough," he said, calling for legislation to be passed in Congress.
evidence.source_title: CBC News: Bill Gates joins call for AI safeguards

evidence.claim: Gates publicly warned (2026) that the AI industry is downplaying risks and that the government must be involved in monitoring; this is a public position on regulation, not a documented executed act.
evidence.quote: Bill Gates says the AI industry is knowingly downplaying the risks of artificial intelligence because too much investment money is at stake.
evidence.source_title: NBC Philadelphia (social post summarizing Gates interview)

evidence.claim: Gates Foundation committed a $1 billion philanthropic AI initiative and a $50 million partnership with OpenAI for AI deployment in African primary health clinics; the Foundation's AI investment is funding for AI deployment, not a safety act.
evidence.quote: Together, the Gates Foundation and OpenAI are committing $50 million in funding, technology, and technical support to back their work.
evidence.source_title: Gates Notes: The risks of artificial intelligence are real but manageable

evidence.claim: Gates sent a May 1996 internal memo to senior executives outlining a strategy against Netscape in the 'browser war', indicating Microsoft would price many Internet products 'free' and noting analysts would consider Netscape's revenue stream.
evidence.quote: In an internal memorandum Bill Gates sent on May 19, 1996, to his senior executives, he outlined a strategy against Netscape in the “browser war.” Gates indicated that Microsoft would price many of Microsoft’s Internet products “free.”
evidence.source_title: U.S. v. Microsoft Proposed Findings of Fact (DOJ), Section V

evidence.claim: In a June 1996 internal email, Gates reported that he told Intel's CEO Andy Grove it was important Intel NOT publicly say it was standardizing on Netscape browsers.
evidence.quote: “I said it was important that Intel NOT ever publicly say they are standardizing on Netscape browsers.”
evidence.source_title: U.S. v. Microsoft Proposed Findings of Fact (DOJ), Section V

evidence.claim: Microsoft's Paul Maritz told Intel in an August 1995 meeting that Microsoft would 'cut off Netscape's air supply'; the government's proposed findings describe Microsoft's pressure on Intel not to support Netscape as part of a predatory scheme. Maritz denied saying it in testimony; the statement is attributed through McGeady's testimony, not Gates directly.
evidence.quote: Paul Maritz told Intel that Microsoft would “cut off Netscape’s air supply”
evidence.source_title: U.S. v. Microsoft Proposed Findings of Fact (DOJ), Section V

evidence.claim: Barksdale testified that senior Microsoft executives, including Bill Gates, called OEM CEOs to warn them of negative consequences from doing business with Netscape; the government's proposed findings cite this as part of Microsoft's retaliation campaign against Netscape's partners.
evidence.quote: “I was told that senior executives of Microsoft, including Bill Gates, called the CEOs of certain OEMs to warn them that there would be negative consequences resulting from doing business with Netscape.”
evidence.source_title: U.S. v. Microsoft Proposed Findings of Fact (DOJ), Section IV

evidence.claim: Microsoft threatened OEMs that did business with Netscape with changes to their Windows 95 licensing terms; the government's proposed findings state Microsoft threatened to retaliate against OEMs for dealing with Netscape. The findings rest on testimony and documents; the court's ruling found Microsoft had illegally maintained its monopoly.
evidence.quote: Microsoft threatened to retaliate against personal computer OEMs that did business with Netscape by changing the terms of their Windows 95 licensing agreements.
evidence.source_title: U.S. v. Microsoft Proposed Findings of Fact (DOJ), Section IV

evidence.claim: Microsoft's Windows license threatened against Compaq for preinstalling Netscape, as reported in court-revealed accounts; Compaq's IE-icon standoff is described in trial summaries (Gates not named as the direct actor).
evidence.quote: Microsoft had threatened to terminate Compaqs Windows license.
evidence.source_title: Summaries: The Microsoft Case (Harvard Cyberlaw trial transcript summaries)

evidence.claim: Microsoft's board, after a late-2019 complaint from an engineer, hired a law firm to investigate a romantic relationship Gates had with a female employee; the board decided in 2020 Gates should leave the board. Gates's spokesperson said the affair ended amicably and was unrelated to his board departure. This is a personal-conduct matter, not an act against a critic or check on power; recorded for completeness only.
evidence.quote: Members of the board tasked with the matter hired a law firm to conduct an investigation in late 2019 after a Microsoft engineer alleged in a letter that she had a sexual relationship over years with Mr. Gates
evidence.source_title: Bill Gates Left Microsoft Board Amid Probe Into Prior Relationship With Staffer (WSJ)

evidence.claim: Paul Allen said he overheard Gates and Steve Ballmer discussing ways to dilute Allen's Microsoft shares while Allen was undergoing lymphoma treatment; Allen's account is uncorroborated in this source, and Gates later wrote an apology letter according to Allen.
evidence.quote: Allen, who was undergoing treatment for his lymphoma, said he overheard Gates and Steve Ballmer talking about him one night at the office. They were unhappy with the fact that Allen was doing less work, and discussing ways to dilute his Microsoft shares.
evidence.source_title: Microsoft made Paul Allen but it was only the start of his legacy (CNN Business)

evidence.claim: Gates' spokesperson denied that Gates mistreated employees and called allegations of mistreatment false; reporting describes some former workers characterizing his 1980s-1990s style as bullying.
evidence.quote: Still, as a leader, his style has been characterised by some who worked with him in the 1980s and 1990s as bullying. (Gates’ spokesperson has denied he mistreated employees.)
evidence.source_title: Bill Gates' origin story describes a life of privilege, exposing the DNA of some of the tech industry's problems (The Conversation)

evidence.claim: Microsoft shifted at least $39 billion in U.S. profits to Puerto Rico, where its tax consultants persuaded the territory's government to give Microsoft a tax rate of nearly 0%, via a sale of intellectual property to a factory subsidiary.
evidence.quote: Microsoft had shifted at least $39 billion in U.S. profits to Puerto Rico, where the company's tax consultants, KPMG, had persuaded the territory's government to give Microsoft a tax rate of nearly 0%.
evidence.source_title: The IRS Decided to Get Tough Against Microsoft. Microsoft Got Tougher. (ProPublica)

evidence.claim: The IRS challenged Microsoft's Puerto Rico profit-shifting; the IRS later said Microsoft owed about $28.9–29 billion in back taxes for 2004–2013, which Microsoft disputes.
evidence.quote: The $29 billion that the IRS was seeking, he wrote, covered 2004 to 2013. He asserted, however, that the total, were the IRS to ultimately prevail, would be reduced by about $10 billion in taxes that Microsoft has already paid on its overseas profits.
evidence.source_title: Why the IRS Says Microsoft Owes $29 Billion in Back Taxes (ProPublica)

evidence.claim: Microsoft, after the IRS audit, aggressively fought in court, lobbied Congress and changed the law to restrict IRS tools used against it; the company's allies succeeded in 2019 in changing the law.
evidence.quote: Then it aggressively fought back in court, lobbied Congress and changed the law.
evidence.source_title: The IRS Decided to Get Tough Against Microsoft. Microsoft Got Tougher. (ProPublica)

evidence.claim: Microsoft's allies, including the U.S. Chamber of Commerce and tech trade groups, rallied against the IRS audit, and a bill was passed changing IRS procedures for designating summonses and appeals.
evidence.quote: Business organizations, ranging from the U.S. Chamber of Commerce to tech trade groups, rallied, hiring attorneys to jump into the fray on Microsoft's side in court and making their case
evidence.source_title: Senator Warren letter to Microsoft re tax avoidance (2023)

evidence.claim: Microsoft's U.S.-to-Puerto Rico structure was estimated by a Senate subcommittee to have saved over $4.5 billion in taxes on goods sold in the U.S. over three surveyed years.
evidence.quote: By routing its activity through Puerto Rico in this way, Microsoft saved over $4.5 billion in taxes on goods sold in the United States during the 3 years surveyed by the Subcommittee.
evidence.source_title: Offshore Profit Shifting and the U.S. Tax Code (Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations hearing)

evidence.claim: Microsoft's Irish-based structures moved profits offshore; the company reported about 40% of pretax income in Ireland, where it employed about 3% of its workforce; Microsoft said the structures are legal.
evidence.quote: Microsoft said it had generated almost 40 percent of its pretax income in tax-friendly Ireland, where it employed about 3 percent of its global work force.
evidence.source_title: Did Microsoft Shift Its Profits to Low-Tax Countries? (Slashdot summary)

evidence.claim: Microsoft's effective tax rate on operations outside the U.S. was as low as 4.5 percent, per its financial disclosures, and the structures are legal per the company.
evidence.quote: Looking only at Microsoft's operations outside the U.S., however, the company's tax rate is as low as 4.5 percent, according to Microsoft financial disclosures.
evidence.source_title: How Microsoft moves profits offshore to cut its tax bill (Seattle Times)

evidence.claim: Microsoft's UK sales routed through an Irish entity: about $3.3 billion in UK product sales in FY2014 generated about $33 million in UK-subsidiary income tax, approximately 3% effective rate.
evidence.quote: Microsoft sold about $3.3 billion in products to U.K. customers in its 2014 fiscal year. The company's local subsidiary paid $33 million in income tax, an approximate effective rate of about 3 percent if that structure didn't exist.
evidence.source_title: How Microsoft moves profits offshore to cut its tax bill (Seattle Times)

evidence.claim: Gates testified before a House committee in 2008 advocating liberalized H-1B visa rules for skilled foreign workers, arguing that limits on H-1B visas hurt US competitiveness.
evidence.quote: Gates testified before the House Committee on Science Technology on Wednesday about what he sees as a need to liberalize rules for H1-B visas for skilled foreign workers.
evidence.source_title: Bill Gates Targets Visa Rules for Tech Workers (NPR)

evidence.claim: The Trump administration suspended Microsoft's access to the PERM green-card program, saying the company is under investigation for its hiring practices; Microsoft says it pays H-1B employees the same as others doing comparable work.
evidence.quote: The Trump administration is suspending Microsoft's access to a program that allows skilled foreign workers to apply for permanent residency in the United States, saying the company is under investigation for its hiring practices.
evidence.source_title: Trump officials block Microsoft's access to program for employee green cards (Washington Post)

evidence.claim: Microsoft's 2008 Microsoft-era lawsuit: a class action alleging racial discrimination was filed against Microsoft and Bill Gates by employees seeking $5 billion; allegations, not a finding.
evidence.quote: Seven current and former Microsoft Corp. employees have filed a $5-billion class action suit against the world's largest software firm and its chairman Bill Gates for alleged discrimination.
evidence.source_title: Microsoft employees sue for racial discrimination (CBC News)

evidence.claim: Microsoft's wage/Puerto Rico structure: Senate subcommittee noted Microsoft Puerto Rico received $1.6 billion from Microsoft's Irish subsidiary Round Island One, and $1.9 billion per year of IP payments went to the US while Microsoft Puerto Rico got $6.3 billion in revenues.
evidence.quote: So Microsoft Puerto Rico got $1.6 billion from Microsoft's Irish subsidiary called Round Island One. Is that correct? Mr. Sample. That is correct, Senator.
evidence.source_title: Offshore Profit Shifting and the U.S. Tax Code (Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations hearing)

evidence.claim: Gates Foundation external review (WilmerHale, commissioned by the foundation; not a regulator or court; unadjudicated) found Gates and foundation staff met with Jeffrey Epstein about 30 times between 2011 and 2014. The review said Gates was aware of Epstein's sex-offense conviction when conversations began in 2011. Status: commissioned review, no legal finding against Gates.
evidence.quote: "Mr. Gates was aware of reputational concerns related to Epstein's prior conviction and sentencing for a sex-related offense when he began conversations with him in 2011," investigators wrote.
evidence.source_title: Review Says Gates Foundation Did Not Participate in Epstein Crimes - The New York Times

evidence.claim: WilmerHale review found foundation staff raised the risks of associating with Epstein multiple times, and those concerns were raised with senior leadership including Gates. Status: commissioned review summary, unadjudicated. The review did not examine Gates's personal dealings or his private office (Gates Ventures).
evidence.quote: "Foundation staff working on the potential DAF raised on multiple occasions the risks of associating with Epstein because of his prior conviction, and those concerns were raised to senior leadership, including Mr. Gates."
evidence.source_title: Bill Gates ignored repeated warnings about Epstein, independent Gates Foundation review finds

evidence.claim: Allegation (unproven, press report on DOJ-released emails): Epstein helped arrange Gates's investment in a biotech venture started by Gates's longtime science adviser Boris Nikolic, who was leaving Gates's private office, and inserted himself into the exit negotiations. No finding of wrongdoing by Gates.
evidence.quote: In 2013, the correspondence shows, Gates agreed to invest tens of millions of dollars into a venture with Boris Nikolic, who was Gates's longtime scientific adviser. Nikolic was leaving Gates's private office and Epstein inserted himself into the negotiations, which led to the creation of Biomatics Capital.
evidence.source_title: How Epstein Inserted Himself Into a Split Between Bill Gates and a Top Gates Adviser

evidence.claim: In a transcribed interview with the House Oversight Committee (June 10, 2026; not a court finding), Gates said Epstein was involved in negotiating an exit package for an employee leaving Gates's private office. Gates described meeting Epstein as a grave error in judgment and denied witnessing or participating in Epstein's criminal conduct (his own unadjudicated account).
evidence.quote: Around that time, he said, Epstein was also involved in negotiating an exit package for an employee who was leaving Gates' private office.
evidence.source_title: Bill Gates tells Congress that meeting Epstein was "a grave error in judgment" - CBS News

evidence.claim: Gates told the House Oversight Committee (June 10, 2026) that he had been unfaithful in his marriage and that Epstein used knowledge of those affairs to pressure him. This is a personal admission, not a legal or regulatory finding; recorded because it bears on the Epstein-related disclosures.
evidence.quote: It was after this that I learned Epstein had become aware of sensitive information about my personal life, including the fact that I had been unfaithful in my marriage.
evidence.source_title: Bill Gates tells Congress that meeting Epstein was "a grave error in judgment" - CBS News

evidence.claim: Press characterization (not a court finding): Gates's 1998 videotaped deposition in US v. Microsoft was described as evasive, and many of his denials were reportedly refuted by e-mails shown at trial. No formal adjudicated finding that Gates gave false testimony was located.
evidence.quote: Many of Gates's denials and pleas of ignorance were directly refuted by prosecutors with snippets of e-mails Gates both sent and received.
evidence.source_title: United States v. Microsoft Corp. (Wikipedia)

evidence.claim: Trial court (Judge Jackson, Findings of Fact/conclusions as quoted in Wikipedia) said Microsoft executives had been 'inaccurate, misleading, evasive, and transparently false.' This is a court comment about Microsoft executives generally, not a finding specific to Gates.
evidence.quote: Microsoft executives had, according to him, "proved, time and time again, to be inaccurate, misleading, evasive, and transparently false.
evidence.source_title: United States v. Microsoft Corp.

notes: R1 benefit P1: power lifted by documented outcome
