people.summary:
Daniel Kokotajlo, AI researcher. Harm profile: tier "not_a_dick" (harm score 0.15; coverage 1.0; confidence 0.73). The only nonzero rubric is R1 (severity 1), based on role descriptions: a governance and capabilities research history at OpenAI [R1-E08, https://www.hsgac.senate.gov/wp-content/uploads/Daniel-Kokotajlo-Testimony.pdf] and a self-reported stint at Anthropic [R1-E09, https://x.com/DKokotajlo/status/2097478689558806951, tier 3]. Rubrics R2, R3 and R4 scored 0. The R2 subpoenas were issued by OpenAI, not by him [R2-E04]. The R4 item concerns OpenAI's public statement, not his conduct [R4-E02].

Benefit profile: "ultimate_guardian" (benefit score 0.76; confidence 1.0). Documented costly acts include forfeiting vested equity, which he estimated at about 85% of his family's net worth, rather than signing a non-disparagement exit agreement [R1-E01]. OpenAI then removed such clauses from exit paperwork [R1-E02]. He also co-signed the Right to Warn letter [R1-E04], supported SB 1047 [R1-E05, R1-E06], and recommended binding transparency measures to Congress [R1-E10].

The harm and benefit profiles are reported separately and are not netted. The benefit evidence does not reduce or offset the harm rating. Several items are tier 3 self-reports or secondary sites, so the harm rating rests on limited documentation of his own conduct.

evidence.claim: Resigned from OpenAI in April/May 2024 after losing confidence the company would behave responsibly around AGI, and refused to sign OpenAI's non-disparagement exit agreement, forfeiting vested equity he estimated at about 85% of his family's net worth.
evidence.quote: I also refused to sign OpenAI's secret nondisparagement agreement, even though this would have cost me >80% of my family's net worth. (In response to public uproar they changed the paperwork and I was able to keep the equity).
evidence.source_title: Daniel Kokotajlo Senate testimony (HSGAC)

evidence.claim: Public refusal to sign OpenAI's nondisparagement clause led OpenAI to remove nondisparagement clauses from exit paperwork and release former employees from existing obligations; Altman publicly apologized.
evidence.quote: We'll remove nondisparagement clauses from our standard departure paperwork, and we're releasing former employees from existing non-disparagement obligations unless the nondisparagement provision was mutual.
evidence.source_title: Leaked Docs Show OpenAI Pressured Employees Over Exit Agreements: Vox - Business Insider

evidence.claim: Resigned from OpenAI partly due to losing confidence the company would behave responsibly around AGI, as stated in his own 2024 post and reported by Vox.
evidence.quote: I left OpenAI because I lost confidence that it would behave responsibly around the time of AGI. I think AGI is coming and that we are not on track to handle it responsibly.
evidence.source_title: Daniel Kokotajlo — Why They Quit OpenAI (2024) · Ethical AI Departures

people.summary:
Dario Amodei: harm tier "major" (harm score 0.70, final score 0.616). Benefit tier "major_guardian" (benefit score 0.616). Coverage and confidence are both 1.0. The harm and benefit profiles are reported separately and are not netted against each other.

Harm profile: The main driver is a safety-policy rollback, rated severity 3 under R1. The evidence states that Amodei, with the board, approved Responsible Scaling Policy v3, which removed the hard commitment to pause training or deployment when safeguards could not be guaranteed in advance [R1-E01, https://time.com/7380854/exclusive-anthropic-drops-flagship-safety-pledge]. Reporting says Anthropic is now far less constrained by its own safety policies [R1-E02]. A draft federal bill would let government block a model only on imminent-risk thresholds and would preempt some state safety laws [R1-E03, https://www.politico.com/news/2026/10/16/anthropic-ai-safety-01124654; R1-E04]. The other rubrics scored zero. The government dispute, including a court finding of unlawful retaliation against the company [R2-E01], concerns actions taken against the company, not documented harm by Amodei.

Benefit profile: Severity 3 under R1, from costly refusals. Amodei's company refused Pentagon demands to remove limits on mass domestic surveillance and fully autonomous weapons [R1-E10, https://www.anthropic.com/news/statement-department-of-war], and the Pentagon's response was partly blocked in court [R1-E11, https://www.washingtontechnology.com/companies/2026/03/judge-blocks-dods-ban-anthropic-calls-it-first-amendment-retaliation/412451]. The company also reports forgoing several hundred million dollars in revenue by cutting off China-linked firms [R1-E13]. These benefit claims are mainly company-reported.

Confidence is high. A benefit rating does not offset the harm rating.

evidence.claim: Anthropic's CEO Dario Amodei approved, with the board, a revised Responsible Scaling Policy (v3) that removed the hard commitment to pause training or deployment when safeguards could not be guaranteed in advance; Kaplan said 'We didn't really feel... that it made sense for us to make unilateral commitments... if competitors are blazing ahead.'
evidence.quote: In February, according to Kaplan, Amodei decided that keeping the company from training new models while competitors raced ahead would be helpful to nobody.
evidence.source_title: Exclusive: Anthropic Drops Flagship Safety Pledge (TIME)

evidence.quote: the change to the RSP leaves Anthropic far less constrained by its own safety policies, which previously categorically barred it from training models above a certain level if appropriate safety measures weren't already in place.
evidence.source_title: Exclusive: Anthropic Drops Flagship Safety Pledge (TIME)

evidence.claim: Anthropic's draft federal AI bill, pitched quietly to lawmakers, would let government block a model only on imminent risk of more than $1 billion damage or killing/seriously injuring more than 50 people, and would preempt some state AI safety laws.

people.summary:
Harm tier: ultimate (score 0.78; coverage 1.0; confidence 1.0). The main reasons, in order of weight:

Legal findings (R4, severity 3): A New York jury convicted Trump on 34 counts of falsifying business records. He received an unconditional discharge, and the conviction stands [R4-E01, https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/trump-was-sentenced-to-an-unconditional-discharge-in-his-hush-money-conviction-heres-what-that-means]. A civil fraud judgment found inflated asset values and ordered payments of about $450 million with interest. It is under appeal [R4-E04, https://ag.ny.gov/press-release/2024/attorney-general-james-wins-landmark-victory-case-against-donald-trump].

Retaliation and institutional pressure (R2, severity 3): A federal judge found that barring CNN, MS NOW and Politico journalists from the White House likely constituted unlawful retaliation [R2-E05, https://www.npr.org/2026/10/14/nx-s1-6001398/white-house-media-ban]. Courts also struck down executive orders against law firms as retaliatory [R2-E07, https://www.politico.com/news/2025/05/02/trump-law-firms-executive-00324973]. Reuters documented at least 470 targets of retribution [R2-E03].

AI policy (R1, severity 3): Executive Order 14365 directs an AI Litigation Task Force to challenge state AI laws [R1-E01, https://www.lw.com/en/insights/ai-executive-order-targets-state-laws-and-seeks-uniform-federal-standards].

Environmental violations (R3, severity 2): A $4.8 million settlement resolved Clean Water Act violations at Trump Tower Chicago [R3-E12, https://www.cbsnews.com/chicago/news/trump-tower-chicago-settlement-clean-water-act-violations].

Benefit tier: none_documented (score 0; benefit confidence 0.5). No benefit evidence was found or rated. This is not a negative finding, and it does not offset the harm profile.

evidence.claim: Signed Executive Order 14365 (Dec 11, 2025) directing a federal legislative recommendation to preempt conflicting state AI laws, an AI Litigation Task Force to challenge state AI laws, and conditioning federal grant funding on states avoiding 'onerous' AI laws.
evidence.quote: The Order is the latest in a sustained effort by the Trump administration to cabin state influence over AI regulation and to ensure regulation of AI technologies is "minimally burdensome."

evidence.source_title: CBS News - Trump's businesses got at least $7.8 million in foreign payments

evidence.claim: Emoluments suit by DC and Maryland AGs: a federal court ruled in July 2018 that the president is prohibited from accepting almost anything of value from foreign or domestic governments; the suit alleged continued acceptance through Trump International Hotel. Allegation-stage litigation; ruling interpreted the clause, not a finding of specific violation.
evidence.quote: In a historic ruling in July 2018, a federal court judge agreed that the president is prohibited from accepting almost anything of value—including gifts, payments, and benefits—from foreign or domestic governments.
evidence.source_title: DC Attorney General - Emoluments Lawsuit

evidence.claim: Classified documents federal case (S.D. Fla.): Trump indicted on dozens of felony counts for willful retention of classified records at Mar-a-Lago and obstructing FBI efforts to retrieve them. Judge Cannon dismissed the case on July 15, 2024 on the ground that the special counsel's appointment was unconstitutional; the DOJ said it would appeal. Charges were never adjudicated on the merits. Judge Cannon later (Feb 2026) permanently barred release of Special Counsel Smith's report on the matter.
evidence.quote: The indictment included dozens of felony counts accusing him of illegally hoarding classified records from his presidency at his Mar-a-Lago estate in Palm Beach, Florida, and obstructing FBI efforts to get them back. He had pleaded not guilty and denied wrongdoing.
evidence.source_title: AP News - Judge Aileen Cannon dismisses Trump classified documents case

evidence.claim: Trump's Trump Organization loans/financial statements: former Deutsche Bank official testified that Trump's financial statements were key to obtaining loans and that he relied on them before approving the loans (trial testimony in civil fraud case).
evidence.quote: Haigh said he reviewed Trump's financial statements before approving the loans and, at the time, had no reason to doubt their validity.
evidence.source_title: PBS News - Trump's fraudulent financial statements were key to getting loans, former bank official says

people.name: Elon Musk
people.descriptor: CEO of Tesla and SpaceX; South African-born American entrepreneur
notes: power backfilled from hand-entered reach and authority, not from a research run
people.summary:
Elon Musk's harm tier is "ultimate" (harm score 0.78; coverage and confidence 1.0). His benefit tier is "minor_guardian" (score 0.15; benefit confidence 0.70). The two are reported separately and are not netted.

Main harm findings, by weight:

1. Securities and disclosure (severity 3). A 2018 SEC settlement over a "funding secured" tweet required a $20M penalty and his step-down as Tesla chairman [R4-E01, https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/press-releases/2018-226]. A 2026 jury found two 2022 Twitter-deal tweets misled investors; Musk says he will appeal [R4-E06, https://www.dandodiary.com/2026/03/articles/securities-litigation/jury-in-rare-securities-suit-trial-finds-musk-misled-twitter-investors].

2. AI safety reporting (severity 3). xAI released Grok 4 without a public system card [R1-E01, https://fortune.com/2025/07/17/elon-musk-xai-grok-4-no-safety-report]. A tracker reports system cards for only 4 of 16+ Grok releases [R1-E02].

3. Actions against critics and workers (severity 2). A federal magistrate judge called a 2025 post about a former FEMA official "state sanctioned intimidation" [R2-E07, https://www.cbsnews.com/news/elon-musk-kristi-noem-mary-comans-fema-official]. The NLRB found a 2018 tweet an unlawful threat to employees [R2-E13].

4. Workplace injuries (severity 2). Reuters found at least 600 unreported SpaceX injuries since 2014 [R3-E01, https://www.workerscompensation.com/daily-headlines/tesla-spacex-workers-report-numerous-injuries-as-elon-musk-chases-innovation].

Benefit findings were minor (severity 1): signing a 2023 letter calling for an AI training pause [R1-E12, https://time.com/6266679/musk-ai-open-letter] and xAI's voluntary signing of the EU AI Code safety chapter [R1-E16]. The source notes the letter cost him nothing. The low benefit score is not a negative finding and does not offset the harm findings.

evidence.claim: Musk's xAI released Grok 4 in July 2025 without a publicly available system card (a standard safety report), per Fortune; a company representative did not respond on whether one would be released.
evidence.quote: Elon Musk's xAI has released its latest AI model, Grok 4, without a system card—an industry-standard safety report—despite Musk's long-standing warnings about the dangers of AI.
evidence.source_title: Elon Musk's xAI's newest model, Grok 4, is missing a key safety report | Fortune

evidence.claim: Per a tracker of frontier AI safety reporting, xAI has published system cards with evaluations for only 4 of its 16+ Grok model releases; no system card was released for Grok 3 or Grok 4.3.
evidence.quote: out of more than 16 Grok model releases, it has released system cards that contain evaluations for only 4. Notably, xAI did not release a system card for Grok 3, a major release, and has not released a system card for Grok 4.3, its most capable model to date.
evidence.source_title: xAI: The Unpriced Risk in SpaceX's IPO

evidence.claim: After the Grok 4 launch, xAI's model card removed a paragraph reporting UK AI Security Institute findings that an un-safeguarded Grok 4 posed a plausible risk of assisting a non-expert in creating a chemical or biological weapon; the change was not announced.
evidence.quote: Also removed was this paragraph: > Third-party evaluations. The UK AI Security Institute conducted additional evaluations on the dual-use capabilities of our models on providing chemical and biological uplift
evidence.source_title: xAI's new safety framework is dreadful - AI Lab Watch

evidence.claim: xAI contracted with the US Department of Defense for up to $200 million to expand AI capabilities across national security operations.
evidence.quote: xAI, along with OpenAI, Alphabet Inc.'s Google and Anthropic also received contracts of up to $200 million each to support the expansion of AI capabilities across national security operations.
evidence.source_title: Elon Musk's AI Startup xAI Strikes Deal With Pentagon To Deploy Grok Models For Military And Civilian Use

evidence.claim: xAI agreed to allow the military to use Grok in classified systems, a Defense official confirmed to Axios.
evidence.quote: Elon Musk's artificial intelligence company xAI has signed an agreement to allow the military to use its model, Grok, in classified systems, a Defense official confirmed to Axios.
evidence.source_title: Musk's xAI, Pentagon reach deal to use Grok in classified systems | Axios

evidence.claim: Senator Elizabeth Warren questioned the $200M xAI Pentagon contract, citing Grok's antisemitic outputs and that the award was made under questionable circumstances.
evidence.quote: Instead, under your leadership, the department awarded a $200 million contract under questionable circumstances to incorporate an AI company with a product that provides misinformation and offensive, antisemitic responses into DOD's operations
evidence.source_title: Hegseth asked to defend Pentagon's 'uniquely troubling' deal with Musk-owned xAI | DefenseScoop

evidence.claim: SpaceX, Musk's company, was awarded a $4.16 billion Space Force contract in May 2026 for a missile-tracking satellite program within the Golden Dome missile-defense effort.
evidence.quote: On May 29, 2026, Space Systems Command (SSC) awarded SpaceX a $4.16 billion contract for the Space‑Based Airborne Moving Target Indicator (SB‑AMTI) program.
evidence.source_title: SpaceX Wins $6.45B to Build Golden Dome's Space Layer - AeroMorning.com

evidence.claim: xAI has sued states to block AI laws, including California's AB 2013 training-data transparency law and a Minnesota law, while Musk argues for industry self-regulation.
evidence.quote: While Musk is arguing for industry self-regulation, his companies have sought to block states' laws governing AI. For example, xAI sued the state of California, trying to negate its AI Training Data Transparency Act (AB 2013)
evidence.source_title: Elon Musk urges cooperation with AI labs, China to test models | CNBC

evidence.claim: xAI sued the state of Colorado to block a bill protecting people from discrimination in high-risk AI systems making consequential decisions.
evidence.quote: In Colorado, xAI is suing to kill a bill that would protect "people from discrimination in high-risk AI systems making consequential decisions"
evidence.source_title: AI Villains and the Trump Administration: Elon Musk | Revolving Door Project

evidence.claim: Musk gave $158 million to a Senate Leadership Fund-linked PAC in September 2026, and his America PAC has spent heavily on 2026 midterm races opposing Democrats.
evidence.quote: His $158 million gift to the PAC in September is among the largest donations in U.S. political history, according to the New York Times
evidence.source_title: Musk's unprecedented effort to buy the 2026 midterm elections

evidence.claim: Musk said in 2016 that the public must revolt against the fossil fuel industry's propaganda and lobbying; this is a public statement, not an executed act, and is recorded as context on the climate side.
evidence.quote: It is quite worrying, the future of the world," he added. "We need to appeal to the people and educate them to sort of revolt against this and to fight the propaganda of the fossil fuel industry which is unrelenting and enormous.
evidence.source_title: Elon Musk: 'We need a revolt against the fossil fuel industry' | The Guardian

evidence.claim: Musk signed the 2023 open letter calling for a six-month pause on training AI systems more powerful than GPT-4; this is a public statement, not an executed act that cost him anything.
evidence.quote: An open letter with signatures from hundreds of the biggest names in tech, including Elon Musk, has urged the world's leading artificial intelligence labs to pause the training of new super-powerful systems for six months
evidence.source_title: Elon Musk Signs Open Letter Urging AI Labs to Pump the Brakes | TIME

evidence.claim: Musk said he refused Ukraine's request to activate Starlink to Sevastopol for a surprise attack on Russian naval forces, citing the risk of a major act of war and nuclear escalation.
evidence.quote: Elon Musk says he refused to give Kyiv access to his Starlink communications network over Crimea to avoid complicity in a "major act of war".
evidence.source_title: Elon Musk says he withheld Starlink over Crimea to avoid escalation | BBC News

evidence.claim: Musk refused Ukraine's request to enable Starlink for a drone attack on Russian ships in Crimea; sources report some drone boats lost connectivity and washed ashore without exploding.
evidence.quote: Musk declined the request but did not disable any existing coverage. The Atlantic said that some drone boats lost connectivity and washed ashore without exploding.
evidence.source_title: Starlink in the Russo-Ukrainian war - Wikipedia

evidence.claim: In October 2026, SpaceX reportedly throttled Starlink/Starshield service used by Ukraine's military, disrupting missile-interception and drone operations; Musk said limits were a matter for the US military.
evidence.quote: Reports emerged on the morning of October 14 that SpaceX throttled Starlink satellite internet service for the Ukrainian military disrupting a number of critical missions.
evidence.source_title: More than 20 U.S. lawmakers call on Trump and Musk to expand Ukraine's Starlink access

evidence.claim: xAI signed the EU AI Act Code of Practice safety and security chapter, a voluntary step, while calling other parts of the code profoundly detrimental to innovation.
evidence.quote: xAI supports AI safety and will be signing the EU AI Act's Code of Practice Chapter on Safety and Security. While the AI Act and the Code have a portion that promotes AI safety, its other parts contain requirements that are profoundly detrimental to innovation
evidence.source_title: Musk's xAI to sign chapter on safety and security in EU's AI code of practice | Reuters

evidence.claim: xAI co-founders and staff departed in February 2026 as xAI was reorganized after merging with SpaceX; Musk said the departures were part of restructuring.
evidence.quote: Musk Announces xAI Reorganization, Staff Departures. Co-founders exit as the artificial-intelligence startup merges with SpaceX
evidence.source_title: Musk Announces xAI Reorganization, Staff Departures | WSJ

evidence.claim: Musk had USSA (a security contractor) remove Karl Hansen, a Tesla Gigafactory investigator who had filed an SEC whistleblower complaint, from his post within ten minutes after noticing him on duty; Hansen alleges Musk was 'infuriated' and that contractor supervisors were told to 'do something' with him. These are allegations in a lawsuit.
evidence.quote: “Musk noticed that Hansen was on duty,” the lawsuit states. “Musk became infuriated and within ten minutes had USSA remove Hansen from his post.
evidence.source_title: Former Employee Files Suit Against Tesla After Whistleblower Complaint | Courthouse News Service

evidence.claim: Musk accused Tesla technician Martin Tripp of sabotage in 2018 after Tripp leaked information to media; Tesla sued Tripp, and Tripp filed a whistleblower complaint with the SEC and a counterclaim; Tripp later settled for $400,000 after Tesla's suit over tips to reporters.
evidence.quote: Martin Tripp, the Tesla technician who CEO Elon Musk accused of sabotage, has filed a formal whistleblower complaint about the electric vehicle maker and hired a prominent New York law firm to represent him.
evidence.source_title: Tesla whistleblower retains law firm that won $22.5 mln Monsanto suit | CNBC

evidence.claim: A Tesla whistleblower (Cristina Balan) who raised a braking-design safety concern in 2014 was pursued through years of litigation; she says she was demoted and threatened after raising issues. A California appeals panel reversed the confirmation of an arbitration decision in her favour; Tesla did not respond to comment. These are the whistleblower's allegations.
evidence.quote: Engineer Cristina Balan lost her job after she raised a safety concern in 2014 about a design flaw which could affect the cars' braking.
evidence.source_title: Tesla whistleblower wins latest legal battle in fight against Musk | BBC

evidence.claim: In December 2022 X (under Musk) suspended the accounts of about ten journalists who covered Musk and the company; Musk said they were suspended for doxxing by sharing the location of his private jet, citing a new rule created the day before. Accounts were reinstated within hours, with lower follower counts.
evidence.quote: On December 15, 2022, Twitter suspended the accounts of ten journalists who had covered the company and its owner, Elon Musk.
evidence.source_title: December 2022 Twitter suspensions | Wikipedia

evidence.claim: Platform temporarily suspended accounts of multiple prominent journalists and commentators critical of Musk; reporting described this as at least the fifth such purge under Musk; accounts were reinstated hours later with significantly lower follower counts.
evidence.quote: All of the suspended accounts were reinstated a few hours later, but initially with significantly lower follower counts than before.
evidence.source_title: Gee, Guess What Twitter Just Did to Accounts Critical of Elon Musk? | The New Republic

evidence.claim: X sued Media Matters (critical watchdog group) in Texas over its report on ads appearing next to pro-Nazi content; Musk said he was preparing a 'thermonuclear lawsuit'. Media Matters later sued X for breach of contract, calling X's multi-country suits 'a vendetta-driven campaign of libel tourism'. Litigation ongoing as reported.
evidence.quote: Days after the report came out, Musk wrote on X that he was preparing "a thermonuclear lawsuit against Media Matters."
evidence.source_title: Media Matters files a new lawsuit against Elon Musk's X | NPR

evidence.claim: A federal magistrate judge found that Musk, while leading DOGE, posted a photo of former FEMA CFO Mary Comans on X and falsely called her government service a 'criminal action'; the judge wrote the post was 'clearly intended to make her afraid' and 'little more than state sanctioned intimidation'. The judge found a coordinated, premeditated campaign by senior officials including Musk to impugn her, after she was fired.
evidence.quote: “Posting Ms. Comans' picture served no legitimate governmental interest and was little more than state sanctioned intimidation," Fitzpatrick wrote.
evidence.source_title: Judge finds Elon Musk, Kristi Noem engaged in premeditated campaign to smear ex-FEMA official | CBS News

evidence.claim: Musk, as head of DOGE, had federal agencies' fired employees and dismantled USAID; a federal judge ruled DOGE's dismantling of USAID likely violated the Constitution, ordering systems restored and no further cuts without an authorized official's approval; the judge said Musk and DOGE likely acted with power limited to Senate-confirmed officials.
evidence.quote: Musk and DOGE have likely acted with power limited to elected officials or individuals confirmed by the Senate.
evidence.source_title: Judge rules Musk, DOGE dismantling of USAID likely unconstitutional, orders systems restoration | Courthouse News

evidence.claim: Federal judge Tanya Chutkan ordered Musk and DOGE to produce records and answer written questions about DOGE's plans to cull agencies and fire employees, in a suit by state attorneys general; the judge called the attorneys general's concerns about 'unchecked authority of an unelected individual' legitimate.
evidence.quote: A federal judge ordered Elon Musk and the Department of Government Efficiency, or DOGE, to hand over documents and answer questions about the group's plans to trim federal agencies.
evidence.source_title: Judge Orders Musk to Turn Over Records and Answer Questions on DOGE | Business Insider

evidence.claim: Musk publicly called for the impeachment of U.S. District Judge Paul Engelmayer after a ruling restricting DOGE's access to Treasury payment systems, and proposed that 'the worst 1% of appointed judges... be fired every year.'
evidence.quote: The tech mogul said that any judge who rules to prohibit or limit the abilities of DOGE should be impeached, as reported by The New York Post.
evidence.source_title: Elon Musk Slams Anti-DOGE Judge, Calls for Impeachment | Resist the Mainstream

evidence.claim: Musk's America PAC ran a $1 million-a-day voter giveaway to registered voters in swing states before the 2024 election; Philadelphia DA Larry Krasner sued Musk and the PAC calling it an illegal lottery. Musk failed to appear at a state court emergency hearing, and the case was removed to federal court then returned to state court. A state judge rejected the DA's request to block the giveaway on Nov 4, 2024.
evidence.quote: Krasner accuses Musk and the PAC of operating an illegal lottery and of trying to influence voters in the presidential election between Donald Trump and Kamala Harris.
evidence.source_title: Elon Musk $1 million voter lottery suit sent back to state court | CNBC

evidence.claim: The NLRB found Musk's May 2018 tweet about Tesla stock options unlawfully threatened employees who unionized and ordered him to delete it; the Fifth Circuit later reviewed the case, with a dissent finding substantial evidence supported the threat finding, and the appeals court's plurality vacated the order to delete the tweet (Musk's tweet was found to be coercive by the Board; the court's plurality assumed without deciding it was a ULP).
evidence.quote: I would conclude that substantial evidence supported the NLRB’s finding that Musk’s May 20, 2018, tweet was a threat to unilaterally rescind stock options if employees unionized.
evidence.source_title: Fifth Circuit opinion, Tesla v. NLRB, No. 21-60285

evidence.claim: The NLRB in March 2021 found Tesla unlawfully interrogated workers over suspected unionization, unlawfully fired one worker and disciplined another; Musk's tweet was ruled an unlawful threat and Tesla was ordered to have Musk delete it. Senate minority staff memo summarises the NLRB finding, including Musk's stock options threat.
evidence.quote: In March 2021, the NLRB found—in a consolidated complaint of eight charges filed in 2017 and 2018—that Tesla committed multiple violations of the National Labor Relations Act (NLRA) in its fight against a union organizing campaign at its Fremont facility, including one unlawful firing, multiple coercive interrogations of employees, threatening the loss of stock options if employees joined a union, and retaliating against organizers
evidence.source_title: Senate HSGAC Minority Staff Memorandum on Elon Musk Conflicts (2025)

evidence.claim: Musk-led DOGE and the Trump administration fired inspectors general of five federal agencies that had been investigating Musk's companies, per a congressional hearing account; this is reported by a secondary advocacy-leaning outlet and is not directly documented as an act by Musk.
evidence.quote: Congressman Greg Casar (D-TX) revealed that the Inspectors General of five federal agencies that were investigating Musk’s companies had been fired by the Trump administration last month.
evidence.source_title: Elon Musk's Companies Were Under Investigation by Five Inspectors General When the Trump Administration Fired Them | Wall Street on Parade

evidence.claim: Musk posted that Germany's AfD was the only party able to 'save Germany' ahead of the February 2025 election; European governments objected, with critics alleging election interference. No documented act of suppressing opponents is described in this source.
evidence.quote: Musk, writing on his platform X, claimed that the AfD is the only party capable of "saving Germany,"
evidence.source_title: Elon Musk sparks controversy in Germany over AfD endorsement | Euronews

evidence.claim: Musk shared a post by UK far-right figure Tommy Robinson urging people to take to the streets after a Belfast stabbing; a DW report says Musk rebutted incitement claims and his lawyers sent ZDF a cease-and-desist letter. Outcome of the riots not attributed to Musk in the source.
evidence.quote: Musk had shared a post by UK far-right figure Tommy Robinson urging people to take to the streets.
evidence.source_title: Elon Musk moves against German broadcaster ZDF after riot report | DW News

evidence.claim: Musk endorsed a conspiracy theory described by reporting as antisemitic (Great Replacement framing: 'You have said the actual truth') and in 2023 said Irish PM Leo Varadkar 'hates the Irish people'; critics said this was inciting hatred; no physical violence is attributed to Musk in the cited source.
evidence.quote: Musk replied to a thread perpetuating the GREAT REPLACEMENT THEORY with, YOU HAVE SAID THE ACTUAL TRUTH.
evidence.source_title: Media Matters president responds to Elon Musk lawsuit threat | YouTube (transcript)

evidence.claim: Reuters found at least 600 previously unreported workplace injuries at SpaceX since 2014 from OSHA records and interviews, including more than 100 cuts/lacerations, 29 broken bones or dislocations, 8 amputations, 5 electrocutions and one traumatic brain injury.
evidence.quote: Reuters looked at OSHA records, and interviewed current and former employees and determined that at least 600 employees have been injured at SpaceX since 2014.
evidence.source_title: Tesla, SpaceX Workers Report Numerous Injuries as Elon Musk Chases Innovation

evidence.claim: OSHA and CalOSHA fined SpaceX a total of $50,836 for violations stemming from one worker's death and seven serious safety incidents.
evidence.quote: OSHA and CalOSHA have fined the billionaire's rocket company a total of$50,836 for violations stemming from one worker's death and seven serious safety incidents, regulatory records show.
evidence.source_title: At SpaceX, worker injuries soar in Elon Musk's rush to Mars

evidence.claim: SpaceX's Kennedy Space Center site reported an injury rate of 21.5 per 100 workers for 2016, about 27 times the industry average, with 16 of 50 workers injured.
evidence.quote: For that year, the facility reported data amounting to an injury rate of 21.5 injuries per 100 workers, about 27 times the industry average. The facility employed only 50 people at the time
evidence.source_title: At SpaceX, worker injuries soar in Elon Musk's rush to Mars

evidence.claim: OSHA fined SpaceX $115,850 for seven violations after a June crane accident during debris cleanup at Starbase, the largest fine for safety issues in the company's history.
evidence.quote: The Occupational Safety and Health Administration levied fines totaling $115,850 against the Elon Musk-led company for seven violations in a June crane accident
evidence.source_title: Feds dock SpaceX with $116K fine over June crane collapse

evidence.claim: SpaceX has 19 OSHA violations from seven inspections since 2017 across Texas, Washington and California sites.
evidence.quote: SpaceX now has 19 OSHA violations from seven inspections since 2017.
evidence.source_title: Feds dock SpaceX with $116K fine over June crane collapse

evidence.claim: Cal/OSHA cited Tesla for four violations totaling $38,000 after a worker was pinned in a car on a conveyor belt at the Fremont plant because power was not cut to the belt.
evidence.quote: California OSHA cited Tesla Inc. for four violations totaling $38,000 after the car manufacturer "failed to ensure power was cut to a conveyor belt while workers were performing quality inspections."
evidence.source_title: Elon Musk's Disregard For Worker Safety At His Companies (AFL-CIO memo)

evidence.claim: Cal/OSHA cited and fined Tesla for omitting hundreds of serious injuries from annual summary data sent to regulators (2018 injuries, citation issued the following year).
evidence.quote: CAL/OSHA cited the company the following year for omitting hundreds of injuries listed in logs at its factory from annual summary data that the company sends each year to government regulators.
evidence.source_title: Elon Musk's Disregard For Worker Safety At His Companies (AFL-CIO memo)

evidence.claim: Tesla's Austin Gigafactory: one in every 21 workers was reportedly hurt in 2022, according to OSHA records analyzed by The Information.
evidence.quote: A report by The Information looked at OSHA records for the Tesla facility and found that one in every 21 workers at the Gigafactory was reportedly hurt in 2022.
evidence.source_title: Tesla, SpaceX Workers Report Numerous Injuries as Elon Musk Chases Innovation

evidence.claim: The NLRB found Musk's May 20, 2018 tweet an unlawful threat to Tesla employees and ordered it deleted; the Fifth Circuit (Oct 2024) vacated the order requiring Musk's deletion, with a dissent noting Tesla's history of labor violations.
evidence.quote: The Board found that a tweet by Tesla CEO Elon Musk was an unlawful threat and ordered it deleted.
evidence.source_title: Fifth Circuit opinion, Tesla v. NLRB, No. 21-60285

evidence.claim: An NLRB administrative law judge concluded that Tesla violated labor law by threatening employees on May 20, 2018 with loss of stock options if they voted for the union.
evidence.quote: An NLRB administrative law judge concluded that Tesla violated labor laws "by … [t]hreatening employees on May 20, 2018, with loss of stock options if they vote in favor of the Union."
evidence.source_title: Tesla, Inc. v. National Labor Relations Board - New Civil Liberties Alliance

evidence.claim: Civil Rights Department sued Tesla (2022) alleging Black workers at Fremont faced racial harassment, concentration in lower-paying jobs and lower pay; an analysis cited by the department found Black employees earned on average $1,533 less per month than white employees between June 2018 and June 2024. Tesla denies wrongdoing.
evidence.quote: An analysis cited by the Civil Rights Department found that Black employees earned an average of $1,533 less per month than white employees between June 2018 and June 2024.
evidence.source_title: Tesla Goes to Trial Over California's Claims of Widespread Race Discrimination at Fremont Factory

evidence.claim: A federal jury in Miami found Tesla 33% liable for a 2019 Autopilot crash that killed Naibel Benavides Leon, awarding about $43 million compensatory and $200 million punitive; a federal judge upheld the verdict in February 2026.
evidence.quote: The jury awarded $43 million in compensatory damages and $200 million in punitive damages
evidence.source_title: Tesla has to pay historic $243 million judgement over Autopilot crash, judge says

evidence.claim: California DMV found Tesla's use of 'Autopilot' and 'Full Self-Driving' marketing misleading and in violation of state law (Dec 2025); Tesla then stopped using 'Autopilot' in California marketing and sued the DMV in Feb 2026 to reverse the ruling.
evidence.quote: The California Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) today issued its decision in the Tesla administrative case (Case Nos. 21-02188 and 21-02189), adopting the administrative law judge's (ALJ) proposed decision, which concludes that Tesla's use of the terms "autopilot" and "Full Self-Driving Capability" to describe its vehicles' Advanced Driving Assistance Features (ADAS) is misleading and violates state law.
evidence.source_title: DMV Finds Tesla Violated California State Law

evidence.claim: Tesla's Swedish strike with IF Metall lasted about 1,027 days and was declared over in August 2026 after Tesla settled with all striking union members; the union did not win a collective agreement.
evidence.quote: The historic Tesla strike ended on 19 August, after 1,027 days.
evidence.source_title: Tesla Outlasted the World's Strongest Union Movement

evidence.claim: Since January 2025, SpaceX has spent about $5.3 million and Tesla about $3.6 million lobbying Washington on issues including NASA funding, defense spending, military launches and missile defense; no tax or labor-protection lobbying is specified in this source.
evidence.quote: Since January 2025, SpaceX has spent about $5.3 million lobbying on issues including NASA funding, defense spending, military launches, missile defense and procurement, while Tesla has spent about $3.6 million lobbying Washington
evidence.source_title: Elon Musk's 2026 election spending and SpaceX, Tesla business interests

evidence.claim: Musk led DOGE's push to slash the federal workforce and pressed for deregulation on several fronts; GAO says the federal workforce contracted by about 250,000 employees during 2025.
evidence.quote: After spending nearly $300 million to help elect Trump and congressional Republicans in 2024, Musk gained extraordinary access to the administration. He led DOGE's push to slash the federal workforce and pressed for deregulation on several fronts.
evidence.source_title: Elon Musk's 2026 election spending and SpaceX, Tesla business interests

evidence.claim: SEC civil fraud complaint (2018) alleged Musk's Aug 7, 2018 'funding secured' tweet about taking Tesla private at $420/share was false and misleading. Settled without admitting or denying: Musk paid a $20M civil penalty, stepped down as Tesla chairman, and agreed to pre-approval of certain tweets. Legal status: settlement (civil penalty, consent judgment).
evidence.quote: Musk and Tesla will each pay a separate $20 million penalty. The $40 million in penalties will be distributed to harmed investors under a court-approved process.
evidence.source_title: SEC.gov | Elon Musk Settles SEC Fraud Charges; Tesla Charged With and Resolves Securities Law Charge

evidence.claim: SEC complaint alleged Musk tweeted on Aug 7, 2018 that funding was secured to take Tesla private at $420/share, while in truth he knew the transaction was uncertain and subject to numerous contingencies. Allegation, resolved by 2018 settlement.
evidence.quote: The SEC's complaint alleged that, in truth, Musk knew that the potential transaction was uncertain and subject to numerous contingencies.  Musk had not discussed specific deal terms, including
evidence.source_title: SEC.gov | Elon Musk Settles SEC Fraud Charges; Tesla Charged With and Resolves Securities Law Charge

evidence.claim: Judge Liman rejected Musk's bid to throw out the 2018 SEC settlement; the settlement also required that Musk not deny the SEC's 2018 fraud allegations. Liman found Musk's economic-duress argument 'wholly unpersuasive'.
evidence.quote: In the settlement, Musk also agreed not to deny the SEC's allegations in the 2018 securities fraud complaint.
evidence.source_title: Elon Musk ordered to abide by SEC settlement over 2018 tweets | PBS News

evidence.claim: SEC alleged Musk violated the 2018 consent decree's pre-approval provision by posting an inaccurate tweet about Tesla production without pre-approval; a Tesla lawyer confirmed no pre-approval. Allegation by SEC filing; resolution not confirmed in sources reviewed.
evidence.quote: "Musk did not seek or receive pre-approval prior to publishing this tweet, which was inaccurate and disseminated to over 24 million people," the SEC said in a filing with the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York. "Musk has thus violated the court's final judgment by engaging in the very conduct that the pre- approval provision of the final judgment was designed to prevent."
evidence.source_title: Tesla CEO Elon Musk violated SEC agreement with misleading tweet, agency says - ABC News

evidence.claim: A 2nd Circuit panel ruled Musk cannot back out of the 2018 SEC settlement; it said there was 'no evidence' the SEC was using the consent decree to conduct bad-faith, harassing investigations, and that each challenged tweet 'plausibly violated the terms of the consent decree.' Appellate ruling against Musk on the settlement's enforceability.
evidence.quote: "no evidence to support Musk's contention that the SEC has used the consent decree to conduct bad-faith, harassing investigations of his protected speech."
evidence.source_title: Federal appeals court rules Elon Musk tweets need lawyer approval - WHYY

evidence.claim: Federal jury in Pampena v. Musk (private securities class action, N.D. Cal.) found two May 2022 tweets (deal 'temporarily on hold' and 'cannot move forward' due to fake accounts) misled Twitter investors. Civil finding by jury; jury rejected the broader 'scheme to defraud' claim. Musk says he will appeal; post-trial motions pending.
evidence.quote: The jury did find that plaintiff had sufficiently established that two of Musk's tweets – the May 13 tweet ("deal temporarily on hold") and May 17 tweet (deal "cannot move forward" because more than 20% of traffic is fake) – misled investors.
evidence.source_title: Jury in Rare Securities Suit Trial Finds Musk Misled Twitter Investors | The D&O Diary

evidence.claim: Jury in the Twitter class action found Musk's tweets materially false or misleading; deliberated four days and unanimously found the scheme-to-defraud claim unproven. Plaintiffs estimated damages around $2.6 billion; Musk's lawyers said they would appeal.
evidence.quote: The jury deliberated for four days and unanimously found that Musk's tweets on May 13 and May 17 were materially false or misleading.
evidence.source_title: Elon Musk Twitter verdict misled investors before $44 billion purchase

evidence.claim: SEC complaint (Jan 14, 2025) alleges Musk filed his beneficial ownership report 11 days late for his >5% Twitter stake and bought over $500 million of shares at artificially low prices, saving at least $150 million. Settled: Musk's revocable trust agreed to pay a $1.5 million civil penalty without admitting wrongdoing (settlement filed May 4, 2026; pending court approval at that time).
evidence.quote: Filings on Monday, signed by attorneys representing the SEC and Musk, said that Musk's revocable trust would pay a civil penalty of $1.5 million to the commission as part of the settlement.
evidence.source_title: SEC and Elon Musk agree to settle lawsuit over Twitter buyout in 2022

evidence.claim: SEC complaint alleges Musk failed to timely file a beneficial ownership report for his >5% Twitter stake and bought over $500 million of shares at artificially low prices. Allegation, later settled as above.
evidence.quote: According to the SEC's complaint, after Musk failed to timely file a beneficial ownership report by March 24, 2022, he purchased more than $500 million worth of Twitter common stock between March 25, 2022 and April 1, 2022.
evidence.source_title: SEC.gov | Elon R. Musk

evidence.claim: Musk did not appear for SEC investigative testimony in Sept 2023 despite a mutually agreed date, and the SEC had to seek a court order compelling compliance in the Twitter-acquisition probe. Allegation by SEC; a court later ordered him to testify. Not adjudicated as obstruction.
evidence.quote: Musk failed to appear for testimony as required by the investigative subpoena served by the SEC, despite: (1) agreeing to appear for testimony on a mutually agreed upon date in September 2023
evidence.source_title: SEC.gov | Elon R. Musk (litigation release on subpoena enforcement)

evidence.claim: Tesla shareholders sued Musk and board members (2024) alleging a conflict from xAI and diversion of Tesla resources. Allegation only, unadjudicated in sources reviewed.
evidence.quote: a group of Tesla shareholders alleged that Mr. Musk's start-up artificial intelligence (AI) company X.AI Corp. (xAI) represents a conflict of interest. Specifically, he is accused of diverting resources from Tesla.
evidence.source_title: Elon Musk Faces Another Shareholder Lawsuit; Sued By Tesla Shareholders Over Rival AI Company

evidence.claim: Per CNBC reporting (June 2024), Musk allegedly ordered Nvidia to redirect a shipment of AI processors reserved for Tesla to X; this reportedly pushed back Tesla's receipt of over $500 million in GPUs by months. Allegation based on reporting and Nvidia emails; not adjudicated.
evidence.quote: By ordering Nvidia to let privately held X jump the line ahead of Tesla, Musk pushed back the automaker's receipt of more than $500 million in graphics processing units, or GPUs, by months
evidence.source_title: Elon Musk told Nvidia to ship AI chips reserved for Tesla to X, xAI

evidence.claim: Senator Warren wrote to Tesla's board calling Musk's redirection of GPUs from Tesla to X a 'glaring conflict of interest'; a political critique, not a finding.
evidence.quote: Mr. Musk's decision to prioritize Nvidia GPUs for X over Tesla raises a glaring conflict of interest between his financial interest in X and his fiduciary duties as CEO of his publicly-traded company.
evidence.source_title: Warren Slams Elon Musk for "Glaring Conflict of Interest," Misappropriation of Company Resources in Redirecting Critical AI chips from Tesla to X

evidence.claim: Musk served as a special government employee advising the President while his companies (SpaceX, Starlink, Tesla) received federal contracts. Allegations of conflict raised by critics; no finding of violation located. As of the NBC report, no conflict-of-interest waiver for Musk was evident, and the White House said he pledged to avoid conflicts.
evidence.quote: there's no evidence that Musk has obtained a conflict of interest waiver.
evidence.source_title: How the White House is handling Elon Musk and potential conflicts of interest

evidence.claim: Congressional Democrats (Reps. Lynch and Connolly) opened an oversight inquiry into Musk's conflicts at DoD, citing at least $9.5 billion in direct DoD contract funds to his companies. Allegation by lawmakers; no finding of violation.
evidence.quote: This includes at least $9.5 billion in directcontract funds Mr. Musk's companies have received from DOD.
evidence.source_title: Reps. Lynch and Connolly Lead Oversight Investigation into Elon Musk's conflicts of interest at DoD

evidence.claim: Under the 2018 SEC settlement Musk stepped down as Tesla chairman and was ineligible to be re-elected chairman for three years; he remained CEO. A governance sanction tied to the settled fraud charge.
evidence.quote: Under the terms of the settlement, Musk has agreed to step down as chairman of the electric-car company as part of a settlement to resolve a securities fraud charge
evidence.source_title: Elon Musk Settles With SEC, Agrees To Step Down As Tesla Chairman : NPR

evidence.claim: SEC moved in August 2023 to distribute about $41.5M from the 2018 Tesla/Musk penalty fund to investors who traded Tesla stock between Aug 7 and Aug 8, 2018, harmed by the misconduct.
evidence.quote: On August 23, 2023, the Commission filed a motion to distribute $41,532,229.44 to eligible investors.
evidence.source_title: SEC.gov | SEC v. Elon Musk Case No. 18-cv-8865 (S.D.N.Y.)  SEC v. Tesla, Inc. Case No. 18-cv-8947 (S.D.N.Y.)

people.name: Flávio Bolsonaro
people.descriptor: Brazilian senator, son of Jair Bolsonaro
notes: power backfilled from hand-entered reach and authority, not from a research run
people.summary:
Harm tier: **major** (final score 0.64; harm score 0.72; coverage 1.0; confidence 0.91).

Main reasons, in order of weight:

1. **Environmental policy (R1, severity 3).** He voted for the general licensing bill PL 2159/2021 [R1-E01, https://oc.eco.br/passagem-de-flavio-bolsonaro-pelo-senado-e-marcada-por-pautas-antiambientais]. He was the only senator to vote against the Climate Adaptation Act and sought to delay it [R1-E03]. He withdrew his own 2019 Forest Code bill after backlash [R1-E05]. He has also said he would authorize oil exploration near the Amazon [R1-E08, https://gasoutlook.com/analysis/drilling-amazon-river-basin].

2. **Conduct toward institutions (R2, severity 1).** A court barred him from visiting his father for 90 days after he read a letter aloud on a livestream [R2-E01, https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/7/14/brazil-court-bars-bolsonaros-son-from-visiting-ex-president-for-90-days]. He also filed an impeachment request against a Supreme Court justice [R2-E02].

3. **Possible conflict of interest (R3, severity 1).** He filed a November 2025 tax amendment that could have benefited his own law practice [R3-E08, https://tvtnews.com.br/mudanca-flavio-imposto-renda-beneficia-escritorio].

4. **Investigations (R4, severity 0).** The scored item is a Supreme Court probe into alleged slander of Lula [R4-E10]. The wider file includes corruption and money-laundering inquiries, but these are unproven allegations, and the subject denies them.

Benefit tier: **none_documented**. No benefit evidence was found or rated. This is not a negative finding, and it does not offset the harm profile.

evidence.claim: Voted in favor of PL 2159/2021 (the 'PL da Devastação' general environmental licensing bill) in the Senate, weakening environmental licensing rules.
evidence.quote: Flávio Bolsonaro votou a favor do projeto de lei 2159/2021 – o famoso PL da Devastação -, contribuindo para o enfraquecimento da política do licenciamento ambiental.
evidence.source_title: Observatório do Clima - Passagem de Flávio Bolsonaro pelo Senado é marcada por pautas antiambientais

evidence.claim: Voted to override President Lula's veto of the environmental licensing law provision that releases Central Bank-supervised financial institutions from monitoring environmental compliance of projects they finance.
evidence.quote: After President Lula vetoed the provision, Flávio voted in November 2025 to override the veto.
evidence.source_title: Old Wine in New Wineskins: The Changing Face of Bolsonarism's Environmental Agenda

evidence.claim: In May 2024 was the only one of 81 senators to vote against the Climate Adaptation Act (Bill 4,129/2021), and filed requests delaying its plenary consideration.
evidence.quote: In 2024, he was the only one of Brazil's 81 Senators to vote against the Climate Adaptation Act.
evidence.source_title: Observatório do Clima - Flávio Bolsonaro senate record

evidence.claim: Filed requests on May 14, 2024 to send the climate adaptation bill to the CCJ and Economic Affairs committee, delaying plenary discussion; argued the private sector needed to be heard.
evidence.quote: On May 14, 2024, Flávio presented Request No. 331/2024, approved by the Senate plenary, to forward the matter to the Committee on Constitution and Justice (CCJ), delaying the discussion in plenary
evidence.source_title: CENARIUM - In 2024, Flávio Bolsonaro opposed climate adaptation law he helped block

evidence.claim: Withdrew his own 2019 bill (PL 2.362/2019) that would have repealed Forest Code legal-reserve rules to allow economic exploitation of those areas, after backlash.
evidence.quote: Entre os projetos retirados pelo próprio autor está o PL 2.362/2019, que propunha revogar as regras de reserva legal previstas no Código Florestal para permitir a exploração econômica dessas áreas.
evidence.source_title: Valor Econômico - O que Flávio Bolsonaro fez em 7 anos como senador

evidence.claim: Co-authored a 2025 bill to make Indigenous land demarcation subject to legislative approval, and voted for the marco temporal to be put in the Constitution.
evidence.quote: Além disso, no mesmo ano, Flávio foi coautor de um projeto de lei para subordinar a demarcação de terras indígenas à aprovação legislativa.
evidence.source_title: Observatório do Clima - Passagem de Flávio Bolsonaro pelo Senado é marcada por pautas antiambientais

evidence.claim: Campaign platform promises to 'eliminate overlaps between Ibama, Funai and ICMBio', to approve licensing by default if agency does not respond, and to authorize fracking; expressed support for oil exploration near the Amazon river mouth.
evidence.quote: Ao mesmo tempo, defende licenciamento mais rápido, expansão da mineração, exploração de petróleo e gás e abertura para o fraturamento hidráulico, o chamado fracking.
evidence.source_title: VEJA - Flávio promete nova política ambiental, mas mantém modelo de Bolsonaro

evidence.claim: Said he would 'authorize oil exploration in the area around the Amazon River' and strongly promote natural gas as a permanent energy source.
evidence.quote: Bolsonaro has recently stated that his administration will "authorize oil exploration in the area around the Amazon River" and "also strongly promote natural gas as a permanent energy source in Brazil."
evidence.source_title: Gas Outlook - From leaks to lawsuits: Drilling in Brazil's Amazon basin draws scrutiny

evidence.claim: Co-authored / voted in favor of bills in Senate that would allow fossil gas projects to access Fundo Clima financing.
evidence.quote: Também votou a favor de: (1) tornar projetos que incluem gás natural fóssil elegíveis ao financiamento do Fundo Clima
evidence.source_title: Observatório do Clima

evidence.claim: Campaign signaled resuming his father's arms-liberalization policy; said 'legítima defesa tem que voltar' and that he would ease access to weapons; close allies plan to revoke the Estatuto do Desarmamento and Lula-era arms decrees (Decrees 11.366 and 11.615).
evidence.quote: Flávio indica retomar agenda armamentista do pai e promete acesso a armas para legítima defesa
evidence.source_title: Folha de S.Paulo - Flávio indica retomar agenda armamentista do pai

evidence.claim: Sponsored/advocated Senate passage of a 2019-2022 arms-related bill (PL 3.723/2019) that flexibilized civilian gun possession, and in March 2022 urged immediate CCJ vote on it.
evidence.quote: Em março de 2022, Flávio Bolsonaro participou de uma reunião da CCJ destinada à análise do projeto e defendeu sua votação imediata.
evidence.source_title: Congresso em Foco - Cartuchos sem registro: entenda projeto citado na sabatina de Flávio

evidence.claim: Presidential campaign platform: voted/pushes measures on public security; in an interview said he would 'invest in artificial intelligence' for policing cameras (1 million+ cameras linked to police networks).
evidence.quote: Eu vou investir em tecnologia. Eu vou investir em, eu vou investir em inteligência artificial. Eu vou comprar mais de 1 milhão de câmeras com inteligência
evidence.source_title: Flávio discusses bill to remove markings from ammunition casings (GloboNews interview transcript)

evidence.claim: Senator has been linked to a 2023 parliamentary amendment of R$200,000 sent to a project in a militia-controlled area at the request of a man arrested over the Marielle Franco murder.
evidence.quote: Em 2023, Flávio Bolsonaro enviou no Senado uma emenda parlamentar de 200 mil reais para um projeto em área de milícia, a pedido de um dos homens presos por envolvimento no assassinato de Marielle Franco.
evidence.source_title: revista piauí - 'Nosso senador': Flávio Bolsonaro mandou emenda a miliciano do caso Marielle

evidence.claim: Under STF/Federal Police investigation for alleged corruption, money laundering and tax evasion for receiving ~R$61 million (about US$10.6-12M) from Banco Master owner Daniel Vorcaro to finance the Dark Horse film; denies wrongdoing and says it was private sponsorship. Not P1-P5 directly; regulatory-capture angle noted by prosecutors regarding legislative initiatives.
evidence.quote: prosecutors have sought to examine whether legislative initiatives he supported may have benefited Banco Master or related interests.
evidence.source_title: Old Wine in New Wineskins (iconnectblog)

evidence.claim: Supported the Brazilian Senate's AI framework (PL 2338/2023) being pushed toward a lighter 'freedom to innovate' approach; BNamericas reports he proposes legislation focused on freedom to create rather than rules that scare away investment.
evidence.quote: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro proposes legislation "focused on the freedom to create and innovate" instead of "rules that scare away investment."
evidence.source_title: BNamericas - AI regulation in Brazil and Mexico: What's really at stake

evidence.claim: Brazil's Senate approved the AI regulatory bill (PL 2338/2023) on Dec 10, 2024, a risk-based framework including safety assessments for high-risk systems; the bill is stalled in the Chamber. Flávio's specific role not established in sources.
evidence.quote: The Senate approved the bill on December 10, 2024.
evidence.source_title: Library of Congress Global Legal Monitor

evidence.claim: Justice Alexandre de Moraes barred Senator Flávio Bolsonaro from visiting his father, Jair Bolsonaro (under house arrest), for 90 days after finding that Flávio had read a letter from his father aloud on a livestream, which the court treated as an indirect breach of the father's social-media ban.
evidence.quote: Brazil's Supreme Court has barred presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro from visiting his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, for 90 days after ruling that the pair had breached the terms of the former leader's house arrest.
evidence.source_title: Brazil court bars Bolsonaro's son from visiting ex-president for 90 days - Al Jazeera

evidence.claim: Flávio Bolsonaro filed an impeachment request in the Senate against Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes, accusing him of bias in the coup case and of political activity incompatible with his office, and asked that Moraes be barred from public office for eight years if removed.
evidence.quote: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (Liberal Party–Rio de Janeiro) filed an impeachment request against Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes after the judge stepped up restrictions on his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, imposing new precautionary measures.
evidence.source_title: Brazilian senator files to impeach top court justice amid crackdown - Valor International

evidence.claim: In May 2026, Flávio Bolsonaro publicly accused The Intercept Brasil, without presenting evidence, of links to organised crime, during a campaign event. Days later, after a freelance reporter visited his brother Eduardo's Texas home, Eduardo publicly accused the reporter of ties to an organised crime group and suggested he could encounter armed civilians; the reporter's photos and personal information were then shared online and he was harassed on X by supporters.
evidence.quote: On May 16, during a campaign event for Congressman Guilherme Derrite, Flávio Bolsonaro publicly accused The Intercept Brasil, without presenting evidence, of having links to organised crime.
evidence.source_title: RSF condemns attacks and threats against The Intercept Brasil after its investigation involving presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro - RSF

evidence.claim: Press freedom group RSF says the doxxing and online harassment of Intercept Brasil staff followed the outlet's investigations into Flávio Bolsonaro; RSF states that publicly exposing journalists and encouraging hostile narratives fuels intimidation.
evidence.quote: Reporters Without Borders (RSF) condemns the doxxing and severe cyber harassment targeting the staff of investigative news site The Intercept Brasil following recent investigations into Senator Flávio Bolsonaro
evidence.source_title: RSF condemns attacks and threats against The Intercept Brasil - RSF

evidence.claim: CPJ reported harassment and threats against Intercept Brasil reporters linked to Bolsonaro family coverage; the Brazilian Association of Investigative Journalism and the National Federation of Journalists published letters repudiating Flávio Bolsonaro's harassment against Intercept Brasil. A Flávio ally, Congressman Hélio Lopes, asked the Supreme Court and TSE to open a criminal investigation into the outlet's reporting.
evidence.quote: The Brazilian Association of Investigative Journalism and the National Federation of Journalists published letters repudiating Flávio Bolsonaro's harassment against Intercept Brasil.
evidence.source_title: Intercept Brasil reporters face harassment, threats - CPJ

evidence.claim: Flávio Bolsonaro is under Supreme Court investigation (opened by Justice André Mendonça at Federal Police request) for alleged corruption and money laundering tied to receiving about 61 million reais from banker Daniel Vorcaro for the film 'Dark Horse'; the investigation is an allegation not yet resolved in court.
evidence.quote: Brazilian presidential candidate Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro is under investigation for corruption, money laundering and tax evasion for receiving millions of dollars from a disgraced banker to finance a movie about his father
evidence.source_title: Flávio Bolsonaro investigated over payments from disgraced Brazilian banker - AP News

evidence.claim: Flávio Bolsonaro publicly backed a Senate-led impeachment push against Supreme Court justices; his campaign manager Rogério Marinho told Chief Justice Fachin on 6 October 2026 that the Senate 'will not stay silent' on impeachable offences by justices. Flávio said in an interview that Moraes had pursued 'adversaries he predetermined' and that he is pursuing impeachment for political-party activity.
evidence.quote: “When a Supreme Court justice commits a crime of responsibility, the Senate will not stay silent,” Marinho said
evidence.source_title: Brazil Bolsonaro Allies Warn Supreme Court on 6 October - The Rio Times

evidence.claim: Ex-assessors of Flávio Bolsonaro in the Alerj (Rio state assembly) withdrew at least R$ 7.2 million in cash, about 60% of what they received from public funds, per the MP-RJ investigation; prosecutors suspected a 'rachadinha' salary-kickback scheme and 'ghost' employees. Calculation covers 24 ex-staff, excluding Fabrício Queiroz. Flávio and Queiroz's defenses denied wrongdoing.
evidence.quote: Ex-assessores do senador Flávio Bolsonaro (Republicanos-RJ) investigados pelo Ministério Público do Rio (MP-RJ) sacaram, em dinheiro vivo, pelo menos R$ 7,2 milhões. O valor sacado em espécie corresponde a 60% do que os servidores receberam dos cofres públicos fluminenses
evidence.source_title: Ex-assessores de Flávio sacaram ao menos R$ 7,2 milhões - Estadão

evidence.claim: A former Alerj aide said he returned about R$ 340,000 to Ana Cristina Valle (Bolsonaro's then-wife), that the practice was a condition for keeping the job, and that the money was withdrawn and handed over in cash. This is an allegation by a witness, not a court finding.
evidence.quote: devolveu, ao todo, cerca de R$ 340 mil, e que a prática era condição para a manutenção do emprego. Os valores, segundo ele, eram sacados e repassados em espécie.
evidence.source_title: Ex-assessor de Flávio na Alerj diz a site que devolvia 80% do salário para então mulher de Bolsonaro - O Globo

evidence.claim: MP-RJ denounced Flávio Bolsonaro for money laundering, concealment of assets, peculato, and criminal organization tied to the Alerj rachadinha scheme; the Coaf reports showed at least R$ 2.7 million moved by Flávio from staff who mostly did not work in the office, per prosecutors.
evidence.quote: no mínimo 2,7 milhões de reais foram movimentados por Flávio a partir de funcionários que, em sua maioria, não exerciam suas atividades no gabinete ou sequer davam expediente da Assembleia do Rio
evidence.source_title: Flávio Bolsonaro é denunciado por lavagem de dinheiro e organização criminosa no caso da 'rachadinha' - El País

evidence.claim: Prosecutors alleged the Kopenhagen chocolate franchise co-owned by Flávio Bolsonaro (Bolsotini) was used to launder roughly R$ 1.6 million to R$ 2.1 million of money diverted from the Alerj rachadinha scheme, including cash deposits and fake invoices; the case was closed without merits judgment due to annulled evidence and statute of limitations.
evidence.quote: A investigação aponta que a lavagem desses recursos era feita por meio de uma franquia de loja de chocolate, da qual Flávio é sócio. Passaram por ali quase R$ 1,6 milhão, segundo os investigadores.
evidence.source_title: O que há de concreto contra Flávio Bolsonaro, segundo investigadores - BBC News Brasil

evidence.claim: A former franchise seller (Cristiano Corrêa Souza) told prosecutors that under Bolsonaro's company the Kopenhagen franchise falsified invoices and sold items below officially recorded prices.
evidence.quote: Cristiano Corrêa Souza, que vendeu o negócio ao político, afirmou ao MP que, sob a gestão da Bolsotini, a franquia fraudava notas fiscais e vendia itens por preços inferiores aos registrados oficialmente.
evidence.source_title: Alvo de investigação das 'rachadinhas', loja de Flávio Bolsonaro no Rio é vendida - O Globo

evidence.claim: Flávio Bolsonaro, as a senator, introduced a 2019 bill to exempt rural producers from the obligation to keep a legal reserve (reserva legal) on their land; the bill was later withdrawn and archived.
evidence.quote: Em abril de 2019, por exemplo, Flávio aproveitou seus primeiros meses no Senado para apresentar um projeto de lei que eximia os produtores rurais da obrigação de manter uma reserva legal em suas propriedades.
evidence.source_title: Passagem de Flávio Bolsonaro pelo Senado é marcada por pautas antiambientais - Observatório do Clima

evidence.claim: Flávio Bolsonaro voted in favor of PL 2159/2021 (the 'PL da Devastação' weakening environmental licensing), voted to include fossil gas projects in Fundo Clima financing, voted to write the marco temporal into the Constitution restricting Indigenous land recognition, and voted to reduce environmental enforcement duties, overriding a Lula veto; reported by Observatório do Clima as part of at least 17 anti-environmental initiatives.
evidence.quote: Flávio Bolsonaro votou a favor do projeto de lei 2159/2021 – o famoso PL da Devastação -, contribuindo para o enfraquecimento da política do licenciamento ambiental. Também votou a favor de: (1) tornar projetos que incluem gás natural fóssil elegíveis ao financiamento do Fundo Clima
evidence.source_title: Passagem de Flávio Bolsonaro pelo Senado é marcada por pautas antiambientais - Observatório do Clima

evidence.claim: Flávio Bolsonaro filed a November 2025 amendment to an income-tax bill that would have excluded from withholding the profits and dividends paid by professional-services companies, which could have benefited his own sole-proprietor law practice.
evidence.quote: O senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) apresentou, em novembro de 2025, uma emenda a um projeto que alterava as regras do Imposto de Renda para excluir da nova tributação lucros e dividendos distribuídos por sociedades de prestação de serviços profissionais. A mudança poderia beneficiar o próprio parlamentar, que mantém uma sociedade individual de advocacia.
evidence.source_title: Mudança proposta por Flávio Bolsonaro no Imposto de Renda poderia beneficiar escritório do senador

evidence.claim: Flávio Bolsonaro's law firm (a sole-proprietor society) issued at least R$ 13.7 million in invoices between January 2023 and July 2026; half of the invoices were issued for payment by other lawyers, and its largest client is a law firm whose partner was appointed by Jair Bolsonaro to the Public Ethics Commission. The firm says contracts were for legitimate private legal consulting.
evidence.quote: O escritório de advocacia do senador e candidato à Presidência Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) emitiu ao menos R$ 13,7 milhões em notas fiscais entre janeiro de 2023 e julho de 2026. Metade dessas notas foi emitida para pagamento por outros advogados.
evidence.source_title: Escritório de Flávio faturou R$ 14 mi enquanto ele exercia cargo de senador - UOL/TAB

evidence.claim: Rio de Janeiro prosecutors (MP-RJ) charged Flávio Bolsonaro in 2020 with leading a criminal organization that diverted part of salaries of staff in his state legislative office (rachadinha), alongside charges of peculato, money laundering, concealment and related crimes. Status: charge (denúncia) only; the Rio court later rejected it, so no conviction. Allegation, denied by Flávio.
evidence.quote: The charges against Flávio Bolsonaro stem from a series of suspicious financial transactions involving staff members at his former legislative office in the Rio de Janeiro State Assembly.
evidence.source_title: Bolsonaro's Eldest Son, a Senator, Faces Graft Charges in Brazil - The New York Times

evidence.claim: Rio state prosecutors alleged that Fabrício Queiroz, Flávio's former aide, ran a scheme with phantom employees in Flávio's office, with part of salaries diverted and laundered through a chocolate shop franchise and two flats. Allegation; Flávio denied wrongdoing. Queiroz was arrested in August 2020 at the home of Flávio's lawyer.
evidence.quote: State prosecutors say 54-year-old Mr Queiroz - a former policeman and ex-driver to Flávio - ran a scheme involving phantom employees in Flávio's office. They allege that part of the salaries was diverted, with the proceeds being laundered through a chocolate shop franchise and two flats.
evidence.source_title: Brazil corruption: Police arrest ex-aide to Jair Bolsonaro's son Flávio

evidence.claim: Brazil's Financial Intelligence Unit (COAF) reported in December 2018 suspicious transactions of about R$1.2 million in an account of Fabrício Queiroz between 2016 and 2017, when Flávio was a Rio state deputy. This is the origin of the case; the COAF reports were later partly annulled.
evidence.quote: Brazilian authorities identified 1.2m reais (£180,000; $220,000 in current figures) in bank transactions in an account belonging to Mr Queiroz between 2016 and 2017, when Flávio Bolsonaro was a Rio state lawmaker.
evidence.source_title: Brazil corruption: Police arrest ex-aide to Jair Bolsonaro's son Flávio

evidence.claim: Federal Police are reported to have obtained documents indicating that Flávio Bolsonaro sought funding from jailed banker Daniel Vorcaro (Banco Master) for the film 'Dark Horse' about his father; reported messages show him asking for about US$24 million (R$134 million). Allegation under investigation; Flávio says the money was private sponsorship and denies wrongdoing.
evidence.quote: Leaked messages published by The Intercept Brasil on 13 May 2026 show Senator Flávio Bolsonaro asked Banco Master owner Daniel Vorcaro for US$24 million (about R$134 million) to finance “Dark Horse,” a biopic about his father, Jair Bolsonaro.
evidence.source_title: Flavio Bolsonaro Banco Master Loan 2026: The $24M Ask - Rio Times

evidence.claim: Investigation (unproven) by Supreme Court Justice André Mendonça, opened July 2026 at the request of the Federal Police, into whether Flávio committed corruption, money laundering, illicit foreign exchange and tax evasion linked to about R$61 million transferred by Vorcaro in 2025 toward the film. Status: investigation opened, no charge; Flávio denies any wrongdoing.
evidence.quote: Supreme Court Justice Andre Mendonca, a Bolsonaro appointee, opened the investigation in July at the request of federal police, but the case remained sealed until Chief Justice Luiz Edson Fachin ordered it made public this week, Reuters reported.
evidence.source_title: Flavio Bolsonaro faces graft probe weeks before Brazil vote - DW

evidence.claim: Federal Police found that about R$61 million was transferred by Vorcaro at Flávio's request toward a Texas fund; investigators are examining whether part of the funds financed Eduardo Bolsonaro's US legal defense. Allegation under investigation, no charge; Eduardo and the film company deny wrongdoing.
evidence.quote: Brazil’s Federal Police suspect that funds transferred by former banker Daniel Vorcaro to a holding company at the request of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (Liberal Party, Rio de Janeiro) may have helped finance the life of the senator’s brother, former congressman Eduardo Bolsonaro, in the United States.
evidence.source_title: Police trace Vorcaro funds in Bolsonaro film probe - Valor International

evidence.claim: A second Federal Police inquiry (reported Oct 2026, referred to STF, assigned to Justice Moraes) examines alleged money laundering involving Flávio and lawyer Willer Tomaz, linked to sports-betting companies; one account tied to Tomaz moved about R$130 million March–May 2025. Unproven allegation; police suspicion, no court ruling; Flávio and Tomaz deny irregularity.
evidence.quote: One account linked to Tomaz moved about R$130 million (about US$25.7 million) from March to May 2025, and the police say the origin and destination of the funds need a closer look.
evidence.source_title: Flávio Bolsonaro Laundering Probe Denied Before Runoff - Rio Times

evidence.claim: Federal Police are examining a R$3.1 million loan from state bank BRB that helped Flávio buy a Brasília mansion in 2021; the loan was paid off in about three years. Allegation under police examination; no finding. Flávio said he acquired the property 'through work'.
evidence.quote: Brazil’s Federal Police are examining the BRB loan that helped Senator Flávio Bolsonaro buy a mansion in Brasília in 2021.
evidence.source_title: Brazil Police Probe Loan for Flávio Bolsonaro Mansion - Rio Times

evidence.claim: Flávio's declared assets rose to R$8.1-8.2 million in his 2026 presidential candidacy registration, up from R$1.74 million in 2018; the increase is attributed partly to a 2021 Lago Sul property purchase. Declared figures, not a finding of wrongdoing.
evidence.quote: When registering his presidential candidacy in 2026, the far-right politician declared total assets of 8.18 million reais, an increase of 6.44 million reais compared with the 1.74 million reais he declared in 2018.
evidence.source_title: Lula Offers to Lift Bank Secrecy as Bolsonaro's Wealth Faces Scrutiny - teleSUR English

evidence.claim: In April 2026 the Supreme Court ordered a probe into Flávio for alleged slander of President Lula over a January 3 social-media post linking Lula to drug trafficking and money laundering, at the request of the justice ministry. Investigation; no finding.
evidence.quote: The Supreme Court said Justice Alexandre de Moraes ordered the investigation at the request of the justice ministry, which deemed that Flavio Bolsonaro "falsely, publicly, and disparagingly attributed criminal acts to the President of the Republic."
evidence.source_title: Brazil Supreme Court orders probe into Flavio Bolsonaro for 'slander' of Lula - France 24

people.name: Javier Milei
notes: power backfilled from hand-entered reach and authority, not from a research run
people.summary:
Javier Milei, President of Argentina, receives a harm tier of "major" (score 0.73; coverage and confidence 1.00). Benefit tier is "none_documented": no benefit evidence was found or rated. This is not a negative finding, and the harm and benefit profiles are reported separately.

The main reasons for the harm tier, in order of weight:

1. Environmental policy (severity 3). Environmental agency budgets were cut by up to 84.5% [R1-E04, https://theenergypioneer.com/argentinas-environmental-budget-slashed-under-president-javier-milei]. Congress approved a glacier-law change in April 2026 that allows mining in glacial and periglacial areas [R1-E05, https://apnews.com/article/milei-glacier-bill-argentina-environment-climate-change-27d4f5638c148f0b10690cf3114309f5]. The government also withdrew its delegation from COP29 [R1-E02, https://www.batimes.com.ar/news/world/milei-pulls-argentinas-delegation-from-cop29-climate-conference.phtml].

2. Press freedom (severity 3). Press credentials were revoked for several outlets in April 2026 [R2-E10, https://latamjournalismreview.org/news/argentine-government-revokes-credentials-of-media-outlets-accused-of-disinformation-campaign]. Milei filed defamation complaints against journalists [R2-E06, https://buenosairesherald.com/human-rights/president-milei-sues-three-journalists-for-defamation]. He called media workers "traitors to the nation" [R2-E04, https://courthousenews.com/we-dont-hate-journalists-enough-milei-escalates-attacks-on-argentine-press-with-lawsuits-and-bans].

3. Labor and economic measures (severity 3). Labor Law 27.802 cuts severance costs and limits strike action, and courts have suspended parts of it [R3-E03, https://www.riotimesonline.com/argentina-labor-reform-severance-court-unconstitutional-2026]. Household loan delinquency reached 12.8% in June 2026 [R3-E12, https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/more-argentines-turn-apps-loans-debt-stress-hits-record-2026-09-04].

Corruption-related allegations scored zero. The $LIBRA matter remains an allegation under investigation, and no charges against Milei have been filed [R4-E01, https://apnews.com/article/argentina-milei-cryptocurrency-fraud-charges-3f572a5f294d7c25437a08151798b917].

evidence.claim: Milei called the climate crisis a 'socialist lie' and pledged to withdraw Argentina from the Paris agreement; in an interview with Le Point he said he was considering quitting the Paris pact 'because I do not adhere to the environmentalist agenda'.
evidence.quote: Earlier this month, right-wing populist leader Milei told French news magazine Le Point he was considering quitting the Paris pact "because I do not adhere to the environmentalist agenda".
evidence.source_title: Risk of financial fallout may deter Argentina from leaving Paris Agreement

evidence.claim: Milei's government ordered the Argentine delegation to withdraw from the COP29 climate summit in Baku in November 2024; the government said it was tied to rejection of the UN 2030 Agenda.
evidence.quote: President Javier Milei government's on Wednesday ordered the entire Argentine delegation to withdraw from the ongoing COP29 climate change conference in Azerbaijan.
