evidence.source_title: Milei pulls Argentina's delegation from COP29 climate conference

evidence.claim: Milei's administration downgraded the environment ministry to a sub-secretariat, moved it under the Chief of Staff, and in April 2026 dissolved the national climate directorates.
evidence.quote: The former Ministry of Environment was downgraded to a sub‑secretariat, later moved under the Chief of Staff's office, and eventually stripped of key technical bodies. In April 2026, the government dissolved both the National Directorate for Sustainable Development and Climate Management and the Directorate for Climate Impact
evidence.source_title: Argentina | Climate Action Tracker

evidence.claim: Milei's government cut federal environmental agency budgets by up to 84.5% and the Climate Change Department was removed from the environment portfolio's structure.
evidence.quote: Since taking office, President Milei's administration has cut up to 84.5% of federal environmental agency budgets, undermining wildfire response, forest conservation, and renewable energy projects
evidence.source_title: Argentina's Environmental Budget Slashed Under President Javier Milei

evidence.claim: Milei sent a bill to Congress loosening glacier protections to allow mining in glacial and periglacial areas; Congress approved it in April 2026 (137-111), with the government arguing it unlocks mining investment.
evidence.quote: The legislation, approved by the Senate in February, was passed with 137 votes in favor, 111 against and three abstentions.
evidence.source_title: Argentina's Congress approves bill easing glacier protections for mining

evidence.claim: Milei backed the glacier law reform, which shifts responsibility for defining protected glacier areas to provincial governments; he said it allows mining where 'there was nothing to protect'.
evidence.quote: President Javier Milei, who backed the reform, said the change "empower[s] the provinces to utilise their resources" and allows mining activities "where there was nothing to protect".
evidence.source_title: Argentina passes bill loosening protection of its glaciers

evidence.claim: Milei's government promoted expansion of Vaca Muerta oil and gas, extended the RIGI investment regime with 30-year tax breaks to shale oil wells, and touted record output growth (310,000 to 670,000 bpd).
evidence.quote: President Javier Milei's marquee program for luring investment into Argentina is poised to attract a new round of applications from crude producers after his administration broadened it to include shale oil wells.
evidence.source_title: Argentina expands incentives to spur Vaca Muerta shale oil investment

evidence.claim: Milei told the UN General Assembly that climate-related agendas were an ideological imposition and called the 'woke agenda' a failure; he sought to distance Argentina from the UN 2030 Agenda.
evidence.quote: During the UN General Assembly in September, he accused the global body of trying to "impose an ideological agenda" and sought to distance Argentina from the UN-sponsored 2030 Sustainable Development Agenda.
evidence.source_title: Argentina withdraws delegates from climate summit as Milei heads for Mar-a-Lago

evidence.claim: Milei publicly promised tech firms that Argentina would keep AI 'unregulated' and proposed a legal framework for AI agents/AI-run companies with minimal regulation.
evidence.quote: President Javier Milei promised the world's tech firms on Thursday that Argentina will create a special legal framework to foster the development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Argentina, reaffirming his commitment to keeping the sector "unregulated."
evidence.source_title: Milei promises tech firms new laws and 'unregulated' AI in Argentina

evidence.claim: Milei's government bought 24 used F-16 fighters from Denmark (about US$301 million), a purchase the government called its most important military acquisition; it later classified the purchase and related exports as state military secrets.
evidence.quote: Decree 370, signed on 26 April 2024, classified the contract to buy the jets.
evidence.source_title: Milei Widens Argentina F-16 Secrecy on Exported Parts

evidence.claim: Milei's government signed a decree classifying a weapons acquisition plan as a state military secret, with suppliers and costs designated confidential.
evidence.quote: The decree classified the procurement plan as a state military secret, with contract details, weapon types, costs, suppliers, and recipient departments designated as "absolutely confidential."
evidence.source_title: Argentina's President Milei Signs Decree to Classify Latest Military Weapon Purchase on October 19

evidence.claim: Milei's government deployed AI-driven surveillance infrastructure, which Amnesty International described as a techno-authoritarian infrastructure of social control.
evidence.quote: Amnesty International on Wednesday released a report detailing how the Argentine government under the leadership of right-wing President Javier Milei has created a massive artificial intelligence surveillance state that the human rights group described as "a techno-authoritarian infrastructure of social control."
evidence.source_title: Amnesty Warns of Right-Wing Argentinian Government's AI-Driven Surveillance State

evidence.claim: Argentina's Security ministry authorized AI for predictive policing, facial recognition comparison and drone surveillance via Resolution 710/2024.
evidence.quote: In public security, Resolution 710/2024 authorizes the UIAAS to utilize AI technologies for crime prevention, predictive analytics based on historical crime data, automated open-source cyber patrols, dark web monitoring, real-time CCTV video analysis, facial recognition comparison, and drone surveillance
evidence.source_title: Argentina AI Regulation Overview | Regulations.AI

evidence.claim: Milei's X account posted 1,674 posts attacking journalists and the media over 47 days (April–May 2026), of which 1,499 were reposts; RSF counted 498 posts accusing journalists of corruption. He regularly insulted journalists as 'disgusting trash'.
evidence.quote: RSF analysed Javier Milei’s X account between April and May 2026 and found that in 47 days, Argentina’s head of state posted 1,674 posts attacking journalists and the media, including reposts
evidence.source_title: Argentina: Javier Milei posts more than 35 anti-media hate messages on X per day | RSF

evidence.claim: FOPEA analysis of 113,649 Milei X posts (Dec 2023–Sep 2025) found he repeatedly referred to journalists as 'criminals', 'corrupt', 'apes' and 'terrorists'; rhetoric recorded with follow-up of record press-aggression counts and a Milei-linked share of stigmatizing discourse.
evidence.quote: FOPEA scrapped 113,649 posts from Milei’s X account from December 2023 to September 2025 and found that the president frequently referred to journalists as “criminals,” “corrupt,” “apes,” and “terrorists.”
evidence.source_title: Argentinian journalism stifled by President Milei’s public attacks, government repression | CPJ

evidence.claim: Milei's rhetoric against the press was followed by 2025 record levels of FOPEA-recorded attacks; FOPEA reported Milei was connected to 43% of stigmatizing-discourse attacks.
evidence.quote: Last year, FOPEA reported that Milei was connected to 43% of attacks in the form of stigmatizing discourse, offenses and insults.
evidence.source_title: Argentinian journalism stifled by President Milei’s public attacks, government repression | CPJ

evidence.claim: Milei called media workers 'traitors to the nation', 'filthy garbage' and 'imbeciles' on social media; La Nación recorded over 1,000 insults aimed at journalists during Easter weekend.
evidence.quote: La Nación, a prominent national newspaper, recorded over 1,000 insults aimed at journalists on Milei’s social media during Easter weekend alone. He called media workers “traitors to the nation,” “filthy garbage” and “imbeciles,”
evidence.source_title: 'We don't hate journalists enough': Milei escalates attacks on Argentine press with lawsuits and bans | Courthouse News Service

evidence.claim: Milei shared on social media a post asking that the press be designated a terrorist organization, and wrote 86 posts insulting journalists in four days (April 2–5, 2026), re-sharing 874 such attacks.
evidence.quote: Over just four days this month, Milei, an avid user of X, wrote 86 posts taunting and insulting journalists, according to an analysis of his feed between April 2 and 5 by prominent Argentine daily La Nación. He re-shared 874 such attacks in that time, including one post asking that he designate the press a terrorist organization
evidence.source_title: Argentine president's journalist ban raises concerns about press freedom | AP News

evidence.claim: Milei filed personal criminal defamation/slander complaints against journalists Carlos Pagni, Viviana Canosa and Ari Lijalad (May 2025); Lijalad said the complaint was for a column stating Milei 'rules by inciting violence and hatred'. Federal judges later dismissed the complaints against Pagni and Lijalad.
evidence.quote: Milei filed a complaint against him for a column in which he wrote that the president “rules by inciting violence and hatred against those who think differently.”
evidence.source_title: President Milei sues three journalists for defamation - Buenos Aires Herald

evidence.claim: Milei has filed defamation lawsuits against at least eight journalists in the last year and encouraged allies to do the same; FOPEA counted civil or criminal legal actions against journalists and media rising from 11 in 2024 to 30 in 2025.
evidence.quote: Milei has turned to the courts, filing defamation lawsuits against at least eight journalists in the last year and encouraging his allies to do the same.
evidence.source_title: Argentine president's journalist ban raises concerns about press freedom | AP News

evidence.claim: Milei shared a deepfake video depicting journalist Julia Mengolini in a sexual act; Milei filed a criminal defamation complaint against Mengolini on 1 July 2025.
evidence.quote: including an incident in which President Javier Milei shared a deepfake video depicting her in a sexual act.
evidence.source_title: Argentinian journalism stifled by President Milei’s public attacks, government repression | CPJ

evidence.claim: Government removed press accreditation/access for ~60 Casa Rosada correspondents in March–April 2026, after a complaint by the Military Household over alleged espionage by TN journalists; the government later restored access but kept some restrictions and denied entry to two TV channels.
evidence.quote: As his government pulled press credentials from the roughly 60 reporters covering the Casa Rosada on Thursday, Milei fired off posts
evidence.source_title: Argentina's leader bars journalists from government HQ, raising concerns about press freedom | LA Times

evidence.claim: On April 6, 2026 the government revoked press credentials for access to the Executive HQ and Congress for outlets including Ámbito Financiero, C5N, El Destape, Tiempo Argentino and A24, after they were implicated in an alleged Russian-linked disinformation campaign exposed by journalists.
evidence.quote: The government of Argentine President Javier Milei revoked on Monday [April 6] the press credentials granting access to the Executive headquarters and Congress for certain local media outlets implicated in an alleged disinformation campaign
evidence.source_title: Argentine government revokes credentials of media outlets accused of disinformation campaign | LatAm Journalism Review

evidence.claim: Government inaugurated an 'Agency/Office for Official Response' to fact-check and 'debunk' critical reporting, mostly on social media.
evidence.quote: Recently, the government inaugurated an office to “fact-check” critical media called “Agency for Official Response,” aimed at “debunking” critical reporting, mostly on social media.
evidence.source_title: 'We don't hate journalists enough': Milei escalates attacks on Argentine press with lawsuits and bans | Courthouse News Service

evidence.claim: Police fired a tear gas canister that struck freelance photojournalist Pablo Grillo in the head at a retirees' protest on 12 March 2025, causing severe brain injury; HRW verified video showing a National Gendarmerie member firing the cartridge at him. Security Minister Bullrich said the government would not investigate security forces' role and praised them.
evidence.quote: The videos and photographs show that a member of the National Gendarmerie fired a tear gas cartridge at Pablo Grillo, a freelance journalist, at 5:17 p.m.
evidence.source_title: Argentina: Abusive Response to Protest | Human Rights Watch

evidence.claim: After the protest, Security Minister Bullrich said the administration would not investigate security forces' role and praised them; the Milei protocol lifted restrictions on tear gas guns for police.
evidence.quote: Following the protest, Security Minister Bullrich said that the administration of President Javier Milei would not investigate security forces’ role in the March 12 protest, and praised them for “protecting democracy, institutions, and citizens.”
evidence.source_title: Argentina: Abusive Response to Protest | Human Rights Watch

evidence.claim: The corporal who fired the tear gas canister that struck Grillo was prosecuted for not following security protocol; his assets were seized and he must report periodically, but was not imprisoned. Grillo's family sought attempted-murder charges.
evidence.quote: The corporal who fired the tear gas canister who struck Grillo in the head was prosecuted for not following security protocol; his assets were seized; he must report periodically to the police, and cannot leave the country; but he was not imprisoned.
evidence.source_title: Argentinian journalism stifled by President Milei’s public attacks, government repression | CPJ

evidence.claim: Milei's government reduced government advertising to media (boasted of cutting media support) and announced a selection system for journalists at Casa Rosada press conferences, including a public vote on access and ability to mute reporters' microphones.
evidence.quote: would involve a public vote on which journalists are allowed access and the ability to mute certain journalists’ microphones
evidence.source_title: Argentina: RSF condemns police violence against photojournalist Pablo Grillo, hospitalised in critical condition | RSF

evidence.claim: Government decree (Decree 941/2025, published Jan 2, 2026) reshaped the SIDE intelligence services and expanded its powers as central intelligence authority; critics raised overreach fears. Milei has changed the intelligence chief more than any president since 1983.
evidence.quote: Changes formalised by Decree 941/2025, published in the Official Gazette on January 2, redefine the functioning of the SIDE intelligence services, reduce its internal structure and expand its powers as the central authority for intelligence.
evidence.source_title: Milei decree reshapes SIDE intelligence services, rekindling overreach fears | Buenos Aires Times

evidence.claim: A federal judge declared unconstitutional Decree 759/2025 that halted university funding law, ordering immediate application; the law had survived Milei's veto after Congress reaffirmed it with two-thirds majorities (cut against: government complied subject to court ruling, litigation).
evidence.quote: Judge Martín Cormick, of Federal Administrative Litigation Court No. 11, ruled last Tuesday that an emergency decree issued by President Milei (Decree 759/2025) was “unconstitutional” because it conditioned the implementation of the University Financing Law.
evidence.source_title: Court declares Milei decree halting university funding 'unconstitutional' | Buenos Aires Times

evidence.claim: Milei ordered dismissal of Argentina's foreign intelligence agency (FIA/AFI) based on an internal audit, replacing it with new agencies.
evidence.quote: "President Javier Milei ordered to dismiss the FIA based on the results of the internal audit, which started on December 12, 2023.
evidence.source_title: President of Argentina dismisses intelligence agency | TASS

evidence.claim: Lijalad reports the government filed a civil and a criminal case against him over comparing Milei's speech to Nazism; he says lawsuits aim to intimidate reporters.
evidence.quote: Ari Lijalad, a reporter who has been repeatedly sued by the government, is still struggling with a civil and a criminal case from the president for comparing his speech to Nazism.
evidence.source_title: 'We don't hate journalists enough': Milei escalates attacks on Argentine press with lawsuits and bans | Courthouse News Service

evidence.claim: Milei's government revoked on Monday 6 April 2026 the press credentials for certain outlets; SiPreBA said the government was 'attempting to silence critical journalism'.
evidence.quote: ‘Just as we warned, the government is attempting to silence critical journalism and is denying entry to several accredited journalists,’
evidence.source_title: Argentine government revokes credentials of media outlets accused of disinformation campaign | LatAm Journalism Review

evidence.claim: Pro-Milei online accounts were reported to harass critics of the president online; in 2023 supporters spread coordinated electoral fraud claims without evidence (not Milei's own act as recorded here).
evidence.quote: Since President Milei took office, reports have documented the existence of social media accounts that fiercely support his government and La Libertad Avanza, potentially constituting “a deliberately planned hierarchical action.”
evidence.source_title: Argentina: Freedom on the Net 2024 Country Report | Freedom House

evidence.claim: Milei called journalists 'disgusting scum' and 'corrupt junkies hooked on advertising bucks and bribes' after the Casa Rosada credential removal.
evidence.quote: “Oh I forgot, you lot are corrupt junkies hooked on advertising bucks and bribes.”
evidence.source_title: Argentine president's journalist ban raises concerns about press freedom | AP News

evidence.claim: Milei signed DNU 70/2023 (Dec 20, 2023) which included labor deregulation: raised probation from 3 to 8 months, reduced severance, allowed dismissal of workers taking part in some protest blockades, and restricted the right to strike. A labor court suspended the labor title in January 2024 and a three-judge panel later ruled it unconstitutional.
evidence.quote: Milei's decree announced in December established several changes in labor rules, including increasing job probation from three to eight months, reducing severance compensation and allowing the possibility of dismissal for workers taking part in blockades during some protests.
evidence.source_title: Argentine court suspends labor changes in a blow to President Milei's economic plan | Courthouse News Service

evidence.claim: Labor court found the labor-reform decree's provisions (Title IV) unjustified as an emergency decree; the labor section also restricted the right to strike and eliminated sanctions for irregular labor.
evidence.quote: Title IV also restricted the right to strike, eliminated sanctions for irregular labor
evidence.source_title: Argentine justice system halts President Javier Milei's labor reforms | EL PAÍS English

evidence.claim: Congressional Labor Modernization Law 27.802, promoted by Milei, was passed in February 2026 and published 6 March 2026; it cuts severance costs, extends working-day flexibility and limits strike action. Courts have since suspended parts of it; an appeals court declared it constitutional as a whole (April 2026) and a later ruling struck article 55 capping severance inflation-updating at 67%.
evidence.quote: It is Milei's Labour Modernisation Law, passed on 27 February 2026 and in force since 6 March. It cuts severance costs, extends working-day flexibility and limits strike action.
evidence.source_title: Argentina's Labour Reform Loses in court (Rio Times)

evidence.claim: The labor reform extends the maximum working day from 8 to 12 hours, reduces union power and cuts severance pay (as described by Buenos Aires Herald).
evidence.quote: Among the modifications, the reform reduces the power of unions, cuts severance pay, and extends the maximum working day from 8 to 12 hours.
evidence.source_title: Federal court temporarily suspends most of Milei's labor reform | Buenos Aires Herald

evidence.claim: Labor reform bill includes a 'dynamic wage' subordinating part of worker pay to employer assessments of firm productivity and financial situation; critics classify it as precarious employment. Decree 407/2026 orders review of ~150 expired collective bargaining agreements, removes automatic ultra-activity protection and lowers the threshold to challenge union representation from 20% to 5%.
evidence.quote: Key changes include revising the ultra-activity principle (removing automatic protection for expired pacts) and lowering the threshold to challenge union representation from 20% to 5%.
evidence.source_title: Milei intensifies his attacks on labour rights in Argentina | Progressive International

evidence.claim: Labor reform's severance changes lower employer costs: the reform streamlines severance calculation by excluding bonuses not part of a worker's regular pay; a pre-funded Labor Assistance Fund is created to which employers contribute monthly (1% for large companies, 2.5% for SMEs).
evidence.quote: The reform streamlines the calculation of severance pay, lowering costs for employers by excluding bonuses that were not part of a worker's
evidence.source_title: Argentina Senate passes Milei labor reform, advancing pro-market overhaul

evidence.claim: Business groups pushed the labor reform to reduce labor costs; business chambers said lawsuits, high labor taxes and rigid rules were the problem.
evidence.quote: Business groups support push to reduce labor costs, Business chambers say those lawsuits, combined with high labor taxes and rigid rules, have
evidence.source_title: Milei's labor reform drive sets up clash with Argentina unions

evidence.claim: Milei's government pushed a Glacier Law reform allowing provinces to define glacier protections, opening ecologically sensitive periglacial areas to mining; Congress approved it in April 2026 over environmental protests. Critics say it weakens water protections for regions relying on glacier meltwater.
evidence.quote: authorises mining in ecologically sensitive areas of glaciers and permafrost, a move that has outraged environmentalists.
evidence.source_title: Argentina MPs approve bill allowing mining in glaciers | Al Jazeera

evidence.claim: Under the glacier reform, the Milei government argued the change would attract large-scale mining; critics warned that shifting authority to provinces could let mining expand into areas connected to glacier-fed water sources.
evidence.quote: Critics, however, warn that shifting authority to the provinces could make it easier for mining to expand into areas connected to glacier-fed [...] Environmental groups and other critics have challenged the changes
evidence.source_title: Argentina Bill Rewinds Glacier Protections | Center for Latin American Studies

evidence.claim: Government reduced energy subsidies: households receiving electricity subsidies fell by 2.1 million and piped gas by 900,000 since December 2023; government says it saved US$5.6 billion; nearly half of households now pay full cost; collection rates rose from 48% to ~97%.
evidence.quote: Currently, 2.1 million fewer households receive support for electricity and 900,000 fewer for piped natural gas compared with the start of the administration, according to government data. The number of users paying the full cost is now close to half of the total.
evidence.source_title: Milei's 'chainsaw' slashes energy subsidies for three million households | Buenos Aires Times

evidence.claim: Household and personal credit distress rose sharply under Milei's financial deregulation; fintech loans (e.g., Mercado Pago) carry much higher rates than bank loans; arrears rose from 4.2% (end 2023) to 17.5% (August 2026). Milei attributed rising delinquency to people buying TVs for the World Cup.
evidence.quote: Under Milei, financial deregulation has led to higher credit costs and increased rates of debt distress. Although personal loan rates from traditional banks have fallen, increasing numbers of Argentines are relying on fintech companies like Mercado Pago, where rates are significantly higher. Between the end of 2023 and August 2026, the percentage of Argentines in arrears ballooned from 4.2% to 17.5%.
evidence.source_title: Millions of Argentines face debt trap amid deregulation, rising costs | Courthouse News Service

evidence.claim: Household loan delinquency reached 12.8% in June 2026, the highest since records began in 2010; at non-bank lenders such as fintechs and digital wallets delinquency exceeded 32%. The government has said the issue is a matter between banks and borrowers.
evidence.quote: The ratio of bad loans among households rose to 12.8% in June, the highest level since records began in 2010, and up from 2.8% when Milei took
evidence.source_title: Argentines turn to apps for loans as debt stress hits record

evidence.claim: Milei scrapped old price and shelf-space controls (Shelf Law, Supply Law, Price Observatory) by decree in June 2026.
evidence.quote: The cuts include the Shelf Law, the Supply Law and the Price Observatory.
evidence.source_title: Argentina Tears Up Old Price and Shelf Controls in Deregulation Drive

evidence.claim: Tax amnesty and cash-deposit measures: the government allowed undeclared assets to be regularized at reduced rates (0% to 15% depending on case; 8% if funds remain abroad), and individuals may deposit up to USD 85,000 without justifying origin of funds; estimated USD 370 billion held outside the tax system.
evidence.quote: As of July 2025, individuals are allowed to deposit up to USD 85,000 in financial institutions without having to justify the origin of the funds
evidence.source_title: 2025 Tax Amnesty in Argentina: Milei Gives Final Green Light

evidence.claim: Milei's 2024 tax reform and Ley de Bases created RIGI, granting 30-year stability on tax, customs and FX benefits to large investment projects (minimum USD 200 million); as of May 2026, 16 projects approved (~USD 30 billion).
evidence.quote: Ley de Bases (Law No. 27,742) created the Régimen de Incentivo para Grandes Inversiones (the Large Investment Incentive Regime or "RIGI).
evidence.source_title: The Milei Administration Pushed through Tax Reform | WSC Legal

evidence.claim: Government cut tax revenue: IARAF estimated Milei has cut the equivalent of 3% of GDP in tax revenue since December 2023, mainly PAÍS tax, export taxes and personal property tax; the government also eliminated export taxes on industrial products.
evidence.quote: A recent survey by research center Argentine Center for Fiscal Analysis (in Spanish, IARAF) estimated that Milei has cut the equivalent of 3% of GDP in tax revenue since taking office in December 2023.
evidence.source_title: Milei kept his promise to cut taxes. The problem is he might have gone too far | Buenos Aires Herald

evidence.claim: Milei's 2023 Tax Reform lowered the wealth tax (Bienes Personales) rate and a 2024 tax reform created an amnesty and moratorium; the wealth tax rate falls toward 0.25% by 2027.
evidence.quote: The 2024 Tax Reform will continue to lower rates so that by 2027, the applicable rate will be 0.25%.
evidence.source_title: The Milei Administration Pushed through Tax Reform | WSC Legal

evidence.claim: Real private-sector registered wages fell 3.6% in inflation-adjusted terms since Milei took office, per INDEC data cited by Buenos Aires Herald.
evidence.quote: According to data from Argentina's statistics institute INDEC, private-sector registered wages have fallen 3.6% in inflation-adjusted terms since Milei took office.
evidence.source_title: Milei and the IMF say debt delinquency is no threat to the economy. Experts disagree | Buenos Aires Herald

evidence.claim: Milei publicly promoted the $LIBRA memecoin on his personal X account on 14 Feb 2025; the token then spiked and collapsed within hours. Status: allegation/investigation only; no charges against Milei have been filed in the criminal case, which is at the evidentiary stage.
evidence.quote: Argentine lawyers filed fraud complaints against the libertarian President on Sunday... She doesn't have a deadline to finish investigating the allegations.
evidence.source_title: Argentine judge investigates President Milei's $LIBRA crypto promotion | AP News

evidence.claim: A Argentine congressional investigative commission (opposition-drafted, not a court) concluded in a 200-page report (Nov 2025) that Milei 'used the presidential office' in promoting $LIBRA, which it said was 'designed for a rug pull'. This is a legislative finding, not a criminal or judicial conclusion; the governing party disputed its legality.
evidence.quote: The committee’s final report, which exceeds 200 pages, finds that Milei “used the presidential office,” ... The governing party questioned the legality of the conclusions but did not submit an alternative statement.
evidence.source_title: Argentine congressional committee says Milei played key role in the alleged $Libra scam | EL PAÍS English

evidence.claim: The report also states that Milei's promotion of an earlier token (KIP Protocol, Dec 2024) was part of a 'similar' scheme; allegation only, from the congressional report.
evidence.quote: “in December 2024, a similar financial scheme was recorded involving the digital currency of KIP Protocol [Peh Chyi Haur’s company], in which the president also participated by promoting it”
evidence.source_title: Argentine congressional committee says Milei played key role in the alleged $Libra scam | EL PAÍS English

evidence.claim: Reporting on court probe: a federal probe reportedly found a document detailing an alleged US$5 million deal linking Milei to the $LIBRA promotion (reported March 2026; allegation under investigation, unproven).
evidence.quote: Argentine court probe finds alleged US$5 million deal tied to Milei's promotion of $LIBRA
evidence.source_title: Argentine court probe finds alleged US$5 million deal tied to Milei's promotion of $LIBRA | MercoPress

evidence.claim: Academic/NGO director (CIPCE) says the evidence shows Milei took interest in a business not his own, which he says could constitute incompatible negotiations; this is an opinion, and the same source says no major charges have been brought against Milei. Judiciary has not summoned witnesses or defendants as of Feb 2026.
evidence.quote: “So far, the president has gotten off very lightly. Milei faces no major charges, not because there is no evidence, but because there is a tacit agreement between judges and prosecutors not to investigate him,”
evidence.source_title: The $Libra case: The crypto scandal Milei has yet to answer for | EL PAÍS English

people.summary:
Jeff Bezos (Amazon founder): harm tier "major" (score 0.48; coverage and confidence 1.0). Main reasons, in order of weight:

1. Rubric R1 (severity 2): AWS pitched Rekognition video analysis to ICE in June 2018 [R1-E02, https://www.latimes.com/business/technology/la-fi-tn-amazon-facial-recognition-20181023-story.html]. The company continued after hundreds of workers wrote to Bezos [R1-E03]. The Project Nimbus contract with Israel drew employee protests, and Amazon has not publicly discussed its scope [R1-E06, https://www.wired.com/story/amazon-google-project-nimbus-israel-idf].

2. Rubric R3 (severity 2): OSHA cited Amazon at six warehouses for failing to report injuries and exposing workers to ergonomic hazards [R3-E01, https://www.cnbc.com/2023/04/12/study-amazon-workers-seriously-hurt-at-twice-rate-of-other-warehouses.html]. The FTC settled Prime enrollment and cancellation allegations for a $1 billion civil penalty; Amazon neither admitted nor denied them [R3-E13, https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2025/09/ftc-secures-historic-25-billion-settlement-against-amazon].

3. Rubric R2 (severity 1): Bezos personally blocked a planned Washington Post endorsement [R2-E01, https://thehill.com/homenews/media/4954196-bezos-decision-post-endorsement].

4. Rubric R4 (severity 0): No finding names Bezos personally. The Prime settlement names other executives [R4-E01]. Suits naming Bezos are unadjudicated allegations.

Benefit profile: "minor_guardian" (score 0.15; benefit confidence 0.57). One benefit item was rated: Amazon imposed a one-year moratorium on police use of Rekognition in June 2020 after about two years of pressure [R1-E05, https://www.technologyreview.com/2020/06/12/1003482/amazon-stopped-selling-police-face-recognition-fight]. Benefit evidence is limited, and it is reported separately. It does not offset the harm findings.

evidence.claim: Amazon marketed its Rekognition facial recognition system to government and law enforcement; ACLU reported Amazon views law enforcement deployment as a 'common use case' for the technology.
evidence.quote: Amazon is marketing Rekognition for government surveillance. According to its marketing materials, it views deployment by law enforcement agencies as a “common use case” for this technology.
evidence.source_title: Amazon Teams Up With Government to Deploy Dangerous New Facial Recognition Technology (ACLU)

evidence.claim: AWS sales representatives pitched Rekognition video tagging and analysis to ICE Homeland Security Investigations officials in June 2018, per FOIA-obtained emails.
evidence.quote: Amazon pitched its Rekognition facial recognition system to US Immigration and Customs Enforcement officials as a way to help them target or identify immigrants.
evidence.source_title: Amazon met with ICE officials over facial-recognition system that could identify immigrants (LA Times)

evidence.claim: Hundreds of Amazon workers wrote Bezos demanding Amazon stop supplying Rekognition to ICE; the company continued the ICE pitch after the letter.
evidence.quote: “We refuse to build the platform that powers ICE, and we refuse to contribute to tools that violate human rights.”
evidence.source_title: Amazon met with ICE officials over facial-recognition system that could identify immigrants (LA Times)

evidence.claim: Amazon shareholders in 2019 urged Amazon to stop selling Rekognition to law enforcement; Amazon defended the sales in response.
evidence.quote: In January 2019, Amazon's shareholders "urged Amazon to stop selling Rekognition software to law enforcement agencies." Amazon in response defended its use of Rekognition
evidence.source_title: Amazon Rekognition (Wikipedia)

evidence.claim: Amazon imposed a one-year moratorium on police use of Rekognition in June 2020, after about two years of pressure; the moratorium's coverage of ICE or DHS was unclear.
evidence.quote: But on Wednesday, June 10, Amazon shocked civil rights activists and researchers when it announced that it would place a one-year moratorium on police use of Rekognition.
evidence.source_title: The two-year fight to stop Amazon from selling face recognition to the police (MIT Technology Review)

evidence.claim: Amazon's Project Nimbus cloud contract with the Israeli government and military (about $1.2 billion, shared with Google) drew employee protests; Amazon has not publicly discussed the scope of the contract.
evidence.quote: Google has insisted that it is not aimed at military work and is not "relevant to weapons or intelligence services," while Amazon, seemingly, has not publicly discussed the scope of the contract.
evidence.source_title: The Hidden Ties Between Google and Amazon's Project Nimbus and Israel's Military (WIRED)

evidence.claim: Amazon Web Services lost the 2019 Pentagon JEDI cloud contract to Microsoft, litigated the award, and the Pentagon cancelled JEDI in 2021 and re-tendered to multiple vendors; Amazon alleged presidential interference.
evidence.quote: Amazon alleged Trump “launched repeated public and behind-the-scenes attacks” against the company in an effort to undermine its contracting bid
evidence.source_title: Pentagon awards multibillion-dollar cloud contract to Amazon, Google, Microsoft and Oracle (CNN)

evidence.claim: Amazon signed a $25 million contract with ICE in September 2025 to run cloud services and databases; reported by a newsletter, not verified against contracting records.
evidence.quote: In September 2025, Amazon signed the aforementioned $25 million contract with ICE to help run the agency’s cloud services.
evidence.source_title: How Jeff Bezos and Amazon became instruments of authoritarianism (Brian Merchant, Blood in the Machine)

evidence.claim: Amazon's lobbying operation, led by Jay Carney and reporting to Bezos, set goals including defeating restrictions on artificial intelligence and biometric technologies, per an internal 2018 goals document.
evidence.quote: The mission included defeating restrictions on artificial intelligence and biometric technologies, along with blocking efforts to make companies disclose the data they keep on consumers.
evidence.source_title: The Amazon lobbyists who kill U.S. consumer privacy protections (Reuters)

evidence.claim: Amazon donated $1 million to Trump's inaugural fund (announced Dec 2024); Sen. Warren wrote to Bezos questioning whether the donations aimed to avoid scrutiny and limit regulation.
evidence.quote: using your massive contributions to the inaugural fund to cozy up to the incoming Trump administration in an effort to avoid scrutiny, limit regulation, and buy favor.
evidence.source_title: Letters on Big Tech Donations to Trump Inaugural Fund (Sen. Warren letter)

evidence.claim: Bezos said in 2026 that outlawing data centers is not a solution to AI concerns and that 'healthy government regulation' should eventually apply to AI tools.
evidence.quote: "There's lots to be said for healthy government regulation to improve safety and products and so on," he said. "And I don't see why that won't be applied at some point to the kinds of new tools that are being built by AI."
evidence.source_title: Jeff Bezos says outlawing data centers isn't a solution to AI concerns (Business Insider)

evidence.claim: Bezos pledged $10 billion to the Bezos Earth Fund in 2020; first grants of $791 million to 16 groups were made in November 2020. This is philanthropy on climate, not a stated cost to Amazon's fossil-linked operations.
evidence.quote: Jeff Bezos said Monday he is giving $791 million to 16 groups fighting climate change, the first grants from his Earth Fund
evidence.source_title: Jeff Bezos gives $791 million to 16 groups fighting climate change (Washington Post)

evidence.claim: PBS Frontline reported Bezos's $10B climate pledge announcement made no mention of Amazon's climate impact, and that AWS works with oil and gas companies to help them extract fossil fuels.
evidence.quote: Amazon Web Services (AWS), the company’s cloud computing division, which works with oil and gas companies to help them better extract fossil fuels.
evidence.source_title: Bezos’ $10 Billion Climate Pledge Makes No Mention of Amazon’s Climate Impact (PBS Frontline)

evidence.claim: Amazon co-founded The Climate Pledge in 2019 committing to net-zero by 2040; this is a company commitment, self-described.
evidence.quote: Driven by the urgency of climate change, we co-founded The Climate Pledge in 2019 and committed to achieve net-zero carbon emissions by 2040.
evidence.source_title: Climate solutions - Amazon Sustainability

evidence.claim: Bezos personally decided to block the Washington Post editorial board's planned endorsement of Kamala Harris before the 2024 election, after the board had drafted one; the Post then announced it would stop presidential endorsements.
evidence.quote: The Post's news division reported on Friday that Bezos personally made the decision not to allow an endorsement of Harris after the newspaper's editorial board had already drafted an editorial backing her that was slated to be published before the election.
evidence.source_title: Washington Post reels from Bezos decision to not endorse

evidence.claim: Bezos announced a directive that the Washington Post opinion section would write only in support of 'personal liberties and free markets' and leave opposing viewpoints to others; opinions editor David Shipley resigned.
evidence.quote: We are going to be writing every day in support and defense of two pillars: personal liberties and free markets, Bezos wrote in a memo to staffers announcing the changes. "We'll cover other topics too of course, but viewpoints opposing those pillars will be left to be published by others."
evidence.source_title: Jeff Bezos revamps Washington Post opinion section, leading editor to quit

evidence.claim: After columnist Ruth Marcus wrote a column criticizing Bezos's opinion-section policy, publisher Will Lewis killed it and she resigned; Bloomberg reported the killed column and resignation.
evidence.quote: Ruth Marcus resigned from the newspaper Monday after Chief Executive Officer Will Lewis killed a column she wrote that criticized recent changes made by Post owner Jeff Bezos.
evidence.source_title: Washington Post Editor Quits After Bezos-Critical Article Killed (Bloomberg)

evidence.claim: Amazon's general counsel David Zapolsky, in a meeting with Bezos's leadership team, advised that fired worker organizer Chris Smalls be made the face of warehouse protest, calling Smalls 'not smart or articulate' and describing his conduct as 'immoral, unacceptable, and arguably illegal'; Bezos was the recipient of the memo per a lawsuit. Amazon said Smalls was fired for violating quarantine rules.
evidence.quote: Zapolsky said Smalls was "not smart or articulate" and said Amazon should focus on highlighting to the press how "the organizer's conduct was immoral, unacceptable, and arguably illegal," according to Vice.
evidence.source_title: Amazon lawyer calls fired warehouse worker 'not smart or articulate'

evidence.claim: A lawsuit alleges the Zapolsky memo was sent to CEO Jeff Bezos and that top executives including Bezos perpetuated discriminatory animus; this is an allegation in a complaint, not an adjudicated finding.
evidence.quote: By and through the release of this memo, it has become clear that top level Amazon executives, including CEO Jeff Bezos, perpetuated the company's pervasive discriminatory animus against its minority workers.
evidence.source_title: Smalls v. Amazon, Inc. - 1:20-cv-05492

evidence.claim: The NLRB General Counsel found Amazon illegally fired worker activists in retaliation for protected organizing (Staten Island pandemic walkout organizers); the NLRB found merit to a complaint that a Staten Island warehouse worker's firing was illegal retaliation.
evidence.quote: In December 2020, the National Labor Relations Board found merit to a complaint that a Staten Island warehouse worker's firing was an illegal retaliation for organizing for pandemic safety procedure.

evidence.claim: The NLRB Board ordered Amazon to bargain with the Amazon Labor Union over the JFK8 facility; Amazon has refused to recognize the union's 2022 election win and has said it will appeal, while also contesting NLRB authority in court filings.
evidence.quote: The Board granted the General Counsel's motion for summary judgment in this refusal-to-bargain case arising from Amazon Labor Union's 2022 election victory at Amazon's JFK8 fulfillment center in Staten Island, New York.
evidence.source_title: 04/02/2026: NLRB Orders Amazon to Bargain with Union

evidence.claim: Amazon argued in a legal filing that the National Labor Relations Board is unconstitutional, and its CEO said the NLRB will not 'rule against itself' and vowed to appeal JFK8 election results to federal courts.

evidence.claim: Amazon, per EPI reporting, has taken anti-union actions including firing and harassing pro-union workers at Staten Island and other facilities; the NLRB rejected Amazon's objections to the Staten Island election.

evidence.source_title: Corporate union busting in plain sight: How Amazon, Starbucks, and Trader Joe's crushed dynamic grassroots worker organizing campaigns

evidence.claim: Washington Post laid off roughly a third of its newsroom in a restructuring in 2026; the Amazon beat reporter Caroline O'Donovan was among those laid off. Critics link the cuts to ownership's direction, but no source records Bezos directing the specific layoffs.
evidence.quote: Among those laid off was Caroline O'Donovan, the Washington Post's beat reporter covering Amazon
evidence.source_title: Mass layoffs at Washington Post, Amazon beat reporter fired, but where is Jeff Bezos

evidence.claim: Amazon paid Melania Trump's production company about $40 million for rights to a documentary and about $35 million for marketing; critics allege the deal was a bribe, and Democratic lawmakers have questioned whether it violated anti-bribery law. evidence.claim: Smalls was charged with trespass and another misdemeanor and spent 24 hours in jail after the Met Gala protest; the arrest was of a protester, not directed by any documented Bezos order.
