people.descriptor: Podcaster, host of The Joe Rogan Experience
notes: power backfilled from hand-entered reach and authority, not from a research run
people.summary:
Joe Rogan's harm tier is "minor" (harm score 0.4, coverage 1.0, confidence 0.8). His benefit tier is "none_documented" (benefit score 0.0, confidence 0.8).

The main reason for the harm tier is climate misinformation, scored at severity 2 under R1. The record includes a cooling claim about a 485-million-year temperature study that AFP fact-checked as misleading [R1-E03, https://www.preventionweb.net/news/five-ways-joe-rogan-misleads-listeners-about-climate-change]. It also includes a cooling claim on the Mel Gibson episode that climate experts said misreads a temperature graph [R1-E04, https://earth.org/what-joe-rogan-is-getting-wrong-about-global-warming], and promotion of a link between global warming and Earth's magnetic field [R1-E05, https://insideclimatenews.org/news/30052023/todays-climate-joe-rogan-climate-misinformation-tiktok].

Health and product items were documented but scored zero under R4. They include repeated ivermectin promotion for COVID-19 [R4-E04] and fact-checks finding several podcast claims misleading [R4-E05]. A supplement class action involving Onnit is only an allegation, with no ruling on the merits [R4-E01]. R2 and R3 were also scored zero.

The only benefit-related item is an episode that platformed AI extinction-risk warnings. The record treats this as a platform, not an executed risk-reducing act [R1-E08, https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=j2i9D24KQ5k]. No benefit was scored. This absence of documented benefit is not a negative finding.

Confidence is moderate because most harm items come from secondary reporting and fact-checks, not adjudicated findings.

evidence.claim: Rogan repeatedly amplified COVID-19 misinformation on his podcast, including booking Dr. Robert Malone and suggesting young people do not need vaccination; hundreds of health professionals wrote to Spotify asking it to act.
evidence.quote: Rogan has faced backlash over the course of the pandemic for repeatedly sharing and providing a platform for misinformation around the Covid-19 pandemic and vaccines.
evidence.source_title: Joe Rogan, Spotify respond to protest over Covid-19 misinformation (NBC News)

evidence.claim: Rogan's climate-related content has been judged to spread climate misinformation: in an episode with Lindzen and Happer, he implied nefarious intent behind climate-policy spending and omitted that fossil fuel companies are among the most profitable firms; the industry spent $219 million in the 2024 US election.
evidence.quote: In both the episode with Lindzen and Happer and the one with Sanders, Rogan repeatedly mentioned the large amount of money being spent on the clean energy transition, implying nefarious intent among those who accept mainstream climate science. These discussions neglected to mention that numerous fossil fuel companies are among the most profitable in the world
evidence.source_title: Five ways Joe Rogan misleads listeners about climate change (PreventionWeb / Yale Climate Connections)

evidence.claim: Rogan misrepresented a 2024 Washington Post-reported study on 485 million years of temperatures, claiming it 'found that we're in a cooling period' on a podcast episode with Bernie Sanders; AFP fact-checked the claim as misleading.
evidence.quote: Rogan misleadingly claimed that the study "found that we're in a cooling period." He added, "This was, like, a very inconvenient discovery."
evidence.source_title: Five ways Joe Rogan misleads listeners about climate change (PreventionWeb / Yale Climate Connections)

evidence.claim: Rogan told Mel Gibson's episode audience that a climate study showed cooling, a claim climate experts said misreads a temperature graph; the Climate Town analysis said the Gibson interview had 11.5 million YouTube views.
evidence.quote: On YouTube alone, Rogan's interview with Gibson was viewed 11.5 million times at the time of writing.
evidence.source_title: What Joe Rogan Is Getting Wrong About Global Warming (Earth.org)

evidence.claim: Rogan promoted a conspiracy theory linking global warming to Earth's magnetic field, a clip that went viral on TikTok per a watchdog report.
evidence.quote: A clip of celebrity podcaster Joe Rogan touting a conspiracy theory that links global warming to Earth's magnetic field has gone viral on TikTok, despite the platform's new policy prohibiting climate misinformation, a new report warns.
evidence.source_title: Joe Rogan Is Fueling Climate Misinformation on TikTok, Watchdogs Warn (Inside Climate News)

evidence.claim: Rogan, speaking on the Joe Rogan Experience about AI governance, said he hoped AI would take over government and military decisions and that 'All war stops on the planet', drawing criticism from an AI ethics expert who called handing government to AI a realistic but concerning direction.
evidence.quote: "It sounds like a crazy hope, but my hope is that as AI becomes more and more omnipresent, as we start farming off various tasks to it, one of the things that we're gonna farm off is government."
evidence.source_title: Joe Rogan's AI Government Idea Draws Stark Warning From Ethics Expert (Newsweek)

evidence.claim: Rogan told LL Cool J on his podcast that his biggest fear is who will control AI, and speculated AI could reject human guidance.
evidence.quote: Rogan said his biggest "fear” is who will control the technology.
evidence.source_title: Joe Rogan Warns AI Will Realize 'Folly of the Human Way' (Newsweek)

evidence.claim: On his podcast with AI safety researcher Roman Yampolskiy, Rogan platformed extinction-risk warnings and said he was in agreement that AI is dangerous, while not taking concrete action; the episode itself is a platform rather than an executed risk-reducing act.
evidence.quote: We have Nobel Prize winners, touring award winners all saying this is very dangerous. 20 30% pdoom.
evidence.source_title: Joe Rogan Experience #2345 - Roman Yampolskiy

evidence.claim: Rogan apologized to Spotify and said he would try harder to book differing views and research topics; he agreed to have about 70 of his episodes removed at his own request, and Spotify's CEO said Rogan made the removal decision and he agreed with it.
evidence.quote: Ek said Rogan made the decision to remove the episodes and that he agreed with the move.
evidence.source_title: Spotify CEO apologizes but backs Joe Rogan after racial slur episodes are removed (NBC News)

evidence.claim: Rogan said he would do his best to research topics and try harder to get people with differing opinions on his show, after the COVID-misinformation backlash; he praised Spotify's addition of content advisories. These were pledges, not verified changes in show practice.
evidence.quote: He said he would "do my best to make sure I've researched these topics" and "try harder to get people with differing opinions" on his show
evidence.source_title: Joe Rogan, Spotify respond to protest over Covid-19 misinformation (NBC News)

evidence.claim: Rogan used the racial slur on podcast episodes over a 12-year span, per a compilation; he said 'I never used it to be racist'. Context: a clip describing a Black neighborhood movie theater as 'like we were in Planet of the Apes'.
evidence.quote: Rogan's message Saturday addressed a video a clip from his podcast 11 years ago in which he talked about going to a movie theater in a Black neighborhood to see "Planet of the Apes". "I was trying to make the story entertaining, and I said we got out and it was like we were in Africa. It's like we were in 'Planet of the Apes.'"
evidence.source_title: Joe Rogan apologizes for using racial slurs after a video surfaces (NPR)

evidence.claim: Spotify pulled over 100 episodes of the show after Rogan's apology; Spotify CEO said Rogan chose to remove episodes and that past comments 'do not represent the values of this company', backing him.
evidence.quote: Ek said in a letter to employees that Joe Rogan decided to remove some episodes of the podcast and that his past comments "do not represent the values of this company."
evidence.source_title: Spotify CEO apologizes but backs Joe Rogan (NBC News)

evidence.claim: In 2024 Rogan hosted Trump and, per fact-checkers, Trump repeated false claims about the 2020 election and voting fraud in the three-hour interview; Rogan's own role was as host and he pressed Trump for evidence in some exchanges.
evidence.quote: Donald Trump used a lengthy interview with podcaster Joe Rogan to dig in on his false claims about voting, election fraud and his loss in
evidence.source_title: FACT FOCUS: Trump repeated election lies in his interview with Joe Rogan (AP)

evidence.claim: Onnit Labs (co-founded by Rogan, per complaint) was sued in a proposed class action (Lotz v. Onnit Labs, S.D.N.Y. 7:24-cv-03098, filed April 2024) alleging false advertising of Alpha BRAIN as supporting memory and focus, based on the company's own 2016 study. Rogan and his podcast were not named as defendants. Allegation only; no ruling on the merits.
evidence.quote: Onnit, which the lawsuit notes was co-founded by Rogan, who promotes the products on his controversial podcast The Joe Rogan Experience, was sold to Unilever in 2021, so neither Rogan nor his podcast are named as defendants in the complaint
evidence.source_title: Joe Rogan-backed company sued for peddling supplements with 'false' advertising | The Independent

evidence.claim: Allegation (unproven): the class action says Onnit's 2016 study showed Alpha BRAIN performed no better than placebo in most tests, and that Onnit's public claims overstated the study's findings. Plaintiff's allegation, not adjudicated.
evidence.quote: the lawsuit claims that the full text from the study showed a very slight improvement in only one aspect of memory and "no improvement for other cognitive domains."
evidence.source_title: Joe Rogan-backed pharma company sued for peddling health supplements with 'false' advertising

evidence.claim: Rogan, on his podcast while promoting Alpha BRAIN Black Label (per 2022 Onnit YouTube clip quoted in the lawsuit coverage), said he and Aubrey Marcus started Onnit and that they funded two double-blind placebo-controlled studies; the plaintiff disputes the study claims. Statement is documented; its accuracy is contested by the plaintiff, not adjudicated.
evidence.quote: "Aubrey and I started Onnit" because Rogan had a fascination with nootropics, and when they created the product together they funded two double-blind placebo-controlled studies "that showed an increase in verbal memory" and "increase in reaction times."
evidence.source_title: Joe Rogan-backed company sued for peddling supplements with 'false' advertising | The Independent

evidence.claim: Rogan repeatedly promoted ivermectin as a COVID-19 treatment on his podcast and in a September 2021 Instagram post, despite FDA and CDC warnings against its use for COVID-19. Public-health misstatement, not a regulatory finding of fraud; relevant only as a documented public statement on a material health fact.
evidence.quote: Spotify aired Joe Rogan's podcast touting ivermectin as part of his COVID-19 treatment, despite the Food and Drug Association (FDA) calling the drug "dangerous" in large doses and warning people not to use it to treat the disease.
evidence.source_title: Joe Rogan Touts Ivermectin for COVID-19 Despite FDA, CDC Warnings

evidence.claim: Fact-check reporting (BBC) found several specific claims made on the podcast to be misleading or untrue, including that vaccines are gene therapy and that vaccinated post-COVID people face greater side-effect risk. Journalistic fact-check, not adjudicated.
evidence.quote: "This is not a vaccine, this is essentially a gene therapy." But this is not true.
evidence.source_title: Joe Rogan: Four claims from his Spotify podcast fact-checked

evidence.claim: Rogan's exclusive Spotify licensing deal (2020, reported ~$100M) was a commercial arrangement; a 2024 renewal (reported estimated earnout up to $250M, terms undisclosed by Spotify) ended exclusivity. Disclosed commercial relationship; no conflict finding was found.
evidence.quote: In 2024, Rogan ended his deal that made "JRE" exclusive to the platform.
evidence.source_title: Joe Rogan Renews Nine-Figure Spotify Deal

evidence.claim: Rogan co-founded Onnit, a supplement company he promoted on his podcast (Onnit sponsored the podcast from around 2010 per Sportskeeda); Onnit was sold to Unilever in 2021. The relationship between his co-founder equity, sponsorship and podcast promotion is documented in press but no adjudicated undisclosed-conflict finding was found.
evidence.quote: Rogan is the biggest promoter of the brand
evidence.source_title: How is Joe Rogan related to health and fitness brand 'Onnit'

people.name: Jon Stewart
people.descriptor: American comedian, host of The Daily Show
notes: power backfilled from hand-entered reach and authority, not from a research run
people.summary:
Harm tier: not_a_dick (harm score 0.0; all four rubrics at severity 0). Benefit tier: minor_guardian (benefit score 0.097; one rubric, R1, at severity 1). The two profiles are reported separately and are not netted against each other. Coverage is 1.0 and confidence is 0.73.

Harm: The most-weighted harm-related item is that Stewart kept hosting during the 2007–2008 Writers Guild strike, which the source describes as crossing the picket line [R3-E01, https://www.currentaffairs.org/news/2015/09/remembering-jon-stewarts-nasty-side]. A former writer's claim that he punished unionizing writers is recorded only as an accusation [R3-E02, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Stewart]. The Apple disputes over The Problem are reported secondhand or as Stewart's own account, with no adjudicated wrongdoing [R4-E01, https://www.nytimes.com/2023/10/19/business/media/jon-stewart-the-problem-ends.html; R4-E03]. His criticism of CBS, the White House and Congress is documented as satire or rebuke, with no documented retaliation [R2-E02, https://www.npr.org/2025/07/27/nx-s1-5480172/colbert-south-park-jon-stewart-paramount-trump].

Benefit: The benefit rating rests on R1 items [R1-E01, R1-E02], which are public criticism of AI leaders. The cited items themselves describe this as commentary rather than a costly act, so the benefit evidence is thin and should be read with that caveat. A lack of documented benefit is not a negative finding.

evidence.claim: Stewart publicly criticized AI leaders' promises and said AI companies should not be allowed to self-police; on The Daily Show he argued 'Why can't we just slow this down rather than let people regulate something they have a clear conflict of interest in regulating?'
evidence.quote: “Why can’t we just slow this down rather than let people regulate something they have a clear conflict of interest in regulating?”
evidence.source_title: Jon Stewart Breaks Down the Threat of AI (Rolling Stone)

evidence.claim: Stewart on The Daily Show criticized Trump's suggestion that AI leaders should police themselves and asked how the tech giants could be trusted to regulate themselves; this is commentary, not a costly act.
evidence.quote: “How can you justify letting the tech giants regulate themselves?”
evidence.source_title: Jon Stewart Breaks Down the Threat of AI (Rolling Stone)

evidence.claim: Stewart, in a Daily Show episode, said AI was being used primarily for surveillance, drone targeting and similar purposes, and questioned the trade-off against a 10-25% extinction risk he cited from AI leaders' own admissions.
evidence.quote: “What are we getting in exchange for this 10-25% chance at extinction?”
evidence.source_title: Jon Stewart's 'Daily Show' Skips David Ellison-Skydance News to Take on AI (Variety)

evidence.claim: Stewart hosted former Anthropic and OpenAI researcher Jacob Coxon, who spoke out about AI dangers, on The Daily Show and discussed AI lab security and risks with him; this is a media platform for a whistleblower, not a costly act by Stewart.
evidence.quote: Jacob Coxon, a former Anthropic and OpenAI researcher who spoke out about the dangers of artificial intelligence, opens up to Jon Stewart about the grim reality of the tech industry
evidence.source_title: Jacob Coxon On Witnessing the Existential Threat of AI from the Inside | The Daily Show

evidence.claim: Apple and Stewart ended The Problem with Jon Stewart in October 2023 amid creative differences reportedly involving AI and China coverage; Stewart later said Apple did not want him to say things that might get him in trouble. Stewart's own account of the dispute is not independently verified.
evidence.quote: Stewart told his show's staff that Apple executives had issues with specific episodes in the works on the topic of China and AI.
evidence.source_title: Jon Stewart walks away from Apple TV show after dispute over AI, China episodes (Mashable)

evidence.claim: Stewart was a sustained advocate for 9/11 responders; in September 2015 he spent a morning lobbying Senate offices for the permanent extension of the Zadroga Act health programs, after a pledge made on his show. (Relevant only as general civic advocacy, outside R1 dimensions.)
evidence.quote: Former "Daily Show" host Jon Stewart joined 100 9/11 first responders today to lobby lawmakers for the extension of 9/11 health programs
evidence.source_title: Jon Stewart Lobbies, Chases Down Lawmakers for 9/11 First Responders (ABC News)

evidence.claim: Stewart's 2019 testimony to a House committee on reauthorizing the 9/11 Victim Compensation Fund; the bill later passed. The fund is not an R1 dimension, so this is recorded only for context.
evidence.quote: Your indifference cost these men and women their most valuable commodity: time.
evidence.source_title: Jon Stewart-Backed 9/11 First Responders' Bill Passes After Emotional Congress Speech (Vanity Fair)

evidence.claim: On The Daily Show Stewart framed fossil fuel emissions criticism in a way that drew backlash for seeming sympathetic to Big Oil: he said that 100 fossil fuel companies make 70 percent of global emissions and suggested it would be better not to villainize them.
evidence.quote: “100 of these [fossil fuel] companies make 70 percent of our global emissions. Wouldn't it be better to hold our noses, to not villainize them,
evidence.source_title: Jon Stewart's Sympathy For Big Oil Sparks Major Backlash (Forbes)

evidence.claim: Stewart co-led the 'Rally to Restore Sanity and/or Fear' on the National Mall (Oct 30, 2010), a satirical counter-event to Glenn Beck's rally; no documented retaliation or force associated.
evidence.quote: The Rally to Restore Sanity and/or Fear was a gathering on October 30, 2010, at the National Mall in Washington, D.C. The rally was led by Jon Stewart
evidence.source_title: Rally to Restore Sanity and/or Fear - Wikipedia

evidence.claim: Stewart delivered a monologue on The Daily Show questioning CBS's statement that the cancellation of The Late Show with Stephen Colbert was 'purely a financial decision'; no documented retaliation against Stewart followed in the sources found.
evidence.quote: He offered a blistering monologue that questioned CBS's statement asserting Colbert's cancellation was "purely a financial decision,"
evidence.source_title: Stephen Colbert, Jon Stewart and South Park push back : NPR

evidence.claim: Stewart mocked Trump's September 2025 response to Jimmy Kimmel's suspension on The Daily Show, satirically praising Trump; satire only, no documented act against Stewart by government.
evidence.quote: Jon Stewart mocks Trump in 'Daily Show' reaction to Jimmy Kimmel getting pulled from ABC
evidence.source_title: Jon Stewart mocks Trump in 'Daily Show' reaction to Jimmy Kimmel getting pulled from ABC

evidence.claim: On The Daily Show Stewart mocked Trump's White House ban on CNN, MS NOW and Politico with satire ('You could ban the press, or you could be a better f***ing president'); verbal criticism only, no documented follow-up act against him.
evidence.quote: “You could ban the press, or you could be a better f—ing president,” he said.
evidence.source_title: Jon Stewart slams Trump's White House media ban on 'The Daily Show'

evidence.claim: Stewart testified before the House Judiciary Subcommittee on Civil Rights and Civil Liberties in 2019, shouting at lawmakers and calling them 'shameful' over the 9/11 Victim Compensation Fund; a public rebuke of Congress, not coercion.
evidence.quote: In his emotional testimony before the House Judiciary Subcommittee on Civil Rights and Civil Liberties, Stewart at times broke down in tears, shouting at the lawmakers and calling them "shameful."
evidence.source_title: Jon Stewart lashes out at hearing on 9/11 responders bill

evidence.claim: Stewart crossed the Writers Guild picket line in 2007-2008 strike by continuing to host, using the title 'A Daily Show with Jon Stewart' during the strike; the show returned while other writers were on strike.
evidence.quote: Stewart publicly insisted he supported the strike, yet undermined his fellow writers by continuing to work.
evidence.source_title: Remembering Jon Stewart's Nasty Side (Current Affairs)

evidence.claim: Former Daily Show writer David Feldman accused Stewart of punishing writers for their decision to unionize by not using their material (accusation; reported in Wikipedia citing a 2012 Patheos post).
evidence.quote: Former Daily Show writer David Feldman also accused Stewart of being anti-union at the time and of punishing his writers for their decision to unionize by not using their material.
evidence.source_title: Jon Stewart - Wikipedia

evidence.claim: Viacom (parent of Comedy Central, where Stewart hosted) settled a class action brought by former unpaid interns; Stewart later said paying interns made the Daily Show more diverse.
evidence.quote: Media giant Viacom has reached a settlement in a class action lawsuit brought by former unpaid interns of the company.
evidence.source_title: Yet Another Unpaid Intern Lawsuit Settles: This Time, It's Viacom (FindLaw)

evidence.claim: Stewart's Apple TV+ show The Problem was cancelled in October 2023 after Apple disagreed over topics including AI and China; Stewart said Apple told him not to have FTC chair Lina Khan on.
evidence.quote: Apple asked us not do it ... They literally said 'please don't talk to her'.
evidence.source_title: The Problem with Jon Stewart - Wikipedia

evidence.claim: Stewart's Daily Show salary was reported at $25-30 million per year by TV Guide's annual salary report (2014), per Business Insider.
evidence.quote: According to TV Guide's annual salary report, "The Daily Show" host makes anywhere from $25-$30 million per year for the Comedy Central show.
evidence.source_title: Jon Stewart Makes Up To $30 Million For 'The Daily Show' (Business Insider)

evidence.claim: Per NYT reporting (sources, not on the record), Stewart and Apple parted ways over creative differences on The Problem; Stewart told staff Apple executives were concerned about potential China and AI topics and some guests. Apple declined to comment. This is a reported editorial dispute, not a legal finding; no wrongdoing was adjudicated.
evidence.quote: But Mr. Stewart and Apple executives had disagreements over some of the topics and guests on “The Problem,” two of the people said.
evidence.source_title: Jon Stewart's Show on Apple Is Ending - NYT

evidence.claim: On the Daily Show (April 2024), Stewart publicly said Apple had asked his team not to have FTC Chair Lina Khan on a podcast; Apple did not respond to the request for comment. This is Stewart's own allegation, not an adjudicated finding; the claim concerns a company's editorial pressure, not a conflict of interest by Stewart.
evidence.quote: “I wanted to have you on a podcast, and Apple asked us not to do it,” Stewart told Khan during an episode of “The Daily Show” on Monday. “They literally said, ‘Please don’t talk to her.’”
evidence.source_title: Jon Stewart says Apple asked him not to interview FTC chair Lina Khan - CNBC

evidence.claim: Per CNN reporting (a person familiar, not on the record), Apple had concerns about three planned season topics (China, Israel, AI); Stewart said he had creative control but grew frustrated with Apple pushing back on guests and subjects. Unproven and reported secondhand.
evidence.quote: He told his show staffers that Apple had concerns about the subject matter he had planned for three shows during the upcoming season, a person familiar with the discussions told CNN in October. Those topics included China, Israel and AI.
evidence.source_title: Jon Stewart rips into Apple, his old boss, on The Daily Show - CNN

people.name: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva
notes: power backfilled from hand-entered reach and authority, not from a research run
people.summary:
Subject: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, Brazilian president. Harm tier: major (final score 0.67; coverage 1.0; confidence 0.98).

Main reasons, in order of weight:

1. Fossil fuel expansion (R1, severity 3). The government granted Petrobras a licence to drill an exploratory well at the mouth of the Amazon, two weeks before COP30, after the environmental regulator had earlier refused it [R1-E02] (https://www.climatechangenews.com/2025/10/21/ahead-of-cop30-brazil-grants-petrobras-a-licence-to-drill-for-oil-in-amazon-region). Reporting says Lula pressed the regulator, whose staff had recommended denial [R1-E03] (https://sumauma.com/en/foz-do-amazonas-governo-lula-autoriza-a-exploracao-de-petroleo-e-enfraquece-a-cop30). Lula also said the regulator acted as if it was "against the government" [R1-E04].

2. Labour and licensing (R3, severity 1). After the labour ministry added BYD to a registry of slavery-like employers, the inspection secretary who did so was dismissed [R3-E01] (https://www.business-humanrights.org/en/latest-news/brasil-chefe-da-fiscaliza%C3%A7%C3%A3o-do-trabalho-%C3%A9-demitido-ap%C3%B3s-controv%C3%A9rsia-envolvendo-inclus%C3%A3o-e-retirada-da-byd-da-lista-de-trabalho-escravo). The ministry denied any link to BYD [R3-E02].

3. Corruption allegations (R4, severity 0) and critics' concerns (R2, severity 0) carry no weight in the harm score. Lower-court convictions were annulled [R4-E01, R4-E02], and other charges were not adjudicated [R4-E05].

Benefit tier: minor_guardian (benefit score 0.38; benefit confidence 0.70). Documented benefit acts include a veto of 63 articles of a licensing bill that environmentalists opposed [R1-E08] and championing a fossil fuel phase-out roadmap at COP30, though the final text omitted it [R1-E10] (https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cn51pn74l23o). These are reported separately and do not offset the harm tier.

evidence.claim: Lula's government approved OPEC+ membership for Brazil (National Energy Council decision, February 2025), which the AP described as Lula's pursuit of increased oil production.
evidence.quote: Brazil's government on Tuesday approved joining OPEC+, Lula's pursuit of increased oil production, however, has met criticism
evidence.source_title: AP: Brazil to join OPEC+, group of major oil-exporting nations

evidence.claim: Lula's government granted Petrobras an environmental licence to drill an exploratory oil well in the Foz do Amazonas Basin (block FZA-M-59) at the mouth of the Amazon, two weeks before COP30, after IBAMA had earlier denied it in 2023; Lula publicly backed exploration, arguing revenues fund the transition.
evidence.quote: After five years of discussions, Brazil's government approved an environmental permit for Petrobras to drill an exploratory oil well in block FZA-M-59 in the Foz do Amazonas Basin, in Amapá state.
evidence.source_title: Climate Change News: Ahead of COP30, Brazil grants Petrobras a licence to drill for oil in Amazon region

evidence.claim: Lula pressured the environmental regulator IBAMA over the Block 59 licence; IBAMA's president signed off despite a technical staff report recommending denial for a third time, amid political pressure from ministers acting for the government.
evidence.quote: In May, amidst political pressure, Ibama's president, Rodrigo Agostinho, ignored a report from 29 technical staff members at the environmental agency and greenlit the finalization of licensing for Block 59.
evidence.source_title: SUMAÚMA: Foz do Amazonas: Lula administration greenlights oil exploration and weakens COP30

evidence.claim: Lula said Ibama was acting as if it was 'against the government' while pressure rose for the Petrobras drilling licence.
evidence.quote: As Petrobras appealed, pressure rose from Lula, who said earlier this year that Ibama was a government agency acting as if it was "against the government."
evidence.source_title: France 24: Brazil greenlights oil drilling in sensitive Amazon region

evidence.claim: Lula publicly announced the Petrobras licence and hailed the August 2026 Foz do Amazonas oil discovery as a 'passport to the country's future', and said he had announced the licence before COP despite objections because national interests were at stake.
evidence.quote: "I took the decision to announce that people wanted to do exploratory drilling there before COP because the interests of our country and our company were at stake."
evidence.source_title: BBC: Brazil's President Lula hails oil discovery near Amazon river

evidence.claim: Lula stated in a speech in February 2025 that humanity will depend on fossil fuels for a long time, while backing oil exploration as a source of revenue for the clean-energy transition.
evidence.quote: "I dream of a day when we no longer need fossil fuels, but that day is still far away. Humanity will depend on them for a long time," he said in a speech back in February in Pará
evidence.source_title: Climate Change News: Ahead of COP30, Brazil grants Petrobras a licence to drill for oil in Amazon region

evidence.claim: Lula's government backed Petrobras's 2026–2030 plan allocating US$69.2 billion to oil and gas exploration and production, more than five times the US$13 billion for transition initiatives over the same period.
evidence.quote: his government has backed Petrobras's 2026–2030 plan to allocate US$69.2 billion for oil and gas exploration and production over five years, more than five times the US$13 billion earmarked over the same period for transition initiatives
evidence.source_title: Climate Rights International: What's at Stake in Brazil's Presidential Election: Fossil Fuels

evidence.claim: Lula's government, through the Environment Ministry, vetoed 63 articles of a congressional environmental licensing bill that environmentalists said would have fast-tracked Amazon projects and weakened agency licensing authority, which was pushed by the opposition.
evidence.quote: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva threw out 63 out of the controversial bill's 400 measures, the government said
evidence.source_title: AP: Brazil's Lula vetoes parts of environment bill pushed by the opposition that could harm the Amazon

evidence.claim: Lula stated that Brazil had to give up no oil; the government's COP30 presidency pushed a fossil fuel transition roadmap, which Lula championed, but it was excluded from the final COP30 text after opposition from oil-producing nations.
evidence.quote: The inclusion of a commitment to create a "Roadmap" for the end of fossil fuels was advocated by President Lula and members of the Brazilian government on several occasions.
evidence.source_title: OECO: Roadmap for Phasing Out Fossil Fuels Left Out of Final COP30 Text

evidence.claim: Lula publicly championed a fossil fuel phase-out roadmap at COP30 and called for defeating climate deniers, though the final text omitted any fossil fuel phase-out language.
evidence.quote: It's time to inflict a new defeat on the deniers,
evidence.source_title: BBC: Fight fake news and climate deniers, Brazil's Lula tells UN talks

evidence.claim: Lula's lawyers sued prosecutor Deltan Dallagnol over a 2016 press conference; the Superior Court of Justice ordered Dallagnol to pay Lula damages. This is a court outcome against a critic-prosecutor, not an act by Lula's government.
evidence.quote: Lula's lawyers filed a lawsuit against prosecutor Deltan Dallagnol, seeking compensation for moral damages for the press conference given by Dallagnol in 2016 in which he used a Microsoft PowerPoint presentation to explain the charges against Lula.
evidence.source_title: Imprisonment of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (Wikipedia)

evidence.claim: The Rio Times reports the STJ ordered Dallagnol to compensate Lula for 'moral damage' tied to a 2016 graphic he showed the press depicting Lula as head of a 'criminal organization'; the STJ judge said the spectacle was not compatible with the seriousness an investigation requires. Lula's lawyers' suit is a private civil action by Lula, and the item concerns Dallagnol's conduct.
evidence.quote: The STJ set the compensation because in 2016 the former prosecutor showed the press a graphic depicting Lula da Silva as the head of a "criminal organization."
evidence.source_title: Brazil's Supreme Court orders prosecutor to compensate former President Lula da Silva for 'moral damage' (Rio Times)

evidence.claim: The Lula government's Secom launched a 'Brasil Contra Fake' misinformation website in March 2023; critics said it was biased toward the government and could be used to delegitimise criticism. Secom said it is not a fact-checking agency but a space to clarify government actions. This is a documented government act, with critics' concern; no documented punishment of critics is reported in this source.
evidence.quote: Launched on March 25th by the Communication Secretariat (Secom, by its Portuguese acronym) of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's government, the Brasil Contra Fake [Brazil against fake news] website has, like other governmental publications, an obvious bias in favor of the authorities and policies in power.
evidence.source_title: Brazilian government launches official fact-checking website and draws criticism from independent agencies (LJR)

evidence.claim: An opinion writer argues the Lula government's anti-misinformation campaign could let it denounce criticism as 'fake news'. This is opinion; no documented act of silencing is cited in the excerpt.
evidence.quote: The initiative, viewed by many as a tool for President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's administration to delegitimise criticism it faces under the guise of "fact-checking", raised serious concerns about government overreach, freedom of expression and the future of Brazil's fragile democracy.
evidence.source_title: A Brazilian 'Ministry of Truth' is in the making (Al Jazeera opinion)

evidence.claim: Lula's government was reported to have been the subject of a 2004 episode in which the government considered expelling a New York Times reporter over an article about Lula's drinking, and the decision was revoked after the reporter issued a written retraction.
evidence.quote: Em 2004, o governo Lula cogitou expulsar do país o jornalista americano Larry Rohter, do The New York Times, por escrever uma reportagem sobre a suposta propensão de Lula a beber, mas a decisão foi revogada depois de uma retratação por escrito do repórter.
evidence.source_title: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (Portuguese Wikipedia)

evidence.claim: Brazil's labour ministry added Chinese EV maker BYD to a national registry of employers accused of slavery-like labour conditions; the government then dismissed the secretary of labour inspection who had added it, and the ministry called the dismissal 'an administrative act'.
evidence.quote: Brazil's secretary of labor inspection was fired for adding Chinese automaker BYD to a registry of employers accused of subjecting workers to conditions described by the government as similar to slavery, two people close to the matter told Reuters.
evidence.source_title: Brazil: Head of labour inspection fired after controversy over BYD's inclusion and removal from the forced labour list

evidence.claim: Labour minister Luiz Marinho was previously accused of interfering in labour inspectors' work to keep big companies off the forced-labour list; the ministry denied the firing was linked to BYD.
evidence.quote: Marinho has previously been accused of interfering in their work to keep big companies off the list.
evidence.source_title: Brazil: Head of labour inspection fired after controversy over BYD's inclusion and removal from the forced labour list

evidence.claim: The 2024 BYD factory inspection found 163 Chinese workers working under conditions described as slavery-like, employed by a third-party contractor; inspectors rejected BYD's defence that subcontractors were responsible.
evidence.quote: The inspector rejected BYD's defence that subcontractors were responsible, concluding the company itself was accountable.
evidence.source_title: Brazil fires labor inspector after flagging BYD for modern slavery - FreedomUnited

evidence.claim: Lula's government later signed a law (September 2024) maintaining payroll relief for 17 sectors with vetoes, after negotiations with Congress; the tax regime was maintained through 2024 with gradual reintroduction of taxes from 2025.
evidence.quote: With vetoes, President Lula signed into law on Monday a bill that ensures the continuation of payroll tax relief for 17 labor-intensive sectors and small municipalities.
evidence.source_title: Lula signs law maintaining payroll relief for 17 sectors, with vetoes

evidence.claim: Lula signed the 2025 General Environmental Licensing Law (easing licences), but vetoed dozens of provisions; critics said the bill allows self-declared licensing and exempts agribusiness from licensing. Congress later overturned 56 of his 63 vetoes in November 2025.
evidence.quote: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva signed into law a bill easing environmental licenses but vetoed dozens of provisions,
evidence.source_title: Lula signs bill to ease Brazil environmental licenses but vetoes key provisions

evidence.claim: Critics say the licensing law's Article 9 exempting agricultural and livestock activities from licensing was not vetoed by Lula; the law was a 'deliberate' weakening per critics.
evidence.quote: In particular, there was no veto to Article 9, which broadly exempts agricultural and livestock activities from environmental licensing.
evidence.source_title: Shortcuts to degradation: environmental consequences of Brazil's general environmental licensing law

evidence.claim: Lula's government, through the chief of staff's office (run by Rui Costa), pushed Ibama to issue Petrobras an exploratory drilling licence in the Foz do Amazonas basin ahead of COP30; the licence was granted in October 2025 for one exploratory well.
evidence.quote: SUMAÚMA found that after environmental agency concluded the process, the decision to issue the license in the lead-up to COP30 came from the office of the president's chief of staff, which is run by Rui Costa (Workers' Party), one of the biggest advocates for oil exploration in Lula's cabinet.
evidence.source_title: Foz do Amazonas: Lula administration greenlights oil exploration and weakens COP30

evidence.claim: Lula publicly backed Amazon-coast oil exploration despite Ibama's 2023 rejection and environmentalists' objections, saying the country might have oil and that Petrobras would be liable for any spill ('we will be the ones that are liable').
evidence.quote: Lula told the BBC in September: "Brazil is a country that has oil. And possibly we have oil in the Equatorial Margin, and we are making surveys. We're following the law strictly."
evidence.source_title: Brazil grants state oil firm exploration license in Amazon region

evidence.claim: Ibama fined Petrobras about $480,000 after a fluid leak during Foz do Amazonas drilling in January 2026.
evidence.quote: Environmental ​issues materialized in January of this year, after a fluid leaked during the drilling. Ibama fined Petrobras around $480,000 for
evidence.source_title: Amazon oil find gives Brazil's Lula reelection campaign a boost

evidence.claim: Brazil's richest 0.1% increased their share of national income to a record 13.1% in 2024 from 10.2% in 2020, per Reuters analysis of tax-return data during Lula's administration; the rise was attributed mainly to higher Selic interest rates benefiting financial-asset holders.
evidence.quote: Estimates by inequality researcher Sergio Gobetti based on the latest ⁠detailed tax filings show the richest 0.1% of Brazilians having increased their share of national income to a record 13.1% in 2024 from 10.2% in 2020.
evidence.source_title: Brazil's richest captured record income share despite Lula's effort to prioritize the poor

evidence.claim: Convicted (first instance, Judge Sergio Moro, 12 July 2017) of passive corruption and money laundering over a Guarujá triplex allegedly received as a bribe from OAS; sentence 9 years 6 months. Later convictions were annulled by the STF in 2021 (lack of jurisdiction, then a 3-2 bias finding against Moro), so the conviction is no longer valid.
evidence.quote: On 12 July 2017, federal judge Sergio Moro sentenced former president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva to nine years and six months in prison in the criminal case involving the triplex apartment, for the crimes of passive corruption and money laundering.
evidence.source_title: Imprisonment of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva - Wikipedia

evidence.claim: Appeal court (TRF-4) raised the triplex sentence to 12 years 1 month in January 2018 (unanimous); STJ in April 2019 reduced it to 8 years 10 months. Convictions annulled in 2021 on jurisdiction grounds and after the STF found Moro biased; no retrial verdict. Status: conviction annulled.
evidence.quote: In the second instance, the sentence was increased to 12 years and one month, after a unanimous vote.
evidence.source_title: Imprisonment of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva - Wikipedia

evidence.claim: Convicted on 6 Feb 2019 by Judge Gabriela Hardt of graft and money laundering in the Atibaia ranch case (alleged OAS and Odebrecht-paid renovations in exchange for Petrobras contracts); sentence 12 years 11 months, later raised to about 17 years on appeal (Nov 2019). Annulled in 2021 on jurisdiction grounds; the Brasília court later declared the charges extinguished by statute of limitations (Aug 2021). Status: annulled, not retried to verdict.
evidence.quote: On February 6, 2019, Lula was sentenced by Judge Gabriela Hardt, Moro's replacement, to 12 years and 11 months in prison in another case involving a ranch in the city of Atibaia, in the interior of São Paulo. In that case, Lula was accused of receiving kickbacks from OAS and Odebrecht through renovations to the ranch.
evidence.source_title: Imprisonment of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva - Wikipedia

evidence.claim: Imprisoned about 580 days (April 2018 to 8 Nov 2019) after the triplex conviction; released after the STF ended mandatory imprisonment after appeal. Status: conviction then under appeal, not final.
evidence.quote: On 8 November 2019, Lula was released from prison after 580 days when the Brazilian Supreme Court ended mandatory imprisonment of convicted criminals after their first appeal failed.
evidence.source_title: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva - Wikipedia

evidence.claim: Federal prosecutors charged Lula (Dec 2016 onward) with passive corruption and money laundering, alleging Odebrecht kickbacks for an apartment in São Bernardo do Campo and a property for the Lula Institute. Allegation only; charges not adjudicated and the cases were annulled and later dismissed (Lewandowski, Feb 2023).
evidence.quote: He was accused of receiving kickbacks from Odebrecht for the purchase of an apartment in São Bernardo do Campo and another property in São Paulo. According to the indictment, this location was intended for the Lula Institute.
evidence.source_title: Imprisonment of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva - Wikipedia

evidence.claim: Federal Police final report (Dec 2023 per Rio Times) alleged that Odebrecht 'donations' of about R$4 million to the Lula Institute (Dec 2013 to Mar 2014) were drawn from an informal kickback account. Allegation by police; no adjudicated finding; the case was later dismissed by the STF (Feb 2023 Lewandowski dismissal reported for Lula Institute cases).
evidence.quote: “The evidence showed that the funds transferred by Odebrecht under the heading of ‘donations’ were cut from a kind of informal kickback account kept with the construction company, similar to those for the acquisition of the property for the Lula Institute,” said the delegate in the report.
evidence.source_title: Federal Police File Charges against Lula on Alleged R$4 Million Bribe from Odebrecht | The Rio Times

evidence.claim: Lula was found guilty by a lower court of accepting R$3.7 million in bribes in the form of improvements to his beachfront house, made by construction company Grupo Metha, which in turn received Petrobras contracts. Other charges included money laundering, influence peddling and obstruction of justice (per Wikipedia summary).
evidence.quote: Lula was found guilty by the lower court of accepting R$3.7 million in bribes ($940,000 US) in the form of improvements to his beachfront house, made by construction company Grupo Metha
evidence.source_title: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva - Wikipedia

evidence.claim: Lula was reported (2015) to be under formal inquiry by federal prosecutors over whether he improperly used his position to help Odebrecht with lobbying in Africa. Investigation only, not adjudicated.
evidence.quote: Federal prosecutors in Brazil have opened a formal inquiry into whether former President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva improperly used his
evidence.source_title: Brazil opens formal inquiry into Lula's links to Odebrecht

people.name: Mark Zuckerberg
people.descriptor: American technology executive, founder and CEO of Meta
notes: power backfilled from hand-entered reach and authority, not from a research run
people.summary:
Harm tier: ultimate (harm score 0.76; coverage 1.0, confidence 1.0). The largest weight comes from the AI and political-influence rubric (R1, severity 3). Documented items include Meta disbanding its Responsible AI team in November 2023 [R1-E01, https://www.cnbc.com/2023/11/18/facebook-parent-meta-breaks-up-its-responsible-ai-team.html] and planning $65 million in 2026 spending across four super PACs backing AI-friendly state politicians [R1-E03, https://www.nytimes.com/2026/02/18/technology/meta-65-million-election-ai.html]. The scam-advertising and consumer-protection rubric (R3, severity 3) is next. Reuters reported internal estimates that about 10% of 2024 sales came from scam and banned-goods ads [R3-E01, https://www.cnbc.com/2025/11/06/meta-reportedly-projected-10percent-of-2024-sales-came-from-scam-fraud-ads.html]. A New Mexico jury found Meta's senior leadership, including Zuckerberg, made misleading privacy statements, but the penalty is against the company [R3-E07, https://www.cbsnews.com/news/meta-new-mexico-25-billion-privacy-ruling]. Whistleblower-related conduct (R2, severity 1) includes Meta's request for an arbitration order against a former employee [R2-E03, https://awo.agency/articles/sarah-wynn-williams-v-meta-platforms-inc]. The regulatory and testimony items (R4, severity 0) are either company-level or unadjudicated allegations [R4-E03].

Benefit tier: minor_guardian (benefit score 0.15). One item was rated: Meta's Frontier AI Framework says it may withhold high-risk releases [R1-E11, https://www.cdomagazine.tech/aiml/meta-unveils-ai-framework-sets-boundaries-on-release-of-high-risk-ai-systems]. Benefit confidence is low (0.23), so this profile is thin.

Harm and benefit are reported separately and are not netted against each other.

evidence.claim: Meta disbanded its Responsible AI (RAI) team in November 2023, reassigning most members to the Generative AI product division and some to AI Infrastructure.
evidence.quote: Meta has disbanded its Responsible AI division, the team dedicated to regulating the safety of its artificial intelligence ventures as they get developed and deployed, according to a Meta spokesperson.
evidence.source_title: Facebook-parent Meta breaks up its Responsible AI team (CNBC)

evidence.claim: Meta launched a multistate super PAC, the American Technology Excellence Project, to elect state candidates aligned with its views on AI oversight and to fight state-level AI regulation; described as tens of millions of dollars.
evidence.quote: The Facebook-maker is investing "tens of millions" of dollars into a new super PAC to fight state-level tech policy proposals that could stifle AI advancement
evidence.source_title: Meta launches super PAC to fight AI regulation as state policies mount (TechCrunch)

evidence.claim: Meta is preparing to spend $65 million in 2026 across four super PACs to back state politicians friendly to the AI industry, explicitly driven by concern over regulation that could inhibit AI development.
evidence.quote: Meta is preparing to spend $65 million this year to boost state politicians who are friendly to the artificial intelligence industry, beginning this week in Texas and Illinois, according to company representatives.
evidence.source_title: Meta Begins $65 Million Election Push to Advance A.I. Agenda (New York Times)

evidence.claim: Meta's Llama model was used by researchers linked to China's PLA Academy of Military Science to build ChatBIT, a tool for potential military applications; Meta said any PLA use was unauthorized.
evidence.quote: Top Chinese research institutions linked to the People's Liberation Army have used Meta's publicly available Llama model to develop an AI tool for potential military applications
evidence.source_title: EXCLUSIVE: Chinese researchers develop AI model for military use on back of Meta's Llama (Reuters)

evidence.claim: Meta reversed its prohibition on military use of Llama, permitting US government agencies and defense contractors to use its AI models for military and national security purposes.
evidence.quote: Meta will allow U.S. government agencies and contractors working on national security to use its artificial intelligence models for military purposes, the company said on Monday, in a shift from its policy that prohibited the use of its technology for such efforts.
evidence.source_title: Meta Permits Its A.I. Models to Be Used for U.S. Military Purposes (New York Times)

evidence.claim: Meta partnered with defense contractor Anduril on a joint bid for an Army VR/AR contract worth up to about $100 million (EagleEye soldier-enhancement system), which Meta said it would pursue regardless of the award.
evidence.quote: Meta and Anduril have placed a joint bid on an Army contract for VR devices that is worth up to $100 million
evidence.source_title: Meta, Anduril partner on VR, AR project intended for U.S. Army (CNBC)

evidence.claim: Meta's internal GenAI content risk standards permitted AI chatbots to hold 'sensual' romantic chats with minors; Meta confirmed the document's authenticity but called the examples erroneous and removed the passages.
evidence.quote: Meta has since confirmed the document's authenticity but insisted the examples were "erroneous and inconsistent" with company rules.
evidence.source_title: Lawmakers demand probe into Meta's AI policies after Reuters exposé (TNND)

evidence.claim: Meta leadership reportedly pushed to loosen guardrails on sexual content for AI companion bots to maximize engagement despite internal staff warnings about minors' access to hypersexualized personas, per a Wall Street Journal report cited by Senate/House letters.
evidence.quote: Meta staff specifically warned leadership that design choices "gave adult users access to hypersexualized underage AI personas and, conversely, gave underage users access to bots willing to engage in fantasy sex with children. "Despite these internal warnings, Meta reportedly proceeded with deploying these technologies to maximize user
evidence.source_title: U.S. Rep. Kathy Castor Leads Colleagues in Urging Meta Halt Deployment of Companion Bots to Children (Rep. Castor letter)

evidence.claim: Zuckerberg reportedly pushed the company's AI team away from a sequence of cautious rollouts; a Reuters-sourced account says Zuckerberg told staff they were too cautious in rolling out chatbots.
evidence.quote: personally scolded his team internally for being too cautious in its rollout of chatbots, and his team acquiesced by greenlighting shocking content risk standards
evidence.source_title: Experts React to Reuters Reports on Meta's AI Chatbot Policies (TechPolicy.Press)

evidence.claim: Zuckerberg said in 2026 that AI labs have enough incentive to build safely on their own and rejected coordinated slowdown; Meta Superintelligence Labs had engaged independent evaluators in several areas.
evidence.quote: Zuckerberg said on Tuesday that competition and liability give AI companies enough reason to act individually on safety, appearing to break from calls by leaders of top AI firms for a coordinated slowdown in AI development.
evidence.source_title: Meta's Zuckerberg says AI labs have enough incentive to build safely (Reuters)

evidence.claim: Meta's Frontier AI Framework (Feb 2025) says Meta may withhold release of systems rated high- or critical-risk, and commits to halt development if a critical risk cannot be mitigated.
evidence.quote: For systems deemed high-risk, Meta plans to restrict internal access and delay public release until effective mitigations reduce the risk to moderate levels.
evidence.source_title: Meta Unveils AI Framework, Sets Boundaries on Release of High-Risk AI Systems (CDO Magazine)

evidence.claim: Yann LeCun, Meta's chief AI scientist, left in late 2025 after Meta placed him under the new Superintelligence Labs chief and shifted investment from fundamental research toward products; the Scale AI deal ($14.3B for 49% stake) preceded the reorganization.
evidence.quote: On November 20, 2025, Yann LeCun left Meta's chief AI scientist role to start a new firm, Advanced Machine Intelligence Labs.
evidence.source_title: Meta Superintelligence Labs (Wikipedia)

evidence.claim: Meta invested $14.3 billion for a 49% non-voting stake in Scale AI and installed its CEO as head of Superintelligence Labs, a capital allocation to frontier AI development.
evidence.quote: Meta invests $14.3 billion in Scale AI to kick-start superintelligence lab
evidence.source_title: Meta Superintelligence Labs (Wikipedia)

evidence.claim: Meta's Responsible AI team breakup happened amid the 2023 'year of efficiency'; no independent evidence found of a documented safety-based refusal or resignation by Zuckerberg himself.
evidence.quote: The RAI restructuring comes as the Facebook parent nears the end of its "year of efficiency," as CEO Mark Zuckerberg called it
evidence.source_title: Facebook-parent Meta breaks up its Responsible AI team (CNBC)

evidence.claim: Zuckerberg publicly disparaged whistleblowers after Frances Haugen's 2021 disclosures, saying their work was 'used to construct a false narrative'; the claim is recorded as a statement with no documented adverse action against Haugen by Zuckerberg in these sources.
evidence.quote: Mark Zuckerberg disparaged whistleblowers claiming past disclosures were, ''used to construct a false narrative.''
evidence.source_title: Examining whistleblower allegations that Meta buried child safety research (Senate Judiciary testimony, 2025)

evidence.claim: Zuckerberg published a blog post responding to Haugen's testimony, saying the internal research was 'taken out of context' and 'used to construct a false narrative that we don't care.'
evidence.quote: "It's disheartening to see that work taken out of context and used to construct a false narrative that we don't care," Zuckerberg wrote.
evidence.source_title: 4 takeaways from Facebook whistleblower Frances Haugen's testimony

evidence.claim: Meta, with Zuckerberg as CEO, sought an emergency arbitration order barring former global public policy director Sarah Wynn-Williams from making disparaging comments about Meta or promoting her memoir; an arbitrator issued an interim award on 12 March 2025 without her appearing.
evidence.quote: Meta obtained a sweeping emergency gag order from a private arbitrator — issued without Ms. Wynn-Williams being present
evidence.source_title: Sarah Wynn-Williams v Meta Platforms, Inc.

evidence.claim: Wynn-Williams's lawsuit alleges Meta has surveilled her for more than a year, with company representatives attending her public appearances and photographing her to document that she said nothing about Meta. Allegation in a complaint; not adjudicated.
evidence.quote: Meta has surveilled her, with company representatives attending her public appearances and photographing her, "all to document that at each event, Ms. Wynn-Williams said nothing about Meta or her book."
evidence.source_title: 'Careless People' author claims Meta surveilled her for a year to enforce her silence

evidence.claim: Meta says it is seeking $50,000 per violation under the non-disparagement clause; the company's stated position is that the former employee broke a signed agreement. This is a contested allegation by Wynn-Williams.
evidence.quote: The lawsuit says Meta is seeking $50,000 in damages for each time Wynn-Williams purportedly violates the non-disparagement agreement
evidence.source_title: 'Careless People' author claims Meta surveilled her for a year to enforce her silence

evidence.claim: Senator Grassley wrote to Zuckerberg in April 2025 asking whether Meta had changed severance/non-disparagement agreements that restrict whistleblower disclosures to Congress and regulators, citing Meta's threats in a Senate hearing and the Wynn-Williams allegations.
evidence.quote: It's crucial that Meta ensures its employees can provide protected disclosures without illegal restrictions and bullying.
evidence.source_title: Grassley letter to Zuckerberg re whistleblower retaliation

evidence.claim: Meta's Senate testimony-era conduct: Meta's legal and communications staff are alleged to have restricted research; a 2025 Senate hearing whistleblower alleged Meta 'installed monitors from their legal department who routinely altered, blocked, and shut down' research. Allegation from a whistleblower's written testimony; Zuckerberg named only in the context of his public testimony.
evidence.quote: Meta installed monitors from their legal department who rou-tinely altered, blocked, and shut down
evidence.source_title: Examining whistleblower allegations that Meta buried child safety research (Senate Judiciary testimony, 2025)

evidence.claim: Zuckerberg's company later reinstated Trump's accounts in 2023 after the two-year suspension, and Zuckerberg subsequently cultivated a relationship with Trump, including a Mar-a-Lago dinner in late 2024 and a $1M donation to the inauguration fund (reported by news outlets).
evidence.quote: Meta to Pay Trump $25 Million to Settle Lawsuit Over 2021 Ban ... Meta later reinstated Trump's accounts in 2023.
evidence.source_title: Meta to Pay Trump $25 Million to Settle Lawsuit Over 2021 Ban

evidence.claim: A New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay $25 billion after a jury found the company misled consumers in a case tied to Cambridge Analytica; the finding concerns corporate misrepresentations and is not an act by Zuckerberg personally in the sources read.
evidence.quote: Meta Platforms was ordered to pay $25B after a jury found it misled consumers
evidence.source_title: Meta ordered to pay $25B to New Mexico in Cambridge Analytica scandal

evidence.claim: Brazil's electoral court (TSE) ordered Meta in October 2026 to demonstrate equal treatment of Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro in platform visibility, then doubled the daily fine after finding noncompliance; Meta told the court it had complied and denied favoring either candidate. Company-level action; no Zuckerberg-personal act recorded.
evidence.quote: "The continued noncompliance, just a few days before the run-off election, demonstrates that the fine imposed was insufficient," a TSE judge said in Monday's order.
evidence.source_title: Brazilian court orders Meta to prove Lula and Bolsonaro get equal treatment

evidence.claim: Meta, with Zuckerberg in the approval chain, shareholders alleged that directors mishandled the Cambridge Analytica scandal; the case settled for $190 million, with Zuckerberg and directors denying wrongdoing. Settlement of a shareholder suit, no admission of liability.
evidence.quote: Mark Zuckerberg and other Meta Platforms directors agreed to a $190 million settlement of claims they failed to rectify repeated violations of Facebook users' privacy and improperly engineered an accord to shield the billionaire chief executive officer from personal liability.
evidence.source_title: Meta Settles Cambridge Analytica-Related Claims for $190 Million

evidence.claim: Zuckerberg was reported to have posted or been associated with a 2024 Truth Social reference? No—not verified. Omitted.

Meta projected that about 10% of its 2024 overall sales (about $16 billion) came from running online ads for scams and banned goods, per internal documents reviewed by Reuters; Meta said the estimate was 'rough and overly-inclusive'.
evidence.quote: Meta projected that 10% of its overall sales in 2024, or about $16 billion, came from running online ads for scams and banned goods, according to a Thursday report from Reuters.
evidence.source_title: Meta reportedly projected 10% of 2024 sales came from scam, fraud ads (CNBC)

evidence.claim: Reuters reported a December 2024 internal document showing Meta generates roughly $7 billion a year in annualized sales from 'higher risk' scam ads, and an estimated 15 billion such ads shown to users each day.
evidence.quote: The Reuters report cited a December 2024 document that showed how Meta each year generates roughly $7 billion in annualized sales from so-called "higher risk" scam ads, which are promotions that are clearly deceptive. Each day, Meta shows users an estimated 15 billion of these higher risk scam ads
evidence.source_title: Meta reportedly projected 10% of 2024 sales came from scam, fraud ads (CNBC)

evidence.claim: Internal Meta documents reviewed by Reuters show Meta kept doing business with a Chinese advertiser whose ads were more than half in breach of its deceptive-practices rules, and raised its ad prices instead of removing it; Meta calculated about 19% of its China-based ad revenue (more than $3 billion) came from scam, illegal gambling and banned content.
evidence.quote: Still, Meta didn't stop doing business with Beijing Tengze, internal documents show. Instead, Meta started charging the company more to advertise.
evidence.source_title: Meta tolerates rampant ad fraud from China to safeguard billions in revenue (Reuters)

evidence.claim: Reuters reported internal documents showing Meta wanted to minimize 'revenue impact' from cracking down on fraudulent Chinese advertisements.
evidence.quote: Internal company documents show Meta wanted to minimize "revenue impact" caused by cracking down on the scams.
evidence.source_title: Meta tolerates rampant ad fraud from China to safeguard billions in revenue (Reuters)

evidence.claim: The IRS contends Meta lowballed the price of trademarks, customer agreements, software licenses and other rights moved offshore, and in a newer argument says Meta failed to report roughly $54 billion in income and owes nearly $16 billion in back taxes and penalties. Meta has sued the IRS in US Tax Court.
evidence.quote: They say the company failed to report roughly $54 billion in income and owes nearly $16 billion in back taxes and penalties.
evidence.source_title: I.R.S. Tactics Against Meta Open a New Front in the Corporate Tax Fight (New York Times)

evidence.claim: A New Mexico jury found Meta misled consumers about data privacy, with 26 of 29 statements misleading and more than 43 million violations of state consumer protection law; a judge ordered Meta to pay $25 billion (reduced from a calculated $219 billion+).
evidence.quote: Jurors on September 25 found that 26 of 29 statements made by the company and its leadership on those issues were misleading. They said the company had committed more than 43 million violations of New Mexico's consumer protection laws
evidence.source_title: Meta ordered to pay $25 billion to New Mexico after jury finds company misled consumers (Reuters)

evidence.claim: The jury found Meta's 'most senior leadership', including Zuckerberg, made misrepresentations about data privacy policies; the judge wrote the statements were part of 'a coherent strategy designed to mislead the public'.
evidence.quote: The jury found that the company's "most senior leadership," including Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and former chief operating officer Sheryl Sandberg, made misrepresentations about the service's data privacy policies, the judge ruled.
evidence.source_title: Meta ordered to pay $25 billion to New Mexico for misleading consumers (CBS News)

evidence.claim: Kenyan Court of Appeals ruled Meta can be taken to trial in Kenya over the dismissal of 185 content moderators, who say they were unlawfully fired after attempting to form a union, seeking $1.6 billion in compensation; Meta says it requires partners to provide industry-leading working conditions.
evidence.quote: The Court of Appeals in Nairobi has ruled that Meta can be taken to trial in Kenya for the dismissal of 185 content moderators.
evidence.source_title: Meta could face trial in Kenya for firing content moderators (DW)

evidence.claim: A Kenyan former content moderator (Daniel Motaung) alleges Meta and Sama engaged in union-busting; he was fired in 2019 after attempting to start a union and was paid $2.20/hour by Sama. Meta argues it never employed him. These are allegations, not findings.
evidence.quote: Motaung was paid $2.20 per hour as a content moderator for Sama, an outsourcing firm contracted by Facebook to screen posts from across sub-Saharan Africa for harmful content. He was fired in 2019 after attempting to start a union. Motaung accuses both Sama and Meta of union-busting and human trafficking
evidence.source_title: Facebook Shouldn't Silence Whistleblower: Rights Groups (TIME)

evidence.claim: Consumer Federation of America filed a class action against Meta in D.C. Superior Court alleging it misled D.C. users about its role in the fraud economy and charged higher-risk advertisers higher rates rather than banning them. Allegation only.
evidence.quote: Rather than prohibiting advertisers the company itself determined as higher risk, Meta chose to charge these advertisers a higher rate, increasing their profits by allowing higher-risk advertisers access to their users.
evidence.source_title: Consumer Federation of America Sues Meta for Failing to Protect Users from Scam Advertisements

evidence.claim: Meta spent about $7.26 million on federal lobbying in Q1 2026, with filings listing Section 230, youth safety and platform integrity among issues; Meta reported the largest tech lobbying spend in Q2 2026 (nearly $6 million).
evidence.quote: In the First Quarter of 2026 alone, Meta spent $7,260,000 on lobbying, with filings explicitly listing Section 230, youth safety, and platform integrity among the issues lobbied.
evidence.source_title: Meta Verdicts Force Congress to Reckon with Section 230 (Legis1)

evidence.claim: Senator Warren's letter says Meta spent nearly $14 million lobbying Congress and federal agencies in the six months before passage of the 2025 tax law (OBBBA), and asks whether its AI capital spending (about $72 billion in 2025) was deducted under those tax breaks. This is a demand for information, not a finding.
evidence.quote: Then, your company spent nearly $14 million lobbying Congress and federal agencies during the six months leading up to the passage of OBBBA.
evidence.source_title: Letter from Sen. Warren to Meta re AI tax breaks

evidence.claim: Meta agreed to an $18 billion settlement with 48 state attorneys general over claims it built Instagram and Facebook to get kids addicted; the agreement includes usage limits and age assurance commitments.
evidence.quote: Mark Zuckerberg's Meta has agreed to pay $18 billion as part of a historic settlement with 48 state attorneys general who alleged the company purposely built Instagram and Facebook to get kids addicted to the apps.
evidence.source_title: Meta agrees to historic $16.7B settlement over claims social media platforms harm children (NY Post)

evidence.claim: A New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay $567 million into an abatement fund after finding its platform conduct a public nuisance, in addition to $375 million in an earlier child-safety verdict; Meta said it disagreed and will appeal.
evidence.quote: Judge Biedscheid compared Meta to a factory, with advertising and content as its product and "the psychological harm and sexual exploitation of children to be the pollution that must be abated".
evidence.source_title: Meta fined $567m in largest child safety ruling against social media giant (BBC)

evidence.claim: SEC charged Facebook (not Zuckerberg personally) with misleading investors about the risk of user-data misuse; Facebook agreed to pay $100 million without admitting or denying the allegations (settlement, no admission). The SEC complaint alleges the company discovered misuse in 2015 but kept describing the risk as hypothetical for over two years. Zuckerberg is not named as a defendant in this action.
evidence.quote: Facebook has agreed to pay $100 million to settle the charges. [...] Without admitting or denying the SEC’s allegations, Facebook has agreed to the entry of a final judgment ordering a $100 million penalty
evidence.source_title: SEC.gov | Facebook to Pay $100 Million for Misleading Investors About the Risks It Faced From Misuse of User Data

evidence.claim: FTC settlement: Facebook (company, not Zuckerberg personally named in the penalty) agreed to a $5 billion civil penalty over alleged violations of the 2012 FTC consent order, including alleged misrepresentations to users about control over data sharing and facial recognition. Settlement without admission of liability per standard FTC practice; the order was approved 3-2 by the FTC. Zuckerberg was subject to the order's compliance-certification provisions as CEO.
evidence.quote: The FTC also alleges that Facebook misrepresented users’ ability to control the use of facial recognition technology with their accounts.
evidence.source_title: FTC Imposes $5 Billion Penalty and Sweeping New Privacy Restrictions on Facebook

evidence.claim: Zuckerberg told the SEC in a February 2019 deposition that he was probably aware of Cambridge Analytica by 2017, which the reporting says conflicts with his April 2018 congressional testimony and his 2019 House testimony that he first learned of the firm around March 2018 (allegation of misleading testimony; characterized by media, not adjudicated).
evidence.quote: On February 19th, 2019, Zuckerberg told the SEC he was aware of Cambridge Analytica at least as early as 2017.
evidence.source_title: SEC deposition shows Zuckerberg misled Congress about Cambridge Analytica (Engadget)

evidence.claim: In the 2019 House hearing Zuckerberg first said he learned of Cambridge Analytica 'around March of 2018', then corrected himself to say he was aware of it as an entity earlier. Reported as a possible inconsistency; no finding of false statement by a court or regulator.
evidence.quote: I do think I was aware of Cambridge Analytica as an entity earlier. I just don't know if I was tracking how they were using Facebook specifically
evidence.source_title: Read Zuckerberg's 2019 Deposition on Facebook User Data (Business Insider)

evidence.claim: Shareholder derivative suit in Delaware Chancery Court (In re Facebook Inc. Derivative Litigation) alleged Zuckerberg and other directors/officers breached fiduciary duties over oversight of the 2012 FTC order, and alleged insider-trading claims against Zuckerberg over stock sales. Court found the complaint pleaded particularized facts (2023 ruling denying dismissal). Settled in 2025 during trial for $190 million paid by Zuckerberg and directors/officers to Meta, with new governance commitments; no admission of liability reported. Allegations only, not adjudicated.
evidence.quote: The parties settled the matter during trial, with Meta agreeing to pay $190 million and institute new internal policies, which included revisions to its whistleblower program, code of conduct, and insider trading policy. Plaintiffs had sought over $8 billion in damages.
evidence.source_title: Facebook Inc. Derivative Litigation (Analysis Group)

evidence.claim: Delaware derivative plaintiffs alleged Zuckerberg breached fiduciary duties as controller and officer by causing Meta to engage in practices that threatened the value of diversified stockholders' portfolios; court (2023 opinion) denied dismissal, describing the complaint as having particularized facts. Allegations only; unadjudicated on the merits.
evidence.quote: that Zuckerberg and Sandberg face a conflict of interest because the bulk of their wealth is tied up in Meta common stock, which causes their interests to diverge from the interests of Meta’s other stockholders
evidence.source_title: Delaware Court of Chancery opinion, In re Facebook Inc. Derivative Litigation (McRitchie/Meta, 2024)

evidence.claim: In 2016 Zuckerberg proposed a stock reclassification enabling him to sell most of his Facebook stock while retaining voting control; Facebook's board approved it and Zuckerberg formally abstained from the board vote but voted his shares for it at the stockholder meeting.
