people.summary:
Mohammed bin Salman has a harm tier of "major" (final score 0.71, coverage 0.75, confidence 0.75).

The main reasons, in order of weight:

1. Yemen and arms transfers (severity 3, P5). As defence minister he launched Operation Decisive Storm in 2015 [R1-E01, https://www.britannica.com/biography/Mohammed-bin-Salman]. UN experts documented coalition violations of international humanitarian law and named third states supplying weapons [R1-E02, https://www.pbs.org/wgbh/frontline/article/u-s-weapon-saudi-airstrikes-yemen]. Amnesty said a roughly $12.5 billion US arms deal he finalised risked complicity in war crimes [R1-E03, https://www.amnesty.org.uk/knowledge-hub/all-resources/usa-new-saudi-arms-deal-risks-further-human-rights-abuses-yemen].

2. Repression of critics and activists (severity 3, D1). Documented examples include a 34-year sentence for a women's rights activist over tweets [R2-E08, https://www.hrw.org/news/2022/08/19/saudi-arabia-woman-sentenced-34-years-tweets] and detention at unofficial sites [R2-E06, https://www.hrw.org/report/2019/11/04/high-cost-change/repression-under-saudi-crown-prince-tarnishes-reforms].

3. The Khashoggi killing (D3). A declassified US intelligence assessment said he approved the Istanbul operation [R2-E10, https://archive.dni.gov/files/ODNI/documents/assessments/Assessment-Saudi-Gov-Role-in-JK-Death-20210226v2.pdf]. This is an assessment, not a court finding, and Saudi Arabia denies his direct role.

Coverage is limited. Labour abuse evidence was rated insufficient and not scored, and the coercion allegations around the 2017 detentions are unproven and were scored zero under the corruption rubric.

Benefit tier: none_documented (score 0, confidence 0.23). The one benefit-side item, an energy-transition framing for halting Aramco's expansion, was scored zero. No benefit was netted against the harm findings.

evidence.claim: As defense minister, Mohammed bin Salman launched Operation Decisive Storm, a military intervention in Yemen's civil war, in 2015; the Saudi-led coalition he led has been documented by UN experts as committing violations of international humanitarian law.
evidence.quote: As defense minister, Mohammed bin Salman launched Operation Decisive Storm, an intervention in Yemen's civil war to support Yemeni President Abd Rabbuh Mansur Hadi against Houthi insurgents.
evidence.source_title: Mohammed bin Salman | Britannica

evidence.claim: UN Human Rights Council experts found that a Saudi-led coalition airstrike violated international humanitarian law, named third states including the US, France and UK for selling weapons used in the conflict, and recommended continued supply restrictions.
evidence.quote: A team of investigators appointed by the U.N. Human Rights Council found that the airstrike violated international humanitarian law and details numerous similar incidents in Yemen that may amount to war crimes.
evidence.source_title: What a Report on War Crimes Means for U.S.-Saudi Arms Deals (FRONTLINE/PBS)

evidence.claim: Mohammed bin Salman and Trump finalised a roughly $12.5 billion arms deal at the White House; Amnesty said the deal risked complicity in war crimes in Yemen because US-made arms were used in strikes on civilians.
evidence.quote: By finalising weapons deals worth billions of dollars with the government of Saudi Arabia, the Trump administration puts the U.S. at risk of being complicit in war crimes committed in Yemen.
evidence.source_title: USA: New Saudi arms deal risks further human rights abuses in Yemen (Amnesty)

evidence.claim: A US Congress-related account reports the crown prince was the subject of a 2019 meeting with a senator who cited Khashoggi's death and Yemen war violations while lawmakers sought to block US arms sales to Saudi Arabia; the crown prince reportedly expressed desire to improve relations with the legislature.
evidence.quote: He cited Khashoggi's death, as well as the violations of international humanitarian law in Yemen described in the recent U.N. report.
evidence.source_title: What a Report on War Crimes Means for U.S.-Saudi Arms Deals (FRONTLINE/PBS)

evidence.claim: US Commerce authorized Saudi AI company HUMAIN, chaired by Mohammed bin Salman, to buy up to 35,000 NVIDIA GB300-equivalent chips under security and reporting conditions; HUMAIN plans about 3GW of data centre capacity by 2030.
evidence.quote: Launched in May 2025 and chaired by Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Humain is owned by the kingdom's Public Investment Fund and plans to develop about 3GW of data centre capacity by 2030 and more than 6GW by 2034.
evidence.source_title: Saudi Arabia's Humain expands Nvidia deal with 84MW AI computing plan (The National)

evidence.claim: Saudi Arabia has no binding AI-specific statute and has not announced a legislative process to enact one; AI is governed through guidance instruments.
evidence.quote: No — Saudi Arabia has no AI law. As of 31 July 2026 there is no binding AI-specific statute in the Kingdom, and no legislative process to enact one has been announced
evidence.source_title: How Saudi Arabia Regulates AI: SDAIA's Framework

evidence.claim: Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry ordered Aramco to halt its oil expansion plan and target maximum sustained capacity of 12 million bpd, 1 million bpd below the 2020 target of 13 million bpd that the crown prince had pushed.
evidence.quote: Saudi Arabia's government on Tuesday ordered state oil company Aramco to halt its oil expansion plan and to target a maximum sustained production capacity of 12 million barrels per day (bpd), 1 million bpd below a target announced in 2020.
evidence.source_title: Saudi Arabia orders Aramco to lower its oil capacity target (Globe and Mail)

evidence.claim: Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman warned during Biden's July 2022 visit that Riyadh 'will not have any more capability to increase production' after reaching the 13 million bpd goal that the kingdom had ordered Aramco to pursue in March 2020.
evidence.quote: Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman during U.S. President Joe Biden's visit to the kingdom in July 2022 warned that Riyadh "will not have any more capability to increase production" after it reached the now-scrapped 13 million-bpd goal. The kingdom had ordered Aramco to expand to that level in March 2020
evidence.source_title: Saudi Arabia orders Aramco to lower its oil capacity target (Globe and Mail)

evidence.claim: Washington Institute analysis reports, citing Reuters industry sources, that the cut to Aramco's expansion came from the top, i.e. from the crown prince, and was at least six months in the making.
evidence.quote: The sources indicated that "the decision came from the top," suggesting it was taken by the kingdom's de facto leader, Crown Prince Muhammad bin Salman, widely known as MbS.
evidence.source_title: Saudi Arabia's Shock Cut in Planned Oil Expansion (Washington Institute)

evidence.claim: Saudi energy minister said Aramco postponed the capacity investment because of the transition to renewables and that energy security will depend on renewables; the expansion halt was framed as an energy-transition decision.
evidence.quote: I think we postponed this [Aramco capacity] investment simply because … we're transitioning.
evidence.source_title: Saudi energy minister pins Aramco's oil capacity halt on green transition (CNBC)

evidence.claim: Mohammed bin Salman said that if Iran developed a nuclear bomb Saudi Arabia would follow suit as soon as possible, a statement that US lawmakers cite in opposing a US-Saudi civil nuclear deal that could allow domestic enrichment.
evidence.quote: Saudi Arabia does not want to acquire any nuclear bombs. But without a doubt, if Iran developed a nuclear bomb, we will follow suit as soon as possible.
evidence.source_title: U.S.-Saudi nuclear power deal faces pushback over potential weapons risks (PBS NewsHour)

evidence.claim: US intelligence community assessed that Saudi Arabia has not ruled out developing a nuclear weapons program, per classified documents provided to Congress, as the US agreed to assist a civilian nuclear program.
evidence.quote: Classified documents provided to Congress include an assessment by the U.S. intelligence community that Saudi Arabia has not ruled out the option of developing a nuclear weapons program
evidence.source_title: Saudis have not ruled out developing nuclear weapons, U.S. intelligence assesses (Washington Post)

evidence.claim: Saudi Arabia reportedly sought to buy Israeli hacking technology; the Khashoggi-related spyware issue involves Saudi government use of NSO's Pegasus against Khashoggi associates, per court filings and reporting.
evidence.quote: Saudi authorities had used the Israeli-made software to spy on the dissident.
evidence.source_title: Pegasus (spyware) - Wikipedia

evidence.claim: A 2021 US ODNI report found Mohammed bin Salman had ordered the assassination of journalist Jamal Khashoggi; this is a surveillance/repression-adjacent atrocity record.
evidence.quote: A 2021 report by the United States Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI) found that Mohammed had ordered the assassination of journalist Jamal Khashoggi.
evidence.source_title: Mohammed bin Salman - Wikipedia

evidence.claim: Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry halted Aramco's capacity expansion plan, a move that analysts saw as a reversal of the kingdom's expansion push; the cut was reported as a 'U-turn'.
evidence.quote: Riyadh's January 30 announcement that it had canceled its plan to increase maximum sustainable production capacity from 12 to 13 million barrels per day (bpd) by 2027
evidence.source_title: Saudi Arabia's Shock Cut in Planned Oil Expansion (Washington Institute)

evidence.claim: Saudi Arabia's Climate Scorecard advocacy calls for Aramco, chaired by the crown prince, to halt new oil and gas field development; this is an NGO demand, not an act by the subject.
evidence.quote: The Kingdom should mandate that Saudi Aramco immediately halt new oil and gas field development and reduce production by 10% every 5 years, reaching zero new extraction by 2045.
evidence.source_title: Saudi Arabia: Plan to Phase Out Fossil Fuel by 2030 (Climate Scorecard)

evidence.claim: Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman led an anti-corruption committee whose campaign from 4 Nov 2017 detained hundreds of princes, ministers and businessmen, many held at the Ritz-Carlton Riyadh; most were released after financial settlements.
evidence.quote: The campaign, launched in November 2017 by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, saw hundreds of elite princes, ministers and businessmen held at the luxury Ritz-Carlton hotel in the Saudi capital Riyadh.
evidence.source_title: Saudi Arabia says 'anti-corruption' campaign ends after netting billions | Middle East Eye

evidence.claim: Detainees in the Ritz-Carlton purge reportedly were beaten and tortured; the government denied torture. Seventeen were hospitalized and one died in custody, per NYT reporting cited by HRW.
evidence.quote: On March 12, the New York Times reported that unnamed sources said 17 detainees–among them princes, businessmen, and former and current government officials–held at the Ritz Carlton Hotel in Riyadh in November 2017 had required hospitalization for physical abuse and that one had died in custody.
evidence.source_title: 2018 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: Saudi Arabia - US State Department

evidence.claim: US intelligence official and former senior US officials told NBC that Ritz-Carlton detainees were coerced, abused and tortured; Saudi Arabia denied any abuse or torture. Detainees were told to sign away assets to be released.
evidence.quote: A U.S. intelligence official and two former senior U.S. government officials told NBC News that the detainees were coerced, abused and tortured.
evidence.source_title: How a Saudi royal crushed his rivals in a 'shakedown' at the Ritz-Carlton

evidence.claim: Former Ritz-Carlton detainees said in November 2020 that they were beaten and intimidated under the supervision of two ministers described as close confidantes of the crown prince, whom the reporting says ordered the purge; the Guardian reporting is cited via Wikipedia.
evidence.quote: The detainees claim that they were beaten and intimidated by authorities under the supervision of two ministers, who were both close confidantes of the crown prince Mohammed bin Salman who ordered the purge.
evidence.source_title: 2017–2019 Saudi Arabian purge - Wikipedia

evidence.claim: Human Rights Watch reported that HRW obtained credible evidence in Nov 2018 that Saudi authorities tortured at least four women activists in detention, including electric shocks, whippings, waterboarding and sexual assault allegations.
evidence.quote: In November 2018, Human Rights Watch obtained credible evidence that Saudi authorities tortured at least four women activists in detention. The torture included electric shocks, whippings, waterboarding, and sexual harassment and assault including touching and groping.
evidence.source_title: The High Cost of Change: Repression Under Saudi Crown Prince Tarnishes Reforms | HRW

evidence.claim: HRW report documents detention of prominent women's rights activists at an unofficial 'hotel' or 'guesthouse' in summer 2018, and reports that authorities held detainees in unofficial places of detention.
evidence.quote: as well as the detention of prominent women’s rights activists at a “hotel” or “guesthouse” during the summer of 2018.
evidence.source_title: The High Cost of Change: Repression Under Saudi Crown Prince Tarnishes Reforms | HRW

evidence.claim: Sept 2017 arrests of at least 16 people deemed critical of bin Salman, who had advocated mild political reforms, per an advocacy statement to the UN HRC.
evidence.quote: In September 2017, authorities arrested at least 16 people deemed to be critical of bin Salman. The detainees had advocated for mild political reforms.
evidence.source_title: HRC Written Statement: Under the Guise of Countering Corruption, Saudi Arabia Suppresses Rights and Freedoms | ADHRB

evidence.claim: Crown Prince's government: the Saudi Specialized Criminal Court sentenced Salma al-Shehab, a women's rights activist and academic, to 34 years in prison in August 2022 after an appeal, based on tweets and retweets supporting women's rights; the initial sentence was six years.
evidence.quote: On August 9, 2022, the appeals court ruled, instead, to increase her sentence, finding that the original sentence failed to achieve “restraint and deterrence.”
evidence.source_title: Saudi Arabia: Woman Sentenced to 34 Years for Tweets | Human Rights Watch

evidence.claim: Prosecution sought the death penalty against activists including Israa al-Ghomgham for participation in peaceful protests; in Jan 2019 authorities dropped the death-penalty request for her.
evidence.quote: On 31 January 2019, Saudi authorities dropped the prosecutor's request for al-Ghomgham to be sentenced to death.
evidence.source_title: Israa al-Ghomgham - Wikipedia

evidence.claim: US intelligence (ODNI, declassified Feb 2021) assessed that the Crown Prince approved an operation in Istanbul to capture or kill journalist Jamal Khashoggi, based on his control of decision-making, his support for violent measures against dissidents abroad, and absolute control of security and intelligence since 2017.
evidence.quote: We assess that Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Muhammad bin Salman approved an operation in Istanbul, Turkey to capture or kill Saudi journalist Jamal Khashoggi.
evidence.source_title: ODNI Assessment: Saudi Government's Role in the Killing of Jamal Khashoggi (declassified)

evidence.claim: CIA assessed with high confidence that the Crown Prince ordered Khashoggi's assassination; the Saudi embassy called the claims false; Trump disputed the assessment.
evidence.quote: The CIA has concluded that Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman ordered the assassination of journalist Jamal Khashoggi in Istanbul last month, contradicting the Saudi government's claims that he was not involved in the killing
evidence.source_title: CIA concludes Saudi crown prince ordered Jamal Khashoggi's assassination - The Washington Post

evidence.claim: Saud al-Qahtani, a close adviser to the crown prince, was fired over Khashoggi's killing and was sanctioned by the US; he was reportedly one of the masked interrogators in the women's rights activist case.
evidence.quote: Al-Qahtani was later sanctioned by the U.S. for his alleged role in the murder of Saudi writer Jamal Khashoggi in the kingdom's consulate in Turkey.
evidence.source_title: Saudi women's rights activist sentenced to nearly 6 years in prison | PBS News

evidence.claim: Crown Prince publicly said the women's rights activist arrests were 'not about women asking for the right to drive' (Bloomberg interview, 2018), per Al Jazeera.
evidence.quote: Speaking to Bloomberg in 2018, MBS said the arrests were “not about women asking for the right to drive … It’s nothing at all to do with that.”
evidence.source_title: Mohammed bin Salman: The dark side of Saudi Arabia's crown prince | Al Jazeera

evidence.claim: Saudi court ordered the Ritz-Carlton-era prosecutions to be handled through specialized criminal units for detainees who did not reach financial settlements; King Salman ordered specialized PPO departments for corruption cases.
evidence.quote: On January 28, local media reported that the Supreme Judicial Council had established two criminal units in the criminal courts of Riyadh and Jeddah to review cases of detainees arrested in the November 2017 anticorruption campaign who did not reach financial settlements with the government.
evidence.source_title: 2018 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: Saudi Arabia - US State Department

evidence.claim: Saudi court under the Specialized Criminal Court (2022) and Amnesty: harsh sentences against Shia and activists; Amnesty documented a pattern of repression through the SCC.
evidence.quote: Amnesty International has also documented a pattern of repression targeting the Shi’a community in Saudi Arabia, namely through the Specialized Criminal Court that has issued harsh prison and death sentences following grossly unfair trials, marred by allegations of torture and other ill-treatment during detention which the prosecution has systematically failed to investigate.
evidence.source_title: SAUDI ARABIA: Release Activist Jailed 34 Years for Tweets

evidence.claim: Saudi Oger, a now-liquidated construction firm, was estimated by the Riyadh Executive Court in 2019 to owe about SAR 2.6 billion (~US$693 million) in unpaid wages and benefits; at least 21,000 workers from the Philippines, Nepal, Bangladesh and Pakistan were reported owed wages by Saudi Oger and a second firm. The source does not tie this directly to MBS personally; it is a PIF-era megaproject contractor context.
evidence.quote: The Executive Court in Riyadh estimated in 2019 that the now-liquidated Saudi Oger owes an estimated SAR 2.6 billion (about US$693 million) in unpaid wages and other benefits to workers. Based on news sources and announcements from the migrants' countries of origin, at least 21,000 workers just from the Philippines, Nepal, Bangladesh, and Pakistan are owed wages by these two companies.
evidence.source_title: Saudi Arabia: Migrant Workers' Long Overdue Wages at Risk | Human Rights Watch

evidence.claim: Of 8,830 Filipino claimants owed wages by Saudi Oger, only 1,352 had been compensated, receiving about SAR 69 million (~US$18.4 million) out of an estimated SAR 2.6 billion, as reported by BWI citing workers' letters.
evidence.quote: Of the 8,830 claimants, only 1,352 have been compensated, receiving a total of SAR 69.050.811 (USD 18.390.201 out of an estimated SAR 2.6 billion – about USD 693 million), while thousands remain unpaid.
evidence.source_title: Saudi Arabia: Worker Abuses Persist Under FIFA's Watch - BWI

evidence.claim: Human Rights Watch reported that PIF-funded giga-project contractors, including NEOM, exploit migrant workers; a NEOM worker said his labor-supply company did not allow workers to change jobs and workers paid recruitment fees.
evidence.quote: Even at these giga-projects' nascent stages, this report reveals that PIF-funded businesses and projects are among those exploiting and abusing migrant workers, including in NEOM, a PIF-funded giga-project that is being built in the northwest of Saudi Arabia
evidence.source_title: "Die First, and I'll Pay You Later": Saudi Arabia's 'Giga-Projects' Built on Widespread Labor Abuses | HRW

evidence.claim: BWI's survey of 193 migrant workers found debt bondage (85%), passport/ID withholding (65%), restrictions on leaving contracts (63%) and wage theft (46%); BWI filed an ILO forced labour complaint in June 2024, admissibility upheld January 2025. The Saudi government contests the complaint in ILO proceedings.
evidence.quote: BWI's survey of 193 workers, for example, found experiences of debt bondage (85% of respondents), withholding passports and identity documents (65% of respondents), restrictions on terminating or leaving contracts (63% of respondents), and wage theft (46% of respondents).
evidence.source_title: Saudi Arabia: BWI files ILO forced labour complaint ahead of 2034 FIFA World Cup bid

evidence.claim: Saudi authorities detained dozens of princes and businessmen at the Ritz-Carlton Riyadh from November 2017 and pressured them to hand over assets to the state in exchange for release, outside a recognizable legal process; Human Rights Watch reports most reached settlements, while some remained detained without charge.
evidence.quote: While the people were in detention, the authorities pressured them to hand over assets to the state in exchange for their release, outside of any recognizable legal process.
evidence.source_title: Saudi Arabia: New Mass Corruption Arrests | Human Rights Watch

evidence.claim: A New York Times investigation (as reported by Al Jazeera) found at least 17 Ritz-Carlton detainees were subjected to physical abuse and hospitalised while the government pressured them to sign over large assets; Saudi officials denied the allegations. Relatives said 'We signed away everything.'
evidence.quote: "Relatives of some of the detainees said they were deprived of sleep, roughed up and interrogated with their heads covered while the government pressured them to sign over large assets," the article, published on Sunday, said.
evidence.source_title: Saudi Arabia used abuse to seize billions during purge: NYT | Al Jazeera

evidence.claim: Saudi authorities said settlements with 87 detainees recovered about $107 billion in real estate, companies, cash and other assets; the Public Prosecutor rejected settlements with 56 people. Official figures; independent reporting questioned the numbers.
evidence.quote: Settlements were made with 87 individuals resulting in the recovery of $107 billion in the form of real estate, companies, cash, and other assets.
evidence.source_title: 2017–2019 Saudi Arabian purge - Wikipedia

evidence.claim: Saudi authorities said the Ritz-Carlton purge netted over 400bn riyals forfeited by as many as 325 people detained; government claimed settlements recovered over $100bn.
evidence.quote: He said 400bn riyals had been forfeited by as many as 325 people detained in the Ritz Carlton hotel in Riyadh, where their personal finances
evidence.source_title: Saudi Arabia claims anti-corruption purge recouped $100bn

evidence.claim: Human Rights Watch reported that PIF's chairman-era projects had workers facing wage delays and that the Saudi government's standards were not enforced; the Saudi Ministry of Human Resources said it was making progress on repayment after a complaint at the ILO.
evidence.quote: While some repayment has begun almost a decade later, Human Rights Watch research shows that the process has been rife with problems.
evidence.source_title: Saudi Arabia: ILO Forced Labor Complaint a Wake-Up Call - Sport & Rights Alliance

evidence.claim: ALQST reported that Saudi authorities illegally displaced local Huwaitat tribes for NEOM without adequate compensation; a NEOM resident was evicted without prior consultation with about $3,000 offered per family.
evidence.quote: The eviction order came without prior consultation. The compensation on offer was approximately $3,000 per family.
evidence.source_title: NEOM Human Cost: Death Sentences, 21,000 Worker Deaths & Tri

evidence.claim: Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, chaired by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, transferred 4% of Aramco shares to the PIF in a restructuring move; the transfer was announced by MBS as chairman of the PIF board.
evidence.quote: Saudi Crown Prince and Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Public Investment Fund (PIF), Mohammed Bin Salman, has announced the transfer of 4 percent of the Saudi Arabian Oil Company's (Aramco) shares to the Public Investment Fund (PIF).
evidence.source_title: Saudi's Crown Prince transfers 4% of Aramco shares to PIF

evidence.claim: Following the November 2017 anti-corruption committee chaired by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, 381 people were summoned; the Royal Court said 87 agreed to settlements (forfeiture of real estate, companies, cash and other assets), 8 refused and 56 were denied settlement due to existing charges. The government said it recovered about $106-107bn. These are government-reported figures; settlements were made outside a published legal process (status: settlements, some reportedly under coercion, unproven by court).
evidence.quote: The Royal Court said a committee led by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman had recovered $107bn (£81bn) in settlements including property, companies and cash.
evidence.source_title: Saudi Arabia ends major anti-corruption campaign (BBC)

evidence.claim: Human Rights Watch reported that Saudi authorities reportedly pressured Ritz-Carlton detainees to hand over assets to the state in exchange for release outside any recognizable legal process; allegation, not adjudicated.
evidence.quote: While in detention at the Ritz-Carlton, authorities pressured detainees to hand over assets to the state in exchange for their release outside of any recognizable legal process, and many reportedly made deals.

evidence.claim: Allegation (unproven, reported by New York Times in March 2018): Saudi authorities used physical abuse to coerce corruption detainees to hand over assets; at least 17 people required hospitalization, including Maj. Gen. Ali al-Qahtani who later died in detention. The government denied torture allegations, saying they were investigated and found unsubstantiated.
evidence.quote: In March 2018, the New York Times reported that Saudi authorities used physical abuse to coerce so-called corruption detainees to hand over assets following their detention in the Ritz-Carton hold in early November 2017. The report stated that at least 17 people required hospitalization for abuse in detention
evidence.source_title: The High Cost of Change (HRW)

evidence.claim: Allegation (unproven): former Ritz-Carlton detainees told the Guardian in November 2020 that they were beaten and coerced by authorities supervised by two ministers described as close confidantes of MBS, who ordered the purge; the Saudi government denies torture allegations.
evidence.quote: The detainees claim that they were beaten and intimidated by authorities under the supervision of two ministers, who were both close confidantes of the crown prince Mohammed bin Salman who ordered the purge.
evidence.source_title: 2017–2019 Saudi Arabian purge (Wikipedia)

evidence.claim: US Director of National Intelligence declassified assessment (Feb 2021) that Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman approved an operation in Istanbul to capture or kill journalist Jamal Khashoggi. This is an intelligence assessment, not a court finding; Saudi Arabia has denied the Crown Prince's direct role.
evidence.quote: We assess that Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Muhammad bin Salman approved an operation in Istanbul, Turkey to capture or kill Saudi journalist Jamal Khashoggi.
evidence.source_title: ODNI Assessment: Saudi Gov Role in JK Death (declassified 26 Feb 2021)

evidence.claim: Civil lawsuit by Khashoggi's fiancee against the Crown Prince was dismissed on 6 Dec 2022 by a US district judge who found the Crown Prince entitled to head-of-state immunity as sitting prime minister, after the Biden administration's suggestion of immunity; the judge noted 'credible allegations' of his involvement. No finding on the merits.
evidence.quote: Judge says Mohammed bin Salman entitled to sovereign immunity despite 'credible allegations' of involvement in journalist's murder.
evidence.source_title: US judge dismisses case against Saudi crown prince over Khashoggi killing (Guardian)

evidence.claim: Human Rights Watch (2024) reports that the Crown Prince, as PIF chairman, circumvented PIF board safeguards in 2020 by going directly to the King to secure a decree allowing investments that the board had opposed; this is a documented account from a public Congressional testimony, not an adjudicated finding.
evidence.quote: This move was opposed by the board of directors, and MBS went beyond the board, circumvented these safeguards, and went directly to the King.
evidence.source_title: Examining the Saudi Arabian Public Investment Fund (US Senate hearing, testimony of HRW's Joey Shea)

evidence.claim: Allegation: Human Rights Watch reports overlapping PIF board appointments to other state and ostensibly private institutions raise conflict-of-interest concerns; the PIF is chaired by the Crown Prince; no adjudicated conflict finding.
evidence.quote: The overlapping appointments of PIF board members to other prominent state and ostensibly private institutions raises serious concerns about conflicts between these individuals' public responsibilities and personal interest, particularly in a political environment without any meaningful avenues available to the public to seek redress for failed policies, mismanagement, and corruption.
evidence.source_title: The Man Who Bought The World (HRW, 2024)

evidence.claim: Reported (unproven) that Crown Prince is pursuing corruption and disloyalty charges and a $15bn settlement demand against former Crown Prince Mohammed bin Nayef, per a Washington Post report cited by Middle East Eye; no adjudicated finding.
evidence.quote: Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman is in the process of levelling corruption and disloyalty charges against his predecessor Mohammed bin Nayef, in a bid to shore up his rule
evidence.source_title: Saudi crown prince preparing new charges against Mohammed bin Nayef (Middle East Eye)

evidence.claim: Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations subpoenaed the PIF in Sept 2023 after it refused to voluntarily comply with disclosure requests; the PIF is chaired by the Crown Prince. Investigation of an institution, not a finding against the named person.
evidence.quote: Chamber's investigations committee is targeting the PIF after it refused to voluntarily comply with requests for disclosure.
evidence.source_title: Senate subpoenas Saudi's $700bn sovereign wealth fund (Guardian)

people.summary:
Harm tier: minor (harm score 0.18; coverage 1.0; confidence 0.875). Benefit tier: none_documented (benefit confidence 0.33). No benefit evidence was found or rated. This is not a negative finding, and benefit is not netted against harm.

The main reasons for the harm tier, in order of weight:

1. Employment disputes (R2, severity 1). A former employee's federal suit alleges harassment, pregnancy discrimination and retaliation. Donaldson was not named as a defendant [R2-E01, https://abcnews.com/US/mrbeasts-company-sued-alleged-sexual-harassment-wrongful-termination/story?id=132293451]. The company calls the claims false [R3-E11]. A co-venture partner's $100M+ countersuit alleges bullying tactics [R2-E03].

2. Beast Games labor and tax-credit allegations (R3, severity 1). A class action alleges wage, break and misclassification violations [R3-E01, https://variety.com/2024/digital/news/mrbeast-amazon-sued-beast-games-contestants-class-action-1236148181; R3-E03]. It also alleges misstated labor costs for Nevada tax credits [R3-E04, R3-E05]. A CARU decision found Feastables misrepresented a taste test to children [R3-E09, https://bbbprograms.org/media/newsroom/decisions/mrbeast-feastables], the one adjudicated finding among these items.

3. Other rubrics (R1 and R4, severity 0). Investment and AI partnership announcements were documented but did not score as harm [R1-E01, R1-E03].

Most harm evidence consists of allegations or contested claims, not findings, so confidence in the tier is moderate.

evidence.claim: Beast Industries received a $200 million investment from BitMine Immersion Technologies (Tom Lee), an ethereum treasury company, announced January 2026; BitMine chairman said the company is pursuing DeFi incorporation into a planned financial services platform.

people.name: Rutger Bregman
notes: power backfilled from hand-entered reach and authority, not from a research run
people.summary:
Rutger Bregman's harm profile is rated "not_a_dick," with a harm score of 0.0, confidence of about 0.62, and full coverage across all four rubrics. Every rubric scored severity 0, so no item reached a harm threshold.

The most-cited material is confrontational public rhetoric. In a 2019 Fox News exchange, he called Tucker Carlson "a millionaire funded by billionaires" [R2-E02, https://www.vox.com/2019/2/20/18233556/tucker-carlson-rutger-bregman-nowthis-dutch-historian]. In a 2025 dispute with journalist Tim Schwab, Bregman called Schwab "the most dishonest" [R2-E07, https://x.com/rutgerbregman/status/1924948465315913948]. Former advisor Anita Naidu reports being blocked on social media after her critique, which Bregman's side has not confirmed [R2-E06, https://www.linkedin.com/posts/anita-naidu_rutger-bregman-apologizes-for-racist-essay-activity-7331101621377978370-lWPf]. No sanction by Bregman is documented.

Funding disclosure is contested. Schwab reported that the School for Moral Ambition did not initially disclose a $75,000 Gates Foundation grant [R4-E01, https://timschwab.substack.com/p/rutger-bregman-apologizes-for-racist]. Bregman's agent said the grant was disclosed on the website, and Gates' site lists it. No regulator or court has made a finding.

Benefit profile: none_documented, benefit score 0.0. No costly risk-reducing act was rated. His AI-regulation advocacy [R1-E01, https://rutgerbregman.substack.com/p/an-inconvenient-truth-about-ai] and donation claims [R1-E03, https://www.moralambition.org/about-us] were treated as advocacy or self-description, not benefit. This absence is not a negative finding.

Harm and benefit are reported separately and do not offset each other.

evidence.claim: Publicly argued in a June 2026 Substack essay that AI safety is under-prioritized, calling it a 'problem of the left' and demanding 'safety standards' and 'international coalitions' from governments; this is advocacy for regulation, not an executed act against his own interest.
evidence.quote: Today, AI denial is a problem of the left, and the consequences could be even more disastrous.
evidence.source_title: An Inconvenient Truth About AI - Rutger Bregman

evidence.claim: Used his Substack essay to praise Anthropic's decision not to release its Mythos model to the public, and to argue that corporate conscience is not a substitute for regulation.
evidence.quote: Yes, a private company, with billions of dollars to be made and with no regulator forcing its hand, concluded that one of its own products was so dangerous it should not be sold to the general public. There is no regulator and no legislation. There was simply a moment of conscience inside the company. I am glad that conscience exists! But conscience is not a policy.
evidence.source_title: An Inconvenient Truth About AI - Rutger Bregman

evidence.claim: Says the School for Moral Ambition, which he co-founded, is funded by individuals and foundations, and that he donates all proceeds from his book Moral Ambition to the movement; the organization's own statement, so treated as self-description.
evidence.quote: Rutger Bregman donates all proceeds from Moral Ambition to the movement, and we publish our largest funders openly.
evidence.source_title: About us | The School for Moral Ambition

evidence.claim: At the 2019 World Economic Forum in Davos, publicly told a panel of elites that tax avoidance by the rich was the real issue and that the topic was being avoided; this is a public statement, not a P1-P5 risk-reducing act, and is recorded only as context.
evidence.quote: I mean, almost no one raises the real issue of tax avoidance right and of the rich just not paying their fair share.
evidence.source_title: Rutger Bregman tells Davos to talk about tax: 'This is not rocket science' (Guardian News)

evidence.claim: Bregman, in a 2019 Fox News pre-recorded interview, told host Tucker Carlson he was 'a millionaire funded by billionaires' and said Fox would not cover tax-evasion stories; Carlson responded with insults and the segment was not aired. Bregman publicly released the footage. This is an exchange with a media host, not a documented act of retaliation by Bregman.
evidence.quote: Historian Rutger Bregman, who became a viral sensation for his blunt talk on taxing the rich, was recently interviewed by Fox News host Tucker Carlson.
evidence.source_title: Tucker Carlson says rant Fox News refused to air 'was genuinely heartfelt' (MarketWatch)

evidence.claim: Bregman said of Carlson on air: 'You're a millionaire funded by billionaires' (confrontational criticism of a media figure; no documented sanction by Bregman).
evidence.quote: BREGMAN: You're a millionaire funded by billionaires. That's what you are.
evidence.source_title: Tucker Carlson, Rutger Bregman clash (Vox)

evidence.claim: Bregman, after the 2025 Reith Lecture, publicly accused the BBC of censoring a line calling Trump 'the most openly corrupt president' and said the decision was made against his wishes; he was describing the BBC's action, not an act of his own against critics. Bregman's own words also called Trump a 'modern-day Caligula' and a 'convicted reality star' (rhetoric with no documented follow-up by him).
evidence.quote: He went on to describe Trump as a "modern-day Caligula", saying: "He surrounds himself with loyalists, grifters and sycophants."
evidence.source_title: Historian Rutger Bregman criticises BBC for removing Donald Trump line from Radio 4's Reith Lecture (BBC News)

evidence.claim: In 2011 Bregman wrote an opinion piece in De Volkskrant that journalist Tim Schwab describes as using racial slurs (including 'niggabitch' and 'negro') to argue Rihanna was too sensitive to racism. This is rhetoric about a group, not a documented act of force or sanction; Bregman later apologised for it.
evidence.quote: In 2011, Dutch writer Rutger Bregman deployed a litany of racial slurs, like “niggabitch” and “negro,” in an essay that argued that Rihanna is too sensitive to racism.
evidence.source_title: Racism, Rihanna----and Rutger Bregman (Tim Schwab Substack)

evidence.claim: In response to a critical investigation by Tim Schwab, Bregman's comment on Schwab's piece described it as misinformation and called it 'a personal attack'; Schwab reports that he deleted Bregman's roughly 1500-word comment because most of it was a personal attack on others. Schwab's account of this is an opinion/advocacy-side source; the claim of a personal attack is contested.
evidence.quote: I had to delete his comment—-actually a 1500-word commentary—because the vast majority of it wasn't about his reckoning with his racist essay. Most of it was a personal attack on others, written through misinformation and mistruths.
evidence.source_title: Rutger Bregman apologizes for racist essay about Rihanna. Then lashes out (Tim Schwab Substack)

evidence.claim: Bregman, responding to former advisor Anita Naidu's critique of the School for Moral Ambition, publicly called her approach to partners 'unethical behaviour' and said she was reaching out to partners behind their backs; Naidu's account says Bregman blocked her on social media after she published her critique.
evidence.quote: Rutger Bregman blocked me after I exposed elitism and ...
evidence.source_title: Rutger Bregman blocked me after I exposed elitism and racism (LinkedIn post by Anita Naidu)

evidence.claim: Bregman, in a comment on Schwab's investigation, responded to a critic by saying Schwab was 'the most dishonest and...' (a personal attack on a journalist), per a post on his own X account. Only the search snippet was seen; the full statement was not read.
evidence.quote: Tim Schwab is the most dishonest and
evidence.source_title: Rutger Bregman on X (search snippet)

evidence.claim: Bregman publicly described the Schwab investigation as dishonest after Schwab reported the School for Moral Ambition had received a $75,000 Gates Foundation grant, and Bregman's school said the funding was not initially disclosed; Schwab reports the response he got did not answer whether Bregman had personal financial ties. Reporting on funding disclosure, not a sanction against critics.
evidence.quote: According to Strunk, the The School for Moral Ambition has received $75,000 from the Gates Foundation to date, which she quickly minimized as a tiny part of the non-profit’s budget.
evidence.source_title: He built a brand criticizing billionaires. Are billionaires now bankrolling his work? (Tim Schwab Substack)

evidence.claim: At Davos 2019, Bregman told business and political elites to talk about taxes rather than philanthropy and called the rest 'bullshit' in his opinion; this is rhetoric directed at elites with no documented use of force or sanction against them.
evidence.quote: "Taxes, taxes, taxes. All the rest is bullshit in my opinion."
evidence.source_title: Dutch historian Rutger Bregman goes viral after challenging Davos panel to talk about taxing the wealthy (ABC News)

evidence.claim: At the World Economic Forum in Davos (2019) Bregman told a panel that almost no one raises the issue of tax avoidance and of the rich not paying their fair share, and said the event should talk about taxes rather than philanthropy.
evidence.quote: almost no one raises the real issue of tax avoidance right and of the rich just not
evidence.source_title: Rutger Bregman tells Davos to talk about tax: 'This is not rocket science' (Guardian News)

evidence.claim: Bregman stated on LinkedIn that Dutch billionaires pay a lower effective tax rate than average Dutch taxpayers (17% vs 45%, 2016 figures he cites), and that billionaires' tax rates have fallen in the US.
evidence.quote: In the Netherlands it's even worse: the average taxpayer in 2016 gave 45 percent of earnings to the government, while billionaires paid just 17 percent.
evidence.source_title: Rutger Bregman LinkedIn post on billionaire effective tax rates

evidence.claim: Bregman publicly argued that Max Verstappen, who lives in Monaco, pays no Dutch income tax, and accused him of costing the Netherlands large sums; the $200m figure is a media characterisation of his claim.
evidence.quote: Rutger Bregman vindt het vreemd dat we juichen voor Max Verstappen terwijl hij geen belasting betaalt in ons land.
evidence.source_title: Quote: Waarom woont Max Verstappen in Monaco?

evidence.claim: Bregman posted that Verstappen, a professional athlete, never paid a single euro in Dutch income tax, and called for Monaco's role as a tax haven for athletes to be addressed; he proposed rules via Dutch economists.
evidence.quote: especially for professional athletes like Max Verstappen (who never paid a single € in income tax)
evidence.source_title: Rutger Bregman on X (June 2023)

evidence.claim: Allegation, unproven (advocacy/journalist critique): Tim Schwab reported that the School for Moral Ambition (SMA), a non-profit co-founded by Bregman, did not disclose Gates Foundation funding when asked for a funders list; SMA's list Schwab received omitted the Gates Foundation and other billionaire philanthropies. Bregman's agent later said the $75,000 Gates grant had been disclosed on the website, and Gates' own site lists a $75,000 grant to the School for Moral Ambition (March 2025). Schwab characterized the non-disclosure as a conflict of interest for Bregman, who had publicly promoted Gates' philanthropy. No finding by any regulator or court.
evidence.quote: SMA sent me a list of funders. I later realized the list they sent was actually not a complete list of funders. Missing from the list were the Gates Foundation and other billionaire philanthropies. That's a big deal because these donors present a stunning financial conflict of interest for Bregman, who had been playing public expert on billionaires and Bill Gates's philanthropic work—-without disclosing these financial ties.
evidence.source_title: Rutger Bregman apologizes for racist essay about Rihanna. Then lashes out (Tim Schwab Substack)

evidence.claim: Documented act, with Bregman's agent's reply: when asked whether he had personal financial interests benefiting from SMA, Bregman's agent did not answer that question and instead stated Bregman had no personal financial ties to Gates. Agent said SMA's donors do not influence its work and that the funder information should be 'more visible'. Status: journalist's account of correspondence; not adjudicated.
evidence.quote: I asked Bregman if he has any personal, financial interests (investments, work contracts, etc.), with any entity, that stands to benefit from the work of the School for Moral Ambition. The response I got—from Strunk—didn't answer this question. Instead, I was told that Bregman has no personal, financial ties to Gates.
evidence.source_title: He built a brand criticizing billionaires. Are billionaires now bankrolling his work? (Tim Schwab Substack)

evidence.claim: Documented act, not a finding of misconduct: Bregman promoted Bill Gates publicly as a progressive voice and said Gates deserved credit for malaria vaccine work in a March 2025 podcast appearance, while the School for Moral Ambition had Gates Foundation funding. Critics (Schwab) argue this was undisclosed in that promotion; Bregman disputes wrongdoing.
evidence.quote: In March 2025, Bregman went on the Trevor Noah Podcast. "I'm actually going to say something nice about billionaires," Bregman said. He talked about the Gates Foundation's work on a vaccine for malaria. "I think someone like Bill Gates deserves an enormous amount of credit for it."
evidence.source_title: Billionaires aren't going to save the planet: Bill Gates and Rutger Bregman (Redd Monitor substack)

evidence.claim: Not a C1-C4 finding but relevant to deception-of-public claims: Schwab reported Bregman's 2011 Volkskrant op-ed used racial slurs about Rihanna; Bregman published an apology in 2025 calling it 'a terrible article... There are no excuses.' Allegation/journalist account; no adjudication. Included only as context for the apology's content.
evidence.quote: In 2011, when I was 23 and still a student, I wrote a deeply ignorant and offensive opinion piece for de Volkskrant about racism in the Netherlands. I'm now 37, and I remain ashamed of it.
evidence.source_title: Rutger Bregman apologizes for racist essay about Rihanna. Then lashes out (Tim Schwab Substack)

people.name: Sam Altman
notes: power backfilled from hand-entered reach and authority, not from a research run
people.summary:
Harm tier: ultimate (score 1.0). Coverage and confidence are both 1.0. The main drivers, in order of weight:

1. Safety governance (R1, severity 4). OpenAI effectively dissolved its superalignment team after its co-leaders resigned [R1-E01, https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2024-05-17/openai-dissolves-key-safety-team-after-chief-scientist-ilya-sutskever-s-exit]. The Financial Times reported that safety testing time was cut from months to days [R1-E04, https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/nnzb7prw2XC8cFhnP/openai-13-altman-at-ted-and-openai-cutting-corners-on-safety]. OpenAI formally opposed California's SB 1047 [R1-E06], and Altman called government approval of AI releases "disastrous" [R1-E09].

2. Equity and NDA terms (R2, severity 1; R3, severity 2). Reporting on documents Altman signed describes clawback authority tied to non-disparagement agreements [R2-E09, https://www.vox.com/future-perfect/351132/openai-vested-equity-nda-sam-altman-documents-employees]. A Kenyan High Court ruled that Worldcoin's data collection breached data protection law [R3-E06, https://new.kenyalaw.org/akn/ke/judgment/kehc/2025/5629/eng@2025-05-05].

3. Candor allegations (R4, severity 0). The board said in 2023 he was "not consistently candid" [R4-E01]. Former colleagues have made deception allegations, including sworn testimony in a pending civil case [R4-E10, https://aitoolly.com/ai-news/article/2026-05-07-mira-murati-testifies-under-oath-regarding-sam-altmans-alleged-misrepresentations-on-ai-safety-standards]. These remain unadjudicated, and Altman denies them.

Benefit tier: minor_guardian (score 0.15). Benefit confidence is low (0.47). Documented items include Altman's 2023 Senate call for licensing of advanced AI [R1-E07, https://www.wsj.com/tech/ai/chatgpts-sam-altman-faces-senate-panel-examining-artificial-intelligence-4bb6942a] and his 2024 departure from OpenAI's internal safety committee, which was made independent [R1-E15, https://time.com/7022026/sam-altman-safety-committee].

These two profiles are reported separately and do not offset each other.

evidence.claim: Superalignment team, formed in 2023 with a pledge of 20% of compute, was effectively dissolved in May 2024 after co-leaders Sutskever and Leike resigned; OpenAI folded the group into broader research efforts.
evidence.quote: OpenAI has effectively dissolved a team focused on ensuring the safety of possible future ultra-capable artificial intelligence systems, following the departure of the group's two leaders
evidence.source_title: OpenAI Dissolves Key Safety Team After Chief Scientist Ilya Sutskever's Exit

evidence.claim: Jan Leike resigned from OpenAI in protest, saying safety culture had taken a backseat to shiny products; Altman was CEO at the time.
evidence.quote: OpenAI's "safety culture and processes have taken a backseat to shiny products."
evidence.source_title: Former OpenAI board member explains why CEO Sam Altman was fired

evidence.claim: Former board member Helen Toner said Altman gave the board inaccurate information about the company's formal safety processes on multiple occasions and withheld information; the board said he was not consistently candid.
evidence.quote: Toner said Altman gave the board "inaccurate information about the small number of formal safety processes that the company did have in place" on multiple occasions.
evidence.source_title: Former OpenAI board member explains why CEO Sam Altman was fired

evidence.claim: Financial Times reported (citing eight people familiar) that OpenAI cut the time and resources for safety testing of its models from months to days amid competitive pressure.
evidence.quote: Staff and third-party groups have recently been given just days to conduct "evaluations," the term given to tests for assessing models' risks and performance, on OpenAI's latest LLMs, compared to several months previously.
evidence.source_title: OpenAI #13 (quoting Financial Times report)

evidence.claim: Altman opposed California SB 1047 frontier AI safety bill through OpenAI's formal opposition letter, despite earlier public calls for regulation; former employees said he opposed even light-touch requirements.
evidence.quote: Sam Altman, our former boss, has repeatedly called for Al regulation. Now, when actual regulation is on the table, he opposes it.

people.name: Sam Bankman-Fried
people.descriptor: American entrepreneur, founder of the FTX cryptocurrency exchange
notes: power backfilled from hand-entered reach and authority, not from a research run
people.summary:
Harm tier: ultimate (final score 1.0). Coverage is complete (1.0), but confidence is moderate (0.81).

The main reasons, in order of weight:

1. Deception and fraud (R4, severity 4). A jury convicted Bankman-Fried on seven counts of fraud, conspiracy and money laundering tied to the FTX/Alameda collapse, and jurors held him responsible for about $10 billion in customer money [R4-E01, https://www.cnbc.com/2024/03/28/live-updates-ftx-founder-sam-bankman-fried-sentencing.html]. The Second Circuit affirmed the conviction and sentence on June 12, 2026 [R4-E02, https://www.politico.com/news/2026/06/12/sam-bankman-frieds-conviction-upheld-by-appeals-court-00960434]. The SEC and CFTC misstatement claims are unadjudicated allegations.

2. Political spending and lobbying (R3, severity 1). Prosecutors allege more than $100 million in political contributions from customer funds, and that FTX lobbying sought legislation that would help it keep taking customer deposits [R3-E09, https://www.cnbc.com/2023/08/14/bankman-fried-used-customer-funds-for-100-million-in-us-political-donations-prosecutors-charge.html].

3. Witness interference (R2, severity 1). A judge found that a leak of a trial witness's private writings was meant to "hurt, discredit or frighten" her [R2-E03, https://nymag.com/intelligencer/2023/07/feds-say-they-want-sbf-in-jail-for-intimidating-witnesses.html].

4. Power and influence (R1, severity 1). Documented activity includes large FTX-linked investments [R1-E04].

Benefit tier: none_documented. No benefit evidence was found that qualified as a costly act reducing risk. The only candidate item (R1-E10) concerns a resignation and is not scored as a benefit. Benefit confidence is low. This absence is not a negative finding and does not offset the harm profile.

evidence.claim: Bankman-Fried directed FTX executives to make political donations in order to evade contribution limits, as part of a push for crypto-friendly regulation; prosecutors said he used stolen customer funds for more than $100 million in political contributions before the 2022 midterms.
evidence.quote: He leveraged this influence, in turn, to lobby Congress and regulatory agencies to support legislation and regulation he believed would make it easier for FTX to continue to accept customer deposits and grow
evidence.source_title: Sam Bankman-Fried charged with using stolen funds for over $100 million in political donations

evidence.claim: FTX lobbied for the Digital Commodities Consumer Protection Act more than any other legislation in 2022; Bankman-Fried supported the bill, which critics said would build a moat around FTX and be detrimental to DeFi.
evidence.quote: Despite the allegations later made against him and his company, Bankman-Fried supported the DCCPA. FTX lobbied for the bill more than any other legislation in 2022, according to watchdog OpenSecrets.
evidence.source_title: Digital Commodities Consumer Protection Act Sam Bankman-Fried FTX fail

evidence.claim: Bankman-Fried admitted in an interview that his political donations were intended to buy influence over regulation, saying people running regulated businesses had to think about which ribbons to pull.
evidence.quote: In an interview shortly before his arrest in the Bahamas, Bankman-Fried admitted that his donations were intended to buy influence of regulations
evidence.source_title: Sam Bankman-Fried - Influence Watch

evidence.quote: Under Bankman-Fried's leadership, FTX invested $500 million in Anthropic, which was founded by ex-OpenAI employees in 2021, before the boom in generative AI.
evidence.source_title: FTX estate sells majority stake in startup Anthropic for $884 million

people.summary:
Stanislav Petrov's result is unrated for both harm and benefit. The required harm rubric, R1, has no usable evidence because research failed (ResearchError), so no tier was assigned. Coverage is 0.75 and confidence is 0.0.

Rubrics R2, R3, and R4 each scored severity 0, but the final tier cannot be set without R1.

The available evidence describes the consequences Petrov faced after the September 1983 incident. He was reprimanded, reportedly for logbook or paperwork errors rather than for his decision [R2-E01, https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-24280831]. He was denied promotions, reassigned to a less sensitive post, and took early retirement. The US National Park Service attributes this to his decision embarrassing superiors [R2-E02, https://www.nps.gov/people/stanislav_petrov.htm]. One source reports that a superior praised his judgment and promised an award that never came [R2-E03, https://www.i24news.tv/en/news/international/artc-feature-the-soviet-officer-who-disobeyed-orders-and-prevented-nuclear-war].

The Arms Control Association reports the documentation reprimand as an allegation, not an adjudicated finding [R4-E02, https://www.armscontrol.org/act/2017-10/news-briefs/man-who-saved-world-dies-77]. No conflict-of-interest move is documented [R4-E04].

No benefit verdict was reached. This is not a negative finding.

evidence.claim: Petrov was reprimanded a few days after the 1983 incident, officially for mistakes in the logbook rather than for his decision, and kept silent about the incident for about 10 years.
evidence.quote: A few days later Mr Petrov received an official reprimand for what happened that night. Not for what he did, but for mistakes in the logbook.
evidence.source_title: Stanislav Petrov: The man who may have saved the world - BBC News

evidence.claim: After the incident Petrov was denied promotions, reassigned and took early retirement; NPS attributes this to his decision having embarrassed superiors.
evidence.quote: He was denied promotions, reassigned and took early retirement.  The story was not even known outside the secretive world of the Soviet military until the late 1990s.
evidence.source_title: Stanislav Petrov (U.S. National Park Service)

evidence.quote: After the incident, Petrov was questioned over his decision not to follow protocol. He later said that Yuri Votintsev, then commander of the Soviet missile-defense forces, praised his judgment and even promised him an award. The award never materialized.

evidence.quote: recalls that he was also reprimanded for improper filing of paperwork because he had not described the incident in the war diary.
evidence.source_title: Stanislav Petrov - Wikipedia

evidence.source_title: Stanislav Petrov, Soviet Officer Who Helped Avert Nuclear War, Is Dead at 77 - NYT

evidence.quote: A few days later Mr Petrov received an official reprimand for what happened that night. Not for what he did, but for mistakes in the logbook.

evidence.claim: Petrov was reportedly reprimanded for allegedly faulty documentation during the key moments of the 1983 incident; Arms Control Association reports this as an allegation, not an adjudicated finding.

notes: power backfilled from hand-entered reach and authority, not from a research run
people.summary:
Tucker Carlson is rated minor on harm (score 0.38, coverage and confidence 1.0). The main driver is climate coverage, rubric R1 at severity 2. Inside Climate News and Media Matters describe his show as a major source of climate misinformation [R1-E01, https://insideclimatenews.org/news/21072023/tucker-carlson-jesse-watters-fox-news-climate-misinformation]. A climate-advocacy analysis found it ran the most climate denial segments [R1-E02, https://www.citizen.org/news/climate-change-denial-dominates-86-of-fox-news-climate-segments], and a peer-reviewed study found it gave no coverage to the IPCC's 2021 report [R1-E03, https://www.nature.com/articles/s43247-023-00760-2].

Rubrics R2, R3 and R4 scored zero. The record still includes evidence on election claims aired on his show. A Delaware court ruled that Dominion-related statements on the show were assertions of fact, not opinion [R2-E01, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominion_Voting_Systems_v._Fox_News_Network]. Fox, not Carlson, was the settling party [R4-E05, https://www.reuters.com/legal/dominions-defamation-case-against-fox-poised-trial-after-delay-2023-04-18]. Workplace allegations from a former producer were never adjudicated [R3-E02, https://www.courthousenews.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/grossberg-foxnews-tuckercarlson-complaint.pdf].

Benefit is rated minor_guardian, based on one item: he publicly urged Americans to oppose a planned $2.8 billion arms sale to Israel [R1-E06, https://www.newsweek.com/tucker-carlson-issues-warning-on-report-of-israel-bomb-sale-no-precedent-12447305]. No costly executed act is documented, and benefit confidence is low (0.23). Benefit is reported separately and does not reduce the harm rating.

evidence.claim: Carlson publicly criticized US military aid to Ukraine on air, arguing the money was being misspent and US weapons stocks for America's military were running low.
evidence.quote: Tucker Carlson trashes sending US aid to 'Zelenskyy and his wife' as weapons for America's military run low
evidence.source_title: Tucker Carlson trashes sending US aid to Zelenskyy and his wife - Fox News

evidence.claim: Carlson publicly urged Americans to oppose a planned $2.8 billion US arms sale to Israel of about 40,000 bombs. This is a public statement opposing an arms transfer; no costly executed act (revenue given up, contract refused) is documented.
evidence.quote: "appears to be the largest transfer of conventional explosive ordnance from the United States in modern history"
evidence.source_title: Tucker Carlson Hits Trump Over Israel Arms Sale, Says No Precedent - Newsweek

evidence.claim: Fox News ended Carlson's show on April 24, 2023, days after Fox agreed to pay $787.5 million to settle the Dominion defamation suit over false election-fraud claims in which Carlson was a central figure. This was a dismissal, not a voluntary resignation, so it is not a benefit act.
evidence.quote: Tucker Carlson ousted at Fox News following network's $787 million settlement
evidence.source_title: Tucker Carlson ousted at Fox News following network's $787 million settlement - Houston Public Media

evidence.claim: Carlson aired on Tucker Carlson Tonight claims about Dominion Voting Systems and the 2020 election that a Delaware court later said were false; the court ruled the statements were assertions of fact, not opinion, and that 'none of the statements relating to Dominion about the 2020 election are true'.
evidence.quote: On March 31, 2023, Delaware Superior Court judge Eric Davis ruled in a summary judgment that it "is crystal clear that none of the statements relating to Dominion about the 2020 election are true"
evidence.source_title: Dominion Voting Systems v. Fox News Network - Wikipedia

evidence.claim: Court ruling on the Carlson-hosted segment (Mike Lindell appearance, Jan. 26, 2021): the court found a statement on Carlson's show asserted facts about Dominion, not opinion, and noted Carlson and producer Pfeiffer had acknowledged allegations were unsupported before hosting Lindell.
evidence.quote: When viewed in the full context of the overall communication expressed during the segment, a reasonable viewer would understand that Statement is asserting facts regarding Dominion, not an opinion.
evidence.source_title: Delaware Superior Court opinion, Dominion v. Fox News (N21C-03-257)

evidence.claim: Carlson wrote privately that the network's job was 'to explain what things mean' rather than to report news, after the Jan. 6 riot, when a colleague was concerned about lies feeding the violence.
evidence.quote: On the evening of Jan. 6, 2021 — after a mob had overrun the U.S. Capitol, fueled by the misguided belief that the 2020 election had been “stolen” — Fox News host Tucker Carlson texted a colleague who was concerned about the lies that fed the violence. “Our job is not to provide news coverage. Not even close. Our job is to explain what things mean,” Carlson wrote.
evidence.source_title: Explaining the Missing Context of Tucker Carlson's Jan. 6 Presentation - FactCheck.org

evidence.claim: Carlson aired a March 2023 segment on previously unreleased Jan. 6 Capitol surveillance footage, provided by Speaker McCarthy, claiming it overturned the account that Officer Sicknick was killed by Trump supporters; FactCheck.org found the claims lacked context. The Sicknick family said they were 'outraged' by the report.
evidence.quote: Carlson said previously unreleased video showed a “healthy and vigorous” Sicknick walking around in the Capitol after his engagement with protesters outside. The footage, Carlson said, “overturns the single most powerful and politically useful lie that Democrats have told us about Jan. 6,”
evidence.source_title: Explaining the Missing Context of Tucker Carlson's Jan. 6 Presentation - FactCheck.org

evidence.claim: Fox News, with Carlson as the top-rated host, settled Dominion's defamation suit for $787.5M shortly before trial; Fox acknowledged the court's rulings finding certain claims about Dominion false. Carlson was not personally a settling party, but his on-air statements were central to the claims.
evidence.quote: We acknowledge the court’s rulings finding certain claims about Dominion to be false.
evidence.source_title: Dominion-Fox News Trial: Fox News Settles Defamation Suit for $787.5 Million - NYT

evidence.claim: Fox News paid $12 million to settle former Carlson producer Abby Grossberg's suit, which alleged a hostile and discriminatory workplace on Carlson's show and that Fox's lawyers pressured her to give false deposition testimony in the Dominion case; she said she was fired after going public with claims. Fox denied her allegations at the time; the settlement ended legal exposure for Carlson.
evidence.quote: Grossberg alleged that Fox's attorneys coerced and impermissibly coached her in preparation for her deposition in Dominion
evidence.source_title: Fox News agrees to pay $12 million to settle lawsuits from ... - CBS News

evidence.claim: Carlson was removed from Tucker Carlson Tonight in April 2023; Fox and Carlson announced they were parting ways. Carlson and Fox denied the ouster was tied to the settlement; Carlson later said in a book he 'knows' the firing was part of a settlement deal.
evidence.quote: Former prime-time host tells biographer he 'knows' firing was part of deal to resolve Dominion Voting Systems defamation case.
evidence.source_title: Tucker Carlson claims in book Fox News firing was part of ... - Guardian

evidence.claim: Carlson's on-air rhetoric promoting the Great Replacement theory (replacement of white populations by immigrants/people of color) has been cited by critics and extremism researchers; the ADL and Media Matters document his repeated use of it. No documented causal link to the Buffalo shooter was established by the sources reviewed; the shooter's manifesto was reported as drawing on the theory.
evidence.quote: This so-called Great Replacement conspiracy theory has been promoted by major far-right media figures including Tucker Carlson of Fox News.
evidence.source_title: Deplatform Tucker Carlson and the "Great Replacement" Theory - ADL

evidence.claim: Fox News paid $12 million to settle a lawsuit by former booker Abby Grossberg, who alleged Carlson's show was a hostile, sexist and antisemitic workplace; the settlement also ended legal peril for Carlson and other named executives.
evidence.quote: Fox News paid $12 million on Friday to settle a former producer's lawsuit claiming that Tucker Carlson's show was an abusive place to work, defined by bigotry, misogyny and bullying.
evidence.source_title: Fox News settles with former Tucker Carlson producer for $12 million

evidence.claim: Grossberg alleged she was isolated, overworked, undervalued and treated worse than male counterparts; the claims were made in her complaint, which was not adjudicated.
evidence.quote: Ms. Grossberg was isolated, overworked, undervalued, denied opportunities for promotion, and generally treated significantly worse than her male counterparts
evidence.source_title: Grossberg v. Fox News complaint (1:23-cv-02368)

evidence.claim: Fox News's Dominion settlement of $787.5 million, reached days before Carlson was expected to testify, followed a judge's ruling that the election claims aired on Fox were false; Carlson was taken off air within days.
evidence.quote: Fox agreed to pay more than $US787 million to settle the lawsuit with Dominion Voting Systems over the network's airing of false claims following the 2020 presidential election.
evidence.source_title: Fox News reaches $18 million settlement with former Tucker Carlson producer - ABC News

evidence.claim: Dominion alleged Carlson's show aired debunked election-fraud claims about the company; the court found the statements about Dominion were false. (Carlson is a named defendant-side participant in the Dominion claims; the court also named Carlson among those responsible for statements on Tucker Carlson Tonight.)
evidence.quote: Dominion alleged in its lawsuit that Carlson allowed debunked election-fraud claims about the voting-technology firm to air on
evidence.source_title: Tucker Carlson leaves Fox News days after Dominion settlement

evidence.claim: Carlson's text messages showed private skepticism of the election claims he aired on air, e.g. calling Sidney Powell's claims a lie and saying 'Our viewers are good people and they believe it'.
evidence.quote: Carlson texted to Laura Ingraham, "Sidney Powell is lying by the way. I caught her. It's insane" and "Our viewers are good people and they believe it."
evidence.source_title: Dominion Voting Systems v. Fox News Network - Wikipedia

evidence.claim: Carlson's show drew a 2018 advertiser boycott by at least 20 advertisers after he said immigration makes the country 'poorer, dirtier and more divided'; Fox said advertisers only moved buys to other programs.
evidence.quote: By the end of 2018, the show had begun to be boycotted by at least 20 advertisers after Carlson said immigration makes the country "poorer, dirtier and more divided".
evidence.source_title: Tucker Carlson - Wikipedia

evidence.claim: Carlson's media company raised a $15 million seed investment from 1789 Capital, a firm that describes itself as investing in 'anti-woke' companies.
evidence.quote: Omeed Malik, through his newly launched 1789 Capital boutique investment firm, has invested $15 million in seed capital into Last Country, the startup founded by Carlson and Neil Patel
evidence.source_title: Tucker Carlson's new media company gets seed funding

evidence.claim: Qatar's embassy paid Lumen8 Advisors $180,000 a month (per FARA records) and Lumen8 arranged Carlson's March 2025 interview with Qatar's Prime Minister; no public record shows Carlson himself was paid, and TCN's CEO denied foreign money was taken.
evidence.quote: No public record cited by the Quincy Institute or the Washington Examiner shows that Carlson was paid. FARA records show the Qatari embassy pays Lumen8 Advisors $180,000 a month for media and communication coaching and consulting, and Lumen8 arranged the March 2025 interview.
evidence.source_title: Qatar Lobbying in the US: $250M Across 88 FARA Firms

evidence.claim: Investigation/allegation (not adjudicated against Carlson personally): In 2016 the Daily Caller received an estimated $150,000 from the Trump presidential campaign for sending at least 25 emails to its subscriber list; the Center for Media and Democracy said Carlson had a conflict of interest and that he did not disclose this funding to Fox News viewers while covering the race. CMD's estimate, not a finding by a court or regulator.
evidence.quote: CMD estimates that Carlson's Daily Caller received at least $150,000 from the Trump campaign in the months right before the November election
evidence.source_title: Exposed: Tucker Carlson, His "Charity," and the Trump Campaign Cash He Didn't Tell FOX Viewers About (CMD)

evidence.claim: Allegation by a watchdog group (CMD) that Carlson had a conflict of interest and violated journalistic standards over the Trump campaign email-list payment to the Daily Caller; no regulator or court finding is cited.
evidence.quote: The watchdog said Carlson had a conflict of interest and had violated journalistic standards.
evidence.source_title: Tucker Carlson - Wikipedia

evidence.claim: Investigation/allegation: Campaign for Accountability filed an IRS complaint (2020) alleging the Daily Caller News Foundation nonprofit improperly subsidized the for-profit Daily Caller; the complaint is an allegation against the organization, not a finding against Carlson personally.
evidence.quote: CfA filed a complaint with the IRS against the Daily Caller News Foundation alleging the nonprofit abused its tax-exempt status.
evidence.source_title: CfA Files IRS Complaint Against Daily Caller News Foundation for Abusing Nonprofit Status

evidence.claim: Court finding (summary judgment, Delaware Superior Court, March 2023) against Fox News, the network on which Carlson hosted: Carlson's January 26, 2021 broadcast statement that asserted 'facts regarding Dominion' was not protected opinion. The court did not find Carlson personally liable; Fox was the defendant. Dominion's claims were settled by Fox for $787.5M without an admission of wrongdoing; Fox 'acknowledge[d] the court's rulings finding certain claims about Dominion to be false.'
evidence.quote: the Court finds that the Statement asserts facts and therefore not protected under the opinion privilege
evidence.source_title: Dominion Voting Systems v. Fox News Network, Delaware Superior Court summary judgment opinion

evidence.claim: Settlement (Fox News, not Carlson personally): Fox agreed to pay Dominion $787.5 million in April 2023 and, per its statement, acknowledged the court's rulings finding certain claims about Dominion to be false; no admission of wrongdoing and no apology. Carlson was not a named party.
evidence.quote: We acknowledge the Court's rulings finding certain claims about Dominion to be false
evidence.source_title: Fox settles Dominion lawsuit for $787.5 million over US election claims (Reuters)

evidence.claim: Documented private texts (produced in litigation discovery, Nov 2020 to Jan 2021) in which Carlson said Sidney Powell 'is lying' about having evidence, while his on-air programming during the same period presented election-fraud claims; Carlson's texts describe viewers as believing claims he privately doubted. Carlson has said the messages reflected a moment when he was 'absolutely infuriated' and did not deny them.
evidence.quote: "Sidney Powell is lying by the way. I caught her. It's insane" and "Our viewers are good people and they believe it."
evidence.source_title: Fox Stars Privately Expressed Disbelief About Trump's Election Fraud Claims (NYT)

evidence.claim: Carlson texted in January 2021 'I hate him passionately' about Donald Trump, a private statement revealed in court filings; this is a private-opinion disclosure rather than a false statement to a regulator or court.
evidence.quote: "I hate him passionately. I blew up at Peter Navarro today in frustration,"
evidence.source_title: Private Fox News text messages, emails released in Dominion suit (NBC News)

evidence.claim: Carlson was removed from Tucker Carlson Tonight by Fox News on April 24, 2023, shortly after the Dominion settlement; Fox said the sides 'agreed to part ways'. Carlson has said he was taken off air as part of the settlement terms (per his 2023 book); Dominion denies it was a firing as part of settlement terms. Not an adjudicated finding of misconduct.
evidence.quote: "FOX News Media and Tucker Carlson have agreed to part ways," the company said in a statement Monday.
evidence.source_title: Tucker Carlson leaves Fox News in wake of Dominion settlement (CNBC)
